definition_zh: 翻耕；犁地：用犁把表土切开并翻转的农事作业，也指犁过的地、留下的犁沟，以及由这一动作引申出的推进与再投入
definition_en: the act or process of cutting and turning over soil with a plough, together with the land, the furrows and the figurative extensions that follow from it
core_image: 犁铧切入湿土，一整条土垡被翻扣到旁边，地面留下一道连续的长沟
scene: 秋雨刚停，农户牵着牲口下地，犁铧切开湿土，整片田被一道一道翻开。Deep plowing brings the lower soil up and buries the weeds.
sceneCN: 这里这个词指翻耕作业（第 1 个义项：切开并翻转表土的农事动作）；句意为深耕把下层土翻上来，同时把杂草埋下去。

pos.zh: 翻耕；犁地（指作业本身，不可数）
犁过的地；犁沟与土垄（动作的结果）
犁；翻耕（美式原形 plow／英式原形 plough 的现在分词与动名词）

collocations.zh: 等高耕作（沿等高线翻地）

collocations.phrase: plowing profits back into the business

derivatives.zh: plow + -man（人）→ 扶犁的人，语义偏移为「农夫」
plow + share（古英语 scear「切分部分」）→ 犁的切土部件，即犁铧
plow + -able（能够……的）→ 能被犁的，语义偏移为「适于耕作的」
snow（雪）+ plow → 除雪机；引申为用犁推的方式除雪
plough + land（土地）→ 一犁所能耕的地，语义偏移为中世纪的土地计量单位

senses.title: Turning the sod
senses.titleCN: 翻耕：把表土切开并翻扣
senses.definition: the farm operation of cutting a slice of topsoil and turning it over with a plough
senses.definitionCN: 用犁把一层表土切开并翻转过来的农事作业
senses.example: Deep plowing brings the lower soil up and buries the weeds.
senses.exampleCN: 深耕把下层土翻上来，同时把杂草埋下去。
senses.why: A plough is a blade that separates one continuous slice of soil and rolls it over, so grass and stubble end up underneath. The word names that single inversion, not any loosening of the ground.
senses.whyCN: 犁是一片切刀，把一整条土垡与底层分开并翻扣过去，草与残茬因此被压到下面。这个词命名的正是这一次翻转，而不是任何松土动作。

senses.title: The ground once turned
senses.titleCN: 犁过的地：翻转之后的状态
senses.definition: land that has already been ploughed and is ready for sowing
senses.definitionCN: 已经犁过、可以直接播种的土地
senses.example: The plowing on the north side was ready for winter wheat.
senses.exampleCN: 北边那块犁过的地已经可以种冬小麦了。
senses.why: The name of an action can shift to its product; what the blade made is a surface of open soil, and farmers speak of that surface by the work that produced it.
senses.whyCN: 动作的名称可以转指它的产物：犁铧造出的是一片敞开的土面，农人便用造成它的那项劳作来称呼这片地。

senses.title: The furrow it leaves
senses.titleCN: 犁沟与土垄：地面上留下的线
senses.definition: the open trench and the ridge of turned soil that together mark a plough's path
senses.definitionCN: 犁开出的沟与翻起的土垄，两者合成犁走过的一条线
senses.example: The plowing ran in long brown ribbons toward the river.
senses.exampleCN: 犁过的痕迹像一条条棕色长带，一直伸向河边。
senses.why: Because the slice is laid beside its own trench, every pass produces a pair of ditch and ridge, and a field is read by counting those pairs.
senses.whyCN: 因为土垡就翻在它自己的沟旁，每走一趟都造出一对「沟与垄」，整块田就是靠数这些对子来读的。

senses.title: Ploughing season
senses.titleCN: 耕作季：一年中翻地的时段
senses.definition: the part of the farming year given over to ploughing, usually autumn or spring
senses.definitionCN: 农事年中专门用于翻地的时段，通常是秋耕或春耕
senses.example: Autumn plowing starts as soon as the harvest ends.
senses.exampleCN: 一收完庄稼，秋耕就开始了。
senses.why: Work that must be done at one point in the year turns into a name for that point; the -ing form marks the season as an activity rather than a date.
senses.whyCN: 必须在一年中某个节点完成的活计，会变成那个节点的名字；动名词形式把这个时段说成一项活动，而不是一个日期。

senses.title: Blade against snow
senses.titleCN: 除雪清障：同样的刀口推过另一种地面
senses.definition: the clearing of snow, rubble or other loose material from a surface with a blade
senses.definitionCN: 用铲刀把雪、碎石等松散物从地面推开的作业
senses.example: Snow plowing begins before the morning commute.
senses.exampleCN: 除雪作业在早高峰之前就开始了。
senses.why: The blade does not care what it cuts; once the same push and roll is applied to snow, the farm word extends to road clearing without changing its shape.
senses.whyCN: 刀口并不在意切的是什么；当同样的推与翻被用到雪上，这个农事词就无需改变形态地延伸到道路清障。

senses.title: Hull through water
senses.titleCN: 破浪前进：船头把水面切开
senses.definition: the movement of a boat that cuts through water and throws it aside
senses.definitionCN: 船头切开水面、把水推向两侧的前进
senses.example: The ferry was plowing across the gray water.
senses.exampleCN: 渡轮正破开灰暗的水面往前开。
senses.why: A bow behaves like a blade: it splits the medium and rolls it to the sides, leaving a wake that is the water's own version of a furrow.
senses.whyCN: 船头像一片刀：它把介质劈开、翻向两侧，留下的尾迹就是水面上的一道犁沟。

senses.title: Working through resistance
senses.titleCN: 艰难推进：像犁地一样一点点往前
senses.definition: progressing slowly and laboriously through a mass of work, text or people
senses.definitionCN: 在大量工作、文字或人群中缓慢而费力地向前推进
senses.example: She spent the weekend plowing through the reports.
senses.exampleCN: 她整个周末都在啃那些报告。
senses.why: When a task offers the resistance of heavy soil, the image of a blade dragged forward fits exactly: progress is measured in rows finished, not in speed.
senses.whyCN: 当任务像重土一样给出阻力，被拖着往前走的刀锋这一意象就正好合用：进度以走完多少行来衡量，而不是以快慢来衡量。

senses.title: Ploughing profits back
senses.titleCN: 把利润再翻回土里
senses.definition: reinvesting earnings in the same enterprise instead of distributing them
senses.definitionCN: 把赚到的钱重新投入本企业，而不是分掉
senses.example: The company kept plowing its profits back into research.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司一直把利润再投回研究。
senses.why: Money is treated as seed and the business as soil: what is turned back into the ground is expected to grow again, which is why the phrase means reinvestment rather than spending.
senses.whyCN: 钱被当作种子，企业被当作土地：翻回土里的东西被期待再长出来，所以这个说法指的是再投入，而不是花掉。

intro.en: Plowing names an Old English implement and its work. The word is Germanic in form, but where the Germanic noun itself came from is not settled, so dates are approximate and every deeper root is a reconstruction.
intro.cn: plowing 的名字来自古英语的犁具与这项劳作。词的形态是日耳曼语的，但这个日耳曼名词本身从何而来并无定论，因此年代只是大致，更早的词根都属于重构。

items.en: Old English had ploh and plog for the implement, and the derived plohland for the strip a plough team could work; the verb plogian meant to turn soil. The modern -ing form is the ordinary verbal noun of that verb.
items.cn: 古英语用 ploh、plog 指犁具，并派生 plohland 指一犁队所能耕作的地条；动词 plogian 意为翻土。现代的分词形式就是该动词的常规动名词。

items.en: The noun is reconstructed as a Germanic form represented by Dutch ploeg, German Pflug and Old Norse plogr. The reconstruction is secure as a shape, but it explains only the Germanic family, not the word's first origin.
items.cn: 这个名词被重构为原始日耳曼语形式，同族有荷兰语 ploeg、德语 Pflug 与古诺斯语 plogr。作为形式，这一重构是可靠的，但它只解释日耳曼语族内部，不解释词的最初来源。

items.en: Source uncertain: many reference works suggest the Germanic noun was borrowed early from a Celtic word, but no Celtic form is agreed on, and attempts to attach it to an Indo-European root for cutting or flowing remain reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定：许多词源资料猜测这个日耳曼名词早期借自凯尔特语，但没有公认的凯尔特语形式，把它挂到某个表示「切」或「流」的印欧词根上的做法也只是重构。

items.en: Middle English kept plouh and plow, and the spelling plough spread in southern writing; both the noun and the verb remained ordinary farm words, and the measure ploughland survived in legal records.
items.cn: 中古英语沿用 plouh、plow，plough 这一拼法在南方文献中流行；名词与动词都仍是普通农事词，土地计量 ploughland 则在法律文书中保留下来。

items.en: Modern English splits the spelling: plow in American usage, plough in British. The verbal noun extends to snow clearing, to a ship's bow wave, to slow progress through work, and to money returned to a business.
items.cn: 现代英语在拼写上分流：美式用 plow，英式用 plough。动名词的用法延伸到除雪、船头破浪、艰难推进工作，以及把钱再投入企业。

note.en: Group one collects forms that look or sound close; group two collects words for the wider job of preparing ground.
note.cn: 第一组是形近或音近的形式；第二组是泛指整地这件事的词。

entries.definition: The British spelling of the same word. It is not a different term, only the other spelling of the base form behind plowing.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个词的英式拼法。它不是另一个词，只是 plowing 背后那个原形的另一种写法。

entries.definition: The trade of pipes and water systems, from Latin plumbum 'lead'. The first syllable is /plʌm/, not /plaʊ/.
entries.definitionCN: 管件与供水系统的行业，出自拉丁 plumbum「铅」。首音节是 /plʌm/，不是 /plaʊ/。

entries.definition: Walking or working slowly and steadily, from plod. It shares the shape of the ending but not the farming sense.
entries.definitionCN: 缓慢而踏实地走或干，来自 plod。它与本词共享词尾形态，但没有农事含义。

entries.definition: Moving in a stream, from flow. It rhymes with the headword but describes liquid motion, not cutting soil.
entries.definitionCN: 像水流一样移动，来自 flow。它与本词押韵，但描述液体运动，而不是切土。

entries.definition: Preparing land for crops by any means; ploughing is one kind of tilling, not its synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 用任何方式整地备种；翻耕只是整地的一种，并非同义词。

entries.definition: Breaking clods and smoothing the surface after ploughing; it follows the blade instead of turning the slice.
entries.definitionCN: 翻耕之后打碎土块、平整地面；它跟在犁后面，而不是翻转土垡。

entries.definition: Cutting a single narrow trench, as for seed or water; ploughing turns the whole surface.
entries.definitionCN: 只开一道窄沟，用于播种或引水；翻耕则是翻整整个地表。

entries.definition: The whole care of a crop, from ground preparation to harvest; ploughing is its first mechanical step.
entries.definitionCN: 从整地到收获的整套作物管理；翻耕是其中第一步机械作业。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real compounds and real farm phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的复合词与真实的农事搭配，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The noun and the verb are one family: the implement and its work share the same Germanic shape.
normal.cn: 名词与动词同属一族：器具与它的活计共享同一个日耳曼语形态。

normal.en: The -ing ending turns the verb into the name of the activity, and also into the name of the season when that activity is done.
normal.cn: 动名词词尾把动词变成活动的名称，也顺带成为开展这项活动的季节之名。

normal.en: In plowshare the second element is not a share of stock but an old word for the cutting part, so the compound means the plough's blade.
normal.cn: plowshare 的第二个成分不是股票份额，而是指切分部分的老词，因此整个复合词指犁的刀口。

normal.en: Snowplow keeps the same image: a blade pushes a loose mass aside, only the ground underneath changes.
normal.cn: snowplow 保留同一个意象：刀口把松散的一堆推到旁边，只是底下的地面换了。

normal.en: The fixed phrases mark the calendar and the economics: autumn plowing, contour plowing, profits ploughed back.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出了时令与经济两层：秋耕、等高耕作、利润再投入。

abstract.en: Picture a single continuous ribbon of earth being lifted, flipped and laid down like a page turned in a book.
abstract.cn: 想象一整条连续的土带被抬起、翻转、再放下，像书页被翻过去一样。

abstract.en: Picture a field read as a stack of paired lines, each ditch answering a ridge.
abstract.cn: 想象一块田被读成一叠成对的线，每一道沟都对应一道垄。

abstract.en: Picture the same blade moving through snow, water, paper and money: always one medium split and pushed aside.
abstract.cn: 想象同一片刀口穿过雪、水、纸堆和钱：永远是把一种介质劈开并推到一旁。

examples.en: Contour plowing keeps the soil from washing down the slope.
examples.cn: 等高耕作能防止土壤顺着坡面被冲走。

examples.en: The old ploughland measure recorded how much a team could turn in a season.
examples.cn: 古老的犁地量记录了一队牲口一季能翻多少地。

examples.en: He kept plowing through the night's paperwork until dawn.
examples.cn: 他一直在啃那堆夜里要处理的文书，直到天亮。

dict_mnemonic.text: plow（犁）+ ing（动名词）＝ 犁地的过程；记「刀口切土、整条翻扣、地面留沟」。

root: 古英语 plōh／plōg「犁；一犁地」，同族有荷兰语 ploeg、德语 Pflug、古诺斯语 plógr；更早来源不确定，常被猜测为早期凯尔特语借词，但无公认形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one blade: it cuts a slice, inverts it, leaves a pair of lines, and can be pushed through snow, water, work or money.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一片刀口展开：切下土垡、翻转、留下成对的线，再被推过雪、水、工作和钱。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a blade enters the ground, lifts one continuous slice, and lays it upside down beside its own trench.
core.cn: 核心意象：刀口入土，抬起一整条土垡，把它翻扣在自己沟旁。

branches.en: THE OPERATION: the blade cuts and rolls the topsoil, and the word names that inversion itself.
branches.cn: 作业本身：刀口切开并翻扣表土，词命名的正是这次翻转。

branches.en: WHAT IS LEFT ON THE GROUND: the turned field as a surface, and the paired ditch and ridge as its lines.
branches.cn: 留在地面的结果：翻好的地作为一种土面，成对的沟与垄作为它的线。

branches.en: THE CALENDAR: because the work belongs to one part of the year, its name becomes the season.
branches.cn: 日历：因为这项活计属于一年中的某一段，它的名字就成了那个季节。

branches.en: ANOTHER MEDIUM: the same blade clears snow, so the farm action becomes road work.
branches.cn: 另一种介质：同一片刀口去推雪，农事动作便成了道路作业。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: water, paperwork and capital are all ground that a bow, a reader or a company turns over.
branches.cn: 比喻层：水面、文书与资本都是被船头、读者或企业翻过的「地」。

intro.en: Plow is a Germanic noun and verb that builds compounds freely; its suffixes are ordinary English ones.
intro.cn: plow 是日耳曼语的名词兼动词，能自由构成复合词，所接的后缀都是普通英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: English borrowed no Latin cognate of plow. Latin expressed the same work with a different family, aratio from arare 'to plough', which is close in meaning but not related in origin.
latinIntro.cn: 英语没有从拉丁语借来与 plow 同族的词。拉丁语用另一词族表达同一件事：aratio 出自 arare「犁」，意义相近，但来源无关。

items.structure: plow (base noun and verb, American spelling)

items.example: They plow the lower field in November.
items.exampleCN: 他们在十一月翻下面那块地。

items.meaning: the same word in British usage
items.example: The plough stood at the edge of the yard.
items.exampleCN: 犁靠在院子边上。

items.meaning: the activity or its ongoing form

definition_zh: 冶金；冶金学：从矿石中提取金属、精炼金属并使其可用的技术与学问
definition_en: the science and technology of extracting metals from their ores, refining them, and preparing them for use
core_image: 矿石在高温炉里被还原，金属沉到炉底流出，废渣从另一侧排走
scene: 炉火整夜不熄，工人把粉碎的矿石与焦炭一层层装进炉口，等着金属从底部流出。The metallurgy of this region grew around iron ores that needed very high temperatures.
sceneCN: 这里这个词指一个地区成体系的金属技术（第 6 个义项：某时代或某文化的冶金水平）；句意为这一地区的冶金业围绕需要极高温度的铁矿发展起来。

pos.zh: 冶金学；冶金术（不可数，指学问或技术总体）
冶金作业；冶炼工艺（指具体的生产实践与流程）

collocations.zh: 提取冶金（从矿石中取得金属）
物理冶金（研究金属组织与性能）

forms.label: 复数（少见，指多种冶金体系）

derivatives.zh: metallurgy + -ical（学科形容词后缀）→ 冶金的，语义偏移为「属于冶金工艺的」
metallurgy + -ist（从事者）→ 冶金学家、冶金工程师
metallurgy + -ic（形容词后缀）→ 冶金的（较 metallurgical 少用）
pyro-（希腊 pyr「火」）+ metallurgy → 火法冶金，语义偏移为「靠高温处理矿石」
hydro-（希腊 hydor「水」）+ metallurgy → 湿法冶金，语义偏移为「用溶液浸出金属」
electro-（电）+ metallurgy → 电冶金，语义偏移为「用电解或电弧提炼金属」

senses.title: The discipline
senses.titleCN: 冶金学：从矿石到金属的学问
senses.definition: the science that studies how metals are extracted from ores and prepared for use
senses.definitionCN: 研究如何从矿石中提取金属并使其可用的学问
senses.example: Metallurgy grew out of assaying and smelting practice.
senses.exampleCN: 冶金学是从试金与熔炼的实践里长出来的。
senses.why: The Greek compound joins metallon 'metal, mine' to ergon 'work', so the name literally says the work of metals; a body of such work becomes a science when its rules are written down.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊复合词把 metallon「金属、矿」与 ergon「劳作」接在一起，字面就是「金属的活计」；当这些活计被写成规则，它便成为一门学问。

senses.title: Work at the furnace
senses.titleCN: 冶金作业：工厂里实际进行的提取与精炼
senses.definition: the actual operations carried on in a works to win metal from ore
senses.definitionCN: 在厂里实际进行、把金属从矿石中提炼出来的作业
senses.example: The metallurgy at this plant relies on electric furnaces.
senses.exampleCN: 这家厂的冶金作业依靠电炉。
senses.why: The same word covers the knowledge and the doing; a works is where abstract rules are forced to meet real ore, heat and slag.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词既指知识也指实干；工厂正是抽象规则被迫与真实矿石、高温和炉渣碰面的地方。

senses.title: Ore to metal
senses.titleCN: 工序链：焙烧、熔炼、精炼
senses.definition: the sequence of steps that turns raw ore into refined metal
senses.definitionCN: 把原矿变成精炼金属的一连串步骤
senses.example: Their metallurgy begins with roasting and ends with electrolysis.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的冶金流程从焙烧开始，到电解结束。
senses.why: Each step removes one kind of unwanted material: fire removes sulphur, a flux removes the rocky gangue, and current removes the last traces of impurity.
senses.whyCN: 每一步除去一类不需要的东西：火去掉硫，熔剂去掉脉石，电流去掉最后一点杂质。

senses.title: Inside the metal
senses.titleCN: 物理冶金：研究金属内部组织与性能
senses.definition: the branch that studies the internal structure of metals and how that structure controls their properties
senses.definitionCN: 研究金属内部组织以及这种组织如何决定性能的分支
senses.example: Physical metallurgy explains why quenching makes steel hard.
senses.exampleCN: 物理冶金解释了为什么淬火会使钢变硬。
senses.why: A metal is not a uniform block: its grains, phases and defects decide whether it bends or breaks, so this branch looks inward rather than at the furnace.
senses.whyCN: 金属不是一块均匀的东西：它的晶粒、相与缺陷决定它是弯还是断，因此这一分支看的是内部，而不是炉子。

senses.title: Recipes and heat
senses.titleCN: 配方与热处理：合金成分的配制
senses.definition: the design of alloy compositions and of the heat treatments applied to them
senses.definitionCN: 设计合金成分，并对其施加热处理
senses.example: Modern metallurgy tunes trace elements to control corrosion.
senses.exampleCN: 现代冶金通过调整微量元素来控制腐蚀。
senses.why: Once the metal is out of the ore, the same craft continues by adding and removing elements deliberately, treating the melt as a recipe rather than as a finished product.
senses.whyCN: 金属从矿石里出来之后，这门手艺继续下去：有意识地加入或去掉元素，把熔体当作一份配方，而不是成品。

senses.title: A period's metal craft
senses.titleCN: 某一时代或文化的冶金水平
senses.definition: the metal technology characteristic of a place or period, as studied by archaeologists
senses.definitionCN: 某一地点或时期特有的金属技术，常由考古学者研究
senses.example: The metallurgy of this region grew around iron ores that needed very high temperatures.
senses.exampleCN: 这一地区的冶金业围绕需要极高温度的铁矿发展起来。
senses.why: Slag, crucibles and furnaces survive after the objects do, so a culture's metal craft can be rebuilt from its waste and read as a level of technique.
senses.whyCN: 炉渣、坩埚与炉子在器物消失之后仍然留存，因此一个文化的金属工艺可以从它的废弃物中重建，并被读作技术水平。

senses.title: Refining anything
senses.titleCN: 比喻：像炼金一样提炼纯化
senses.definition: the figurative process of purifying or strengthening something by removing what is coarse
senses.definitionCN: 比喻义：通过去掉粗劣部分来纯化或强化某物
senses.example: The metallurgy of language strips away every word that adds nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 语言的「冶金」会把每个不添分量的词都剥掉。
senses.why: Smelting separates metal from slag, and any process that keeps the valuable part and discards the rest borrows that image.
senses.whyCN: 熔炼把金属与炉渣分开；任何保留有价值部分、丢掉其余部分的过程，都可以借这个意象。

senses.title: The trade and its teaching
senses.titleCN: 行业、专业与课程
senses.definition: the occupation of metallurgists, and the subject as it is taught and organised
senses.definitionCN: 冶金从业者的职业，以及作为课程与建制存在的这门学科
senses.example: She took metallurgy as her major and later joined a smelter.
senses.exampleCN: 她主修冶金，后来进了一家冶炼厂。
senses.why: A discipline becomes a trade when people earn their living by it, and a curriculum when it must be handed on; the word names all three layers at once.
senses.whyCN: 一门学问在有人靠它吃饭时成为行业，在必须传下去时成为课程；这个词同时命名这三个层次。

intro.en: Metallurgy is a Greek compound taken into Latin and then into English. The second element is clear, but the first element, the Greek word for metal, has no agreed origin.
intro.cn: metallurgy 是希腊语复合词，经拉丁语进入英语。第二个成分清楚，但第一个成分即希腊语的「金属」一词，来源并无定论。

items.en: Metallon meant 'metal' and also 'mine, quarry'. Its own origin is uncertain: ancient writers connected it with metalleuein 'to search after, to mine', but that is a later explanation, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: metallon 既指「金属」，也指「矿、采石场」。它自身的来源不确定：古代作者把它与 metalleuein「搜寻、采矿」联系起来，但那是较晚的解释，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Ergon 'work, deed' is the second element and is well attested across Greek. Its Indo-European ancestry is usually reconstructed, so the deeper form is not a recorded word.
items.cn: ergon「劳作、事迹」是第二个成分，在希腊语中用例丰富。它更早的印欧来源通常只能重构，因此更深的形式并非有记录的词。

items.en: The compound metallourgia named the working of metals. The suffix -ia turned the abstract activity into a noun, which is the shape English later borrowed.
items.cn: 复合词 metallourgia 指金属的加工。后缀 -ia 把这个抽象活动变成名词，英语后来借的正是这个形态。

items.en: Medieval and Renaissance Latin used metallurgia for the art of metals, alongside metallum 'metal, mine' and metallicus 'of metal'. Technical Latin carried the Greek noun into the learned languages of Europe.
items.cn: 中世纪与文艺复兴拉丁语用 metallurgia 指金属之艺，同时并用 metallum「金属、矿」与 metallicus「金属的」。技术拉丁语把这个希腊名词带进欧洲的学术语言。

items.en: English metallurgy appears in the seventeenth century, first for the practical art of winning and refining metals; in the twentieth century it split into extractive, physical and process branches with their own laboratories.
items.cn: 英语 metallurgy 于十七世纪出现，最初指提取与精炼金属的实际技艺；到二十世纪，它分成提取、物理与工艺等分支，各自拥有实验室。

items.en: Source uncertain: the meaning of metallon is clear but its etymology is not, the oldest written dates are approximate, and every proposed Indo-European root behind metallon or ergon is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定：metallon 的意义清楚而词源不清，最早书证年代只是大致，凡为 metallon 或 ergon 拟出的印欧词根都是重构。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like metallurgy but name other things; group two holds the neighbouring trades and processes.
note.cn: 第一组是看起来像冶金、实际另指他物的词；第二组是相邻的行当与工序。

entries.definition: The adjective describing what belongs to metallurgy; the field itself is the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 描述属于冶金的形容词；这门学问本身是名词。

entries.definition: The study of metal surfaces and internal structure under the microscope, a tool of physical metallurgy rather than the whole field.
entries.definitionCN: 在显微镜下研究金属表面与内部组织的学问，是物理冶金的工具，而非整个学科。

entries.definition: An element with properties between metals and non-metals, such as silicon; the ending -oid means 'like', not 'study'.
entries.definitionCN: 性质介于金属与非金属之间的元素，如硅；词尾 -oid 意为「像」，而不是「学问」。

entries.definition: A person who practises metallurgy; the -ist ending marks the practitioner, not the discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 从事冶金的人；-ist 词尾标记从业者，而不是学科。

entries.definition: Cutting, forming and joining metal once it is already refined; metallurgy gets the metal out of the ore first.
entries.definitionCN: 金属已经精炼之后再切割、成形与连接；冶金则先要把金属从矿石里取出来。

entries.definition: Purifying crude metal, one step inside metallurgy rather than its whole scope.
entries.definitionCN: 提纯粗金属，只是冶金内部的一步，而不是全部范围。

entries.definition: Testing an ore or alloy to find how much of a metal it holds; the measuring habit that metallurgy grew out of.
entries.definitionCN: 检验矿石或合金中某种金属的含量；冶金正是从这种测量习惯中长出来的。

entries.definition: Crushing and separating ore from waste rock before any metal is won; it prepares the feed for metallurgy.
entries.definitionCN: 在提炼金属之前把矿石破碎并与废石分开；它为冶金准备入炉原料。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two Greek morphemes, real relatives and real process words.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个希腊语语素、真实的同族词与真实的工序词。

normal.en: metallon 'metal' + ergon 'work': the work of metals, which is exactly what the discipline does.
normal.cn: metallon「金属」+ ergon「劳作」：金属的活计，正是这门学问做的事。

normal.en: The -urgy ending also appears in dramaturgy, the working of a drama; the same 'work' element is inside.
normal.cn: -urgy 这个词尾也出现在 dramaturgy（戏剧的编排）里，同一个「劳作」成分就在其中。

normal.en: The three prefixes mark three routes to metal: pyro- for fire, hydro- for solution, electro- for current.
normal.cn: 三个前缀标出三条取金属的路：pyro- 用火，hydro- 用溶液，electro- 用电流。

normal.en: Fixed phrases pair it with its neighbours: extractive metallurgy, physical metallurgy, powder metallurgy.
normal.cn: 固定搭配把它与邻近分支配在一起：提取冶金、物理冶金、粉末冶金。

normal.en: The work order is ore, then dressing, then smelting, then refining, then alloy design.
normal.cn: 作业顺序是：矿石、选矿、熔炼、精炼，最后才是合金设计。

abstract.en: Picture a furnace as a translator that turns silent stone into a speaking metal.
abstract.cn: 想象炉子是一位译者，把沉默的石头译成会说话的金属。

abstract.en: Picture slag as the discarded draft of a sentence: everything the metal was not.
abstract.cn: 想象炉渣是一句话被划掉的草稿：金属所不是的一切。

abstract.en: Picture a single craft splitting into three rooms — fire, water, current — each claiming one route to the same metal.
abstract.cn: 想象同一门手艺分成三个房间——火、水、电——每个房间都声称掌握通往同一块金属的一条路。

examples.en: Extractive metallurgy and physical metallurgy ask different questions about the same metal.
examples.cn: 提取冶金与物理冶金对同一块金属提出不同的问题。

examples.en: The department teaches metallurgy alongside ceramics and polymers.
examples.cn: 这个系把冶金与陶瓷、高分子一起教授。

examples.en: Early metallurgy left behind slag heaps that can still be dated.
examples.cn: 早期冶金留下了至今仍可测年的炉渣堆。

dict_mnemonic.text: metallo（金属）+ urgy（劳作）＝ 金属的活计；记「矿石进炉、金属出炉、炉渣排走」。

root: 希腊 metallon「金属、矿」+ ergon「劳作」→ metallourgia「金属加工」，经拉丁 metallurgia 进入英语；metallon 的来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the metal itself: a discipline, a works, a chain of steps, the inside of the metal, its recipe, a culture's craft, a metaphor, and a trade.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着金属走：先是学问，再是车间，再是工序链，然后是金属内部、它的配方、一个文化的手艺、一个比喻，最后是一门行业。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rock goes into heat, metal comes out liquid, and waste slag is left behind.
core.cn: 核心意象：石头进入高温，金属以液态流出，废弃的炉渣留在后面。

branches.en: THE KNOWLEDGE: the whole body of rules for winning metal from ore.
branches.cn: 知识层：把金属从矿石中取出的一整套规则。

branches.en: THE DOING: a works in operation, and the ordered steps from roasting to electrolysis.
branches.cn: 实干层：运转中的车间，以及从焙烧到电解的有序步骤。

branches.en: THE INSIDE: once the metal exists, its grains and phases decide how it behaves.
branches.cn: 内部层：金属一旦存在，晶粒与相就决定它如何表现。

branches.en: THE RECIPE AND THE RECORD: alloy design in the plant, and the craft of a whole culture read from its slag.
branches.cn: 配方与记录：厂内的合金设计，以及从炉渣读出的整个文化的手艺。

branches.en: THE EXTENSIONS: smelting as a metaphor for purification, and the trade that teaching hands on.
branches.cn: 延伸层：熔炼成为纯化的比喻，以及由教学传承的行业。

intro.en: Metallurgy is built from two Greek bound elements, and both still combine with new material in modern technical English.
intro.cn: metallurgy 由两个希腊语构词成分搭成，两者在现代技术英语里仍能与新成分组合。

latinIntro.en: Latin took the Greek compound whole as metallurgia and also kept metallum for the metal or mine; the Latin adjectives metallicus and metallurgicus passed into learned English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语把希腊复合词整体借作 metallurgia，同时保留 metallum 指金属或矿；拉丁形容词 metallicus 与 metallurgicus 也进入学术英语。

items.meaning: metal; metalliferous
items.example: The metallo- element also opens metalloprotein and metallocene.
items.exampleCN: metallo- 这一成分也出现在 metalloprotein 与 metallocene 中。

items.meaning: the working or making of something
items.example: The same suffix appears in dramaturgy.
items.exampleCN: 同一后缀也出现在 dramaturgy 中。

items.meaning: the working of metals
items.example: Metallurgy is taught as a separate department here.
items.exampleCN: 这里把冶金作为一个独立的系来教。

items.meaning: belonging to the craft of metals
items.example: The metallurgical laboratory tests each heat.
items.exampleCN: 冶金实验室检验每一炉。

items.meaning: one who practises the craft
items.example: A metallurgist read the slag to date the furnace.
items.exampleCN: 一位冶金学家通过炉渣为炉子断代。

items.meaning: bearing metal, said of rock or veins
items.meaningCN: 含金属的（用于岩石或矿脉）
items.example: The metalliferous layer lies under the clay.
items.exampleCN: 含金属的地层位于黏土之下。

items.meaning: winning metal by heat alone
items.example: Pyrometallurgy dominates copper production.
items.exampleCN: 火法冶金在铜生产中占主导。

items.meaning: winning metal with solutions
items.example: Hydrometallurgy recovers gold from low-grade ore.
items.exampleCN: 湿法冶金从低品位矿石中回收金。

items.meaning: winning or refining metal with current
items.meaningCN: 用电流提取或精炼金属
items.example: Electrometallurgy produces aluminium from alumina.
items.exampleCN: 电冶金从氧化铝中产出铝。

senses.title: Of the discipline
senses.titleCN: 学科属性：属于冶金学的
senses.definition: belonging to metallurgy as a field of study
senses.definitionCN: 属于作为一门学问的冶金学
senses.example: Metallurgical research at the institute focuses on phase diagrams.
senses.exampleCN: 该研究所的冶金研究以相图为主。
senses.why: The -ical ending makes a relational adjective: it does not mean 'metal' but 'of the field that studies metal', so it points at the discipline rather than at the material.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词后缀构成关系形容词：它不是「金属的」，而是「研究金属那门学问的」，指向学科而非材料。

senses.title: Of winning metal
senses.titleCN: 提取与精炼：属于把金属从矿石中取出的环节
senses.definition: relating to the extraction and refining of metal from ore
senses.definitionCN: 与从矿石中提取、精炼金属有关的
senses.example: The metallurgical process begins with roasting the concentrate.
senses.exampleCN: 这一冶金过程从焙烧精矿开始。
senses.why: In a works the adjective marks the front half of the chain, where rock is still being turned into metal; the shaping of the finished metal comes later and belongs to other trades.
senses.whyCN: 在厂里，这个形容词标出链条的前半段——石头还在变成金属；成品金属的成形属于后面的行当。

senses.title: Of the metal's inside
senses.titleCN: 组织与性能：属于物理冶金的
senses.definition: relating to the internal structure of a metal and the properties that structure produces
senses.definitionCN: 与金属内部组织以及由该组织决定的性能有关的
senses.example: A metallurgical microscope revealed unusually large grains.
senses.exampleCN: 金相显微镜显示晶粒异常粗大。
senses.why: Once a metal exists, the question shifts from where it came from to how its grains are arranged; the same adjective now points inward at structure.
senses.whyCN: 金属一旦存在，问题就从「它从哪里来」转向「它的晶粒怎样排列」；同一个形容词此时向内指向组织。

senses.title: Of a grade
senses.titleCN: 等级属性：冶金级的原料或产品
senses.definition: used of raw materials or products graded for use in metal production
senses.definitionCN: 用于标明供金属生产使用的原料或产品等级
senses.example: Metallurgical coal must be low in ash and sulphur.
senses.exampleCN: 炼焦煤必须低灰低硫。
senses.why: Some materials exist only to feed a furnace, so a whole grade of coal or coke is named by the industry it serves rather than by what it is.
senses.whyCN: 有些材料存在的唯一目的就是进炉，于是整整一个煤或焦的等级，是按它服务的行业来命名的，而不是按它本身是什么。

senses.title: Of a cause of failure
senses.titleCN: 失效归因：由冶金原因造成的
senses.definition: describing a failure whose cause lies in the metal's composition, structure or treatment
senses.definitionCN: 描述原因出在金属成分、组织或处理上的失效
senses.example: The crack was a metallurgical failure, not a design fault.
senses.exampleCN: 这条裂纹属于冶金失效，而不是设计缺陷。
senses.why: When a part breaks, engineers sort causes by stage; if the fault was already in the metal before it was shaped, the failure is labelled with this adjective.
senses.whyCN: 零件断裂时，工程师按阶段给原因归类；如果毛病在成形之前就已藏在金属里，这类失效就用这个形容词来标记。

senses.title: Of the industry
senses.titleCN: 产业属性：冶金工业与工厂
senses.definition: belonging to the industry, its plants and its equipment
senses.definitionCN: 属于冶金工业、其工厂与设备的
senses.example: The metallurgical industry employs thousands in this valley.
senses.exampleCN: 冶金工业在这个山谷里雇用了数千人。
senses.why: An adjective can name a whole sector by its core activity, and then attach itself to plants, towns and jobs that live off that activity.
senses.whyCN: 一个形容词可以用核心活动来命名整个部门，再附着到靠这项活动生存的工厂、城镇与岗位上。

senses.title: Of people and teaching
senses.titleCN: 人员、教学与文献：属于冶金专业的
senses.definition: used of metallurgical engineers, courses, journals and textbooks
senses.definitionCN: 用于冶金工程师、课程、期刊与教科书
senses.example: She wrote the standard metallurgical textbook on copper smelting.
senses.exampleCN: 她写了那本关于炼铜的标准冶金教科书。
senses.why: A field trains its own people and writes its own books; the adjective travels with them, marking what belongs to the profession rather than to the metal.
senses.whyCN: 一门学问会培养自己的人、写自己的书；这个形容词随他们一起走，标出属于这一行而非属于金属本身的东西。

senses.title: Of testing old metal
senses.titleCN: 检验属性：用于对金属器物的科学分析
senses.definition: used of the scientific examination of metal objects, especially in archaeology and conservation
senses.definitionCN: 用于对金属器物进行的科学检验，尤在考古与文物保护中
senses.example: Metallurgical analysis showed the pin was almost pure copper.
senses.exampleCN: 冶金分析显示这枚别针几乎是纯铜。
senses.why: A museum object cannot be re-smelted, so the only way to know its metal is to measure it; the adjective marks the laboratory half of that work.
senses.whyCN: 博物馆的器物不能再熔一次，唯一知道它是什么金属的办法就是测量；这个形容词标出这项工作里属于实验室的那一半。

intro.en: Metallurgical is the adjective of metallurgy, built from a Greek compound plus a Latin adjectival ending. The Greek first element remains the uncertain part.
intro.cn: metallurgical 是 metallurgy 的形容词，由希腊复合词加拉丁形容词词尾构成。希腊语的第一个成分仍是存疑之处。

items.en: Metallon 'metal, mine' and ergon 'work' formed metallourgia, the working of metals. Metallon's own origin is uncertain, and the ancient link to metalleuein 'to mine' is an explanation rather than a proven derivation.
items.cn: metallon「金属、矿」与 ergon「劳作」构成 metallourgia，即金属的加工。metallon 自身的来源不确定，古人把它与 metalleuein「采矿」相联系，那是一种解释而非已证实的派生。

items.en: Latin formed the adjective metallurgicus on the model of metallurgia, alongside metallicus 'of metal'. The two adjectives were kept apart: one belonged to the craft, the other to the material.
items.cn: 拉丁语依照 metallurgia 造出形容词 metallurgicus，同时另有 metallicus「金属的」。两个形容词彼此分工：一个属于工艺，一个属于材料。

items.en: English borrowed the Latin adjective and reshaped it with -ical, the ending that makes relational adjectives such as metallurgical, chemical and practical.
items.cn: 英语借入拉丁形容词后，用 -ical 这一词尾重塑，它正是构成 metallurgical、chemical、practical 这类关系形容词的后缀。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the adjective attached itself to processes, grades, microscopes and failures, until metallurgical became a general label for anything belonging to the industrial handling of metal.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，这个形容词附着到工艺、等级、显微镜与失效上，逐渐成为任何与金属工业处理有关之物的通称。

items.en: Source uncertain: the earliest English use is not precisely dated, metallon has no agreed etymology, and every proposed Indo-European source for either Greek element is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定：最早的英语用例没有精确年代，metallon 没有公认词源，凡为两个希腊成分拟出的印欧来源都是重构。

note.en: Group one separates forms of the same family from near neighbours; group two separates words about metal as a material from words about working it.
note.cn: 第一组把同族形式与邻近词分开；第二组把指金属材料的词与指加工金属的词分开。

entries.definition: The field itself. The adjective describes something belonging to it; the noun names it.
entries.definitionCN: 这门学问本身。形容词描述属于它的东西，名词则是它的名称。

entries.definition: A rarer adjective with the same sense, built with -ic instead of -ical; the longer form is the usual one.
entries.definitionCN: 意义相同但少见的形容词，用 -ic 而非 -ical 构成；较长的那一种是常用形式。

entries.definition: An element between metals and non-metals. The -oid ending means 'like', so it is not an adjective of the field.
entries.definitionCN: 介于金属与非金属之间的元素。-oid 词尾意为「像」，因此它不是本学科的形容词。

entries.definition: The practitioner. It ends in -ist, which marks a person, not a property.
entries.definitionCN: 从业者。它以 -ist 结尾，标记的是人，而不是属性。

entries.definition: Made of metal, or resembling metal in shine or sound; it describes the material itself, not the science of winning it.
entries.definitionCN: 金属制的，或在光泽与声音上像金属的；它描述材料本身，而不是提取它的学问。

entries.definition: Containing metal, said of rock or ore; it is a statement about the ground, not about a process.
entries.definitionCN: 含金属的，用于岩石或矿石；它说的是地层，而不是工艺。

entries.definition: The shaping and joining of metal after it has been refined; metallurgical work begins earlier, at the ore.
entries.definitionCN: 金属精炼之后的成形与连接；冶金工作开始得更早，从矿石就开始了。

entries.definition: The broader study of all materials, of which the metallurgical branch is one part.
entries.definitionCN: 研究所有材料的更大学科，冶金分支只是其中一部分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two Greek elements, the Latin adjective, and the fixed phrases that mark each sense.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个希腊成分、拉丁形容词，以及标出各义项的固定搭配。

normal.en: metallon 'metal' + ergon 'work' + -ical: literally 'of the metal-working'. The whole adjective is readable from its parts.
normal.cn: metallon「金属」+ ergon「劳作」+ -ical：字面就是「属于金属加工的」。整个形容词可由各部分读出。

normal.en: The ending -ical makes a relation, not a substance: metallurgical research is research in the field, not research on metal alone.
normal.cn: -ical 词尾造出的是关系而非物质：冶金研究是在这门学问里做研究，而不只是研究金属。

normal.en: The neighbours sort themselves: metallurgy is the field, metallurgist the person, metallurgical the property of belonging to it.
normal.cn: 同族词各就各位：metallurgy 是学问，metallurgist 是从业者，metallurgical 是属于这门学问的属性。

normal.en: Its fixed phrases mark the stages: metallurgical process, metallurgical coal, metallurgical microscope, metallurgical failure.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各个阶段：冶金过程、炼焦煤、金相显微镜、冶金失效。

normal.en: The microscope is the giveaway: if the adjective is used with a lens, it points at structure rather than at ore.
normal.cn: 显微镜是个提示：当这个形容词与镜头一起出现，它指的是组织，而不是矿石。

abstract.en: Picture the adjective as a label pinned to a chain of stages, moving from rock to ingot to grain to broken part.
abstract.cn: 想象这个形容词是一枚标签，别在一条阶段链上：从石头到铸锭，到晶粒，再到断掉的零件。

abstract.en: Picture a metal's inside as a map of small territories, each boundary a place where cracks can start.
abstract.cn: 想象金属内部是一张小区划图，每条边界都是裂纹可能起步的地方。

abstract.en: Picture the word as a lens: it never looks at the metal from outside, only at what belongs to the craft that handles it.
abstract.cn: 想象这个词是一片透镜：它从不从外面看金属，只看属于处理金属那门手艺的东西。

examples.en: Metallurgical coke is produced in ovens that must be kept at a steady heat.
examples.cn: 冶金焦是在必须保持稳定温度的火炉中生产的。

examples.en: The report blamed a metallurgical defect rather than the welding.
examples.cn: 报告把问题归因于冶金缺陷，而不是焊接。

examples.en: Her metallurgical training let her read the slag like a page of history.
examples.cn: 她的冶金训练让她能把炉渣当作一页历史来读。

dict_mnemonic.text: metall（金属）+ urg（劳作）+ ical（形容词）＝ 金属加工的；记「炉前提取、镜后看晶粒」。

root: 希腊 metallon「金属、矿」+ ergon「劳作」→ metallourgia，拉丁形容词 metallurgicus，英语加 -ical；metallon 来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight adjective senses travel along the metal chain: the field, the ore, the grain, the grade, the failure, the industry, the people, and the museum test.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个形容词义项沿着金属链移动：学问、矿石、晶粒、等级、失效、产业、人员，最后是对器物的检验。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lens on polished metal, where bright grains meet along dark boundaries.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片抛光金属在镜头下，明亮的晶粒沿着暗色边界相接。

branches.en: THE FIELD: the adjective marks what belongs to the discipline itself.
branches.cn: 学问层：这个形容词标出属于学科本身的东西。

branches.en: THE FRONT OF THE CHAIN: extraction and refining, where rock becomes metal.
branches.cn: 链条前端：提取与精炼，石头在这里变成金属。

branches.en: THE INSIDE: grains and boundaries, seen in a works or measured in a museum.
branches.cn: 内部层：晶粒与边界，或在厂里被看见，或在博物馆里被测量。

branches.en: THE SCALE OF INDUSTRY: a graded raw material and a sector with plants and jobs.
branches.cn: 产业尺度：一种被定级的原料，以及拥有工厂与岗位的整个部门。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE AND THE BREAK: engineers and textbooks on one side, failures blamed on the metal on the other.
branches.cn: 人与断裂：一边是工程师与教科书，另一边是归咎于金属的失效。

intro.en: The adjective combines a Greek noun root, a Greek work root and a Latin-derived English ending; each piece is still productive.
intro.cn: 这个形容词组合了希腊名词词根、希腊「劳作」词根，以及源自拉丁的英语词尾；每一部分至今都能产。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplied metallum for the material, metallurgia for the craft and metallurgicus for the adjective; English took the last two through learned and technical writing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了指材料的 metallum、指工艺的 metallurgia，以及形容词 metallurgicus；英语经学术与技术文献吸收了后两者。

items.meaning: metal; metal-bearing
items.example: The metallo- prefix also opens metallocene.
items.exampleCN: metallo- 前缀也构成 metallocene。

items.meaning: working of a material
items.example: Dramaturgy uses the same work element.
items.exampleCN: dramaturgy 用了同一个「劳作」成分。

items.meaning: belonging to; connected with
items.example: The same ending builds chemical and practical.
items.exampleCN: 同一词尾也构成 chemical 与 practical。

items.meaning: the craft of winning and preparing metals
items.meaningCN: 提取与处理金属的工艺
items.example: Metallurgy is the noun behind this adjective.
items.exampleCN: metallurgy 是这个形容词背后的名词。

items.meaning: a person who practises the craft
items.example: A metallurgist checked the furnace lining.
items.exampleCN: 一位冶金学家检查了炉衬。

items.meaning: in metallurgical terms; as regards the metal
items.meaningCN: 从冶金角度看；就金属而言
items.example: The two ores are metallurgically similar.
items.exampleCN: 这两种矿石在冶金性质上相似。

items.meaning: belonging to fire-based metal winning
items.example: The pyrometallurgical route consumes less water.
items.exampleCN: 火法冶金路线耗水更少。

items.meaning: belonging to solution-based metal winning
items.example: The hydrometallurgical plant leaches copper from heaps.
items.exampleCN: 湿法冶金厂从矿堆中浸出铜。

items.meaning: not belonging to metal production
items.example: Nonmetallurgical uses of the coke include heating.
items.exampleCN: 这种焦炭的非冶金用途包括取暖。

latinEntries.structure: metallum, -i (n., second declension, from Greek metallon)

definition_zh: 金属加工；金工：把已经提炼的金属切割、成形、连接并进行表面处理，制成器物或构件的手艺与工业
definition_en: the craft and industry of cutting, forming, joining and finishing metal into objects or parts
core_image: 一块平板金属被夹在台钳上，锯、锉、钻孔之后逐步变成一只带铰链的盒子
scene: 台面上摆着锯、锉、钻与焊枪，师傅把一块平板金属一步步做成带铰链的盒子。Metalworking here still relies on hand tools more than on machines.
sceneCN: 这里指金属加工这门手艺整体（第 1 个义项：把金属材料加工成器物的工艺总称）；句意为这里的金属加工仍更多依靠手工工具，而不是机器。

pos.zh: 金属加工；金工（不可数，指工艺或行业总体）
（可数，指具体的加工活动或一次作业）

derivatives.zh: metal + work → 金工件；金属制品，语义偏移为「加工出来的物件」
metalworking + -er（从事者）→ 金工、金属加工工人
metal + ware（器皿）→ 金属器皿，语义偏移为「成套家用金属器具」
metal + smith（锻工）→ 金工师傅，语义偏移为「专做金属小件的匠人」
sheet（薄板）+ metalworking → 钣金加工，语义偏移为「以薄板为原料的成形工艺」

senses.title: The craft as a whole
senses.titleCN: 工艺总称：把金属变成器物的整套手艺
senses.definition: the whole craft of turning refined metal into useful objects
senses.definitionCN: 把精炼后的金属做成有用器物的整套手艺
senses.example: Metalworking here still relies on hand tools more than on machines.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的金属加工仍更多依靠手工工具，而不是机器。
senses.why: Metal leaves the smelter as a blank material; a second craft must give it shape, and the -ing form names that craft as one continuous activity rather than a single operation.
senses.whyCN: 金属从冶炼厂出来时只是一块空白材料；必须有第二门手艺给它形状，动名词形式把这门手艺说成一项持续的活动，而不是一个单独的操作。

senses.title: Cutting and forming
senses.titleCN: 切割与成形：锯、锉、车、铣、压
senses.definition: the operations that cut stock to size and shape it
senses.definitionCN: 把坯料切到尺寸并成形的各项操作
senses.example: Metalworking begins with measuring, marking and sawing the plate.
senses.exampleCN: 金属加工从量线、划线与锯板开始。
senses.why: Every later step depends on a clean cut and a true edge, so the craft's first skill is removing material exactly where it is not wanted.
senses.whyCN: 后面每一步都依赖干净的切口的准确边线，因此这门手艺的第一项本领，就是在不该有材料的地方精确地把它去掉。

senses.title: Joining and assembly
senses.titleCN: 连接与装配：焊接、铆接、螺栓固定
senses.definition: the operations that fasten separate pieces into one assembly
senses.definitionCN: 把分开的部件固定成一个整体的各项操作
senses.example: Metalworking includes welding, riveting and bolting.
senses.exampleCN: 金属加工包括焊接、铆接与螺栓连接。
senses.why: Once parts exist, they must be made to act as one body; heat, pressure or a fastener replaces the continuity that cutting destroyed.
senses.whyCN: 部件一旦存在，就必须让它们作为一个整体受力；热、压力或紧固件取代了切割所破坏的那种连续性。

senses.title: Finishing the surface
senses.titleCN: 表面处理与精饰：抛光、镀层、涂装
senses.definition: the operations that clean, polish, coat or otherwise finish a metal surface
senses.definitionCN: 对金属表面进行清洁、抛光、镀层或涂装的各项操作
senses.example: Final metalworking gives the sheet a brushed finish.
senses.exampleCN: 最后的金属加工给薄板做出拉丝表面。
senses.why: A surface is what a hand and an eye meet first, so the craft ends by controlling shine, texture and protection rather than shape.
senses.whyCN: 手和眼最先接触的是表面，因此这门手艺最后控制的是光泽、质感与防护，而不是形状。

senses.title: The shop
senses.titleCN: 作坊与车间：进行金工的场所
senses.definition: a workshop or bay where metal is worked
senses.definitionCN: 进行金属加工的作坊或车间
senses.example: The metalworking at the back of the yard was loud all day.
senses.exampleCN: 院子后面的金属加工车间整天都很吵。
senses.why: The activity's name transfers to the place built for it, because a shop is defined by the work done inside it.
senses.whyCN: 活动的名称转移到为它建造的场所，因为一个车间正是由里面所做的活计来定义的。

senses.title: A culture's metal craft
senses.titleCN: 历史与考古：某一文化的金属工艺
senses.definition: the metal craft of a place or period, studied from surviving objects and workshop waste
senses.definitionCN: 某一地点或时期的金属工艺，依据存世器物与作坊遗物研究
senses.example: Early metalworking in the region used native copper before any smelting.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区早期的金属加工在任何熔炼出现之前，先利用天然铜。
senses.why: Hammers, anvils and offcuts outlast the finished pieces, so a culture's craft can be reconstructed from the tools and scraps it left rather than from its treasures.
senses.whyCN: 锤子、砧子与边角料比成品存留得更久，因此一个文化的工艺可以从它留下的工具与碎料重建，而不是只靠珍品。

senses.title: The industry and the trade
senses.titleCN: 产业与职业：金属加工工业与工种
senses.definition: the sector that works metal commercially, and the occupation of those employed in it
senses.definitionCN: 以金属加工为业的产业部门，以及其中从业者的职业
senses.example: The metalworking sector employs more people than the smelter itself.
senses.exampleCN: 金属加工部门雇用的人比冶炼厂本身还多。
senses.why: A craft becomes an industry when its shops are counted together, and the same word then appears on payrolls, trade figures and training schemes.
senses.whyCN: 当众多作坊被合并计数，一门手艺就成了产业；同一个词随后出现在工资单、贸易数据与培训计划上。

senses.title: What comes out
senses.titleCN: 制品总体：加工出来的金属件
senses.definition: the collective output of metal parts and objects produced by the craft
senses.definitionCN: 这门手艺产出的金属件与器物的总体
senses.example: The museum's metalworking collection fills three rooms.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆的金属加工藏品占了三间展厅。
senses.why: Output can be named by the process that made it, so a shelf of hinges and brackets is spoken of as metalworking rather than as a list of parts.
senses.whyCN: 产出可以用制造它的过程来命名，于是一架铰链与托架被统称为金属加工品，而不是逐一列出零件。

intro.en: Metalworking is a transparent modern compound: an ancient borrowed noun for the material plus the oldest English verb for doing. Its parts are old, but the compound itself is modern.
intro.cn: metalworking 是一个透明的现代复合词：一个古老的借来名词指材料，加上英语最古老的动词之一表示「做」。部件很老，复合词本身却很新。

items.en: Metallon meant 'metal' and 'mine'. Its origin is uncertain, and the ancient connection with metalleuein 'to search after' explains the sense rather than proving the derivation.
items.cn: metallon 既指「金属」也指「矿」。它来源不确定，与 metalleuein「搜寻」的古老联系解释的是词义，而非证明了派生。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek noun as metallum and passed it to French, from which Middle English took metal. The Latin form also gave metallic and metallurgy their first element.
items.cn: 拉丁语把希腊名词借作 metallum，再传给法语，中古英语从法语取来 metal。这个拉丁形式也为 metallic 与 metallurgy 提供了第一个成分。

items.en: Work goes back to Old English weorc, with cognates across the Germanic languages. Its Indo-European ancestry is reconstructed, so the deepest form is not attested.
items.cn: work 可追溯到古英语 weorc，在日耳曼诸语中有同族词。它更早的印欧来源属于重构，最深的形式并无记录。

items.en: Metal entered English in the Middle Ages through Old French metal, alongside the older native words for iron and steel; work already had both the noun and the verb senses it has today.
items.cn: metal 在中世纪经古法语进入英语，与指铁和钢的本族老词并存；work 当时已具备今天所有的名词与动词义。

items.en: The compound metalworking belongs to modern industrial writing; metalwork is recorded earlier as a word for worked metal and for the craft, and the -ing form grows with factory vocabulary in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: metalworking 这一复合词属于现代工业文献；metalwork 更早被记录，指加工过的金属与这门工艺，而动名词形式随十九世纪的工厂词汇一同壮大。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first recorded use of the exact compound is not fixed, and the etymology of the Greek word for metal remains unsettled in every reference that discusses it.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这一确切复合词的最早书证没有定论，而希腊语「金属」一词的词源，在每一部讨论它的资料中都仍未解决。

note.en: Group one separates the close family forms; group two separates working metal from winning or studying it.
note.cn: 第一组把同族的近形词分开；第二组把加工金属与提取、研究金属分开。

entries.definition: The older noun for the craft and for worked metal as a class; metalworking stresses the activity and the industry.
entries.definitionCN: 更早的名词，指这门工艺或加工过的金属这一类东西；metalworking 更强调活动与产业。

entries.definition: The person who does the work; the -er ending marks the doer, not the doing.
entries.definitionCN: 做这项工作的人；-er 词尾标记做的人，而不是做的动作。

entries.definition: Metal household goods taken as a class; it names products, not the process that made them.
entries.definitionCN: 作为一类的家用金属器皿；它命名产品，而不是制造产品的过程。

entries.definition: The extraction and refining of metal from ore; the metal must exist before metalworking can begin.
entries.definitionCN: 从矿石中提取与精炼金属；金属必须先存在，金属加工才能开始。

entries.definition: Working hot metal with hammer and anvil; it is the oldest branch of metalworking, not the whole of it.
entries.definitionCN: 用锤与砧加工热金属；它是金属加工最古老的一支，而不是全部。

entries.definition: Cutting metal with powered tools to precise dimensions; one operation inside metalworking.
entries.definitionCN: 用动力工具把金属切到精确尺寸；是金属加工内部的一项操作。

entries.definition: Building a structure from cut and joined pieces, often on site; it uses metalworking methods but adds assembly and erection.
entries.definitionCN: 用切好并连接好的部件造出结构，常在现场进行；它使用金属加工方法，但多了装配与安装。

entries.definition: Making parts by pouring molten metal into moulds; casting is a different route from cutting and hammering.
entries.definitionCN: 把熔融金属浇入铸型来造零件；铸造走的是与切割、锤打不同的路线。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: two real words joined, a real family of forms, and stage words that mark the craft.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个真词合成、一组真实的同族形式，以及标出这门手艺各阶段的词。

normal.en: metal + working: the compound simply says what is done to the material, which is why it needs no Latin suffix.
normal.cn: metal + working：这个复合词直接说出对材料做了什么，所以它不需要任何拉丁词尾。

normal.en: The family is regular: metalwork for the craft or the goods, metalworker for the person, metalware for the products.
normal.cn: 同族形式很规整：metalwork 指工艺或制品，metalworker 指人，metalware 指产品。

normal.en: The stage words are all real operations: sawing, filing, drilling, turning, welding, riveting, polishing.
normal.cn: 各阶段的词都是真实操作：锯、锉、钻、车、焊、铆、抛光。

normal.en: Its fixed phrases name the material and the place: sheet metalworking, metalworking shop, metalworking industry.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出材料与场所：钣金加工、金工作坊、金属加工工业。

normal.en: The contrast to remember is with metallurgy: winning metal from rock versus shaping metal already won.
normal.cn: 要记住的对比是与 metallurgy：从石头里取金属，对比把取来的金属做成形。

abstract.en: Picture a flat sheet as a sentence that the craft rewrites by removing, joining and polishing.
abstract.cn: 想象一块平板是一句话，这门手艺通过去掉、连接与打磨来改写它。

abstract.en: Picture four rooms in a row: one cuts, one joins, one smooths, one checks the shine.
abstract.cn: 想象并排的四个房间：一间在切，一间在接，一间在磨，一间在看光泽。

abstract.en: Picture the same workshop seen twice, once as a noisy bay and once as a museum shelf of hinges.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个作坊看两次：一次是吵闹的车间，一次是博物馆里摆满铰链的架子。

examples.en: Sheet metalworking turns flat stock into ducts and casings.
examples.cn: 钣金加工把平板坯料做成风管与外壳。

examples.en: Metalworking tools were among the first objects buried with their owners.
examples.cn: 金工工具是最早与主人一同下葬的物件之一。

examples.en: The metalworking shop makes brackets for the same factory it supplies.
examples.cn: 这家金工作坊为它所供货的那家工厂制作托架。

dict_mnemonic.text: metal（金属）+ working（加工）＝ 金属加工；记「先切、再成形、再连接、最后抛光」。

root: metal 来自希腊 metallon「金属、矿」，经拉丁 metallum 与古法语进入英语；working 来自古英语 weorc「劳作」。两词合用，指金属成形的手艺。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the stock: it is cut, formed, joined and finished, and the work also names a shop, a culture, an industry and its output.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着坯料走：被切、成形、连接、精饰；这门活计又命名了车间、一种文化、一个产业以及它的产出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: flat stock is measured, cut, bent, joined and polished until it is a finished object.
core.cn: 核心意象：平板坯料被量、切、弯、接、磨，直到成为一件成品。

branches.en: THE CRAFT: the whole second stage that begins after the metal is already refined.
branches.cn: 手艺整体：金属精炼之后才开始的整个第二阶段。

branches.en: TAKING MATERIAL AWAY AND PUTTING IT TOGETHER: cutting and forming, then welding and fastening.
branches.cn: 去掉材料与把材料接上：先切割成形，再焊接紧固。

branches.en: THE SURFACE: polishing and coating, where the eye and the hand meet the object.
branches.cn: 表面：抛光与镀层，手和眼在这里接触器物。

branches.en: THE PLACE AND THE PAST: a noisy shop here, a reconstructed craft tradition there.
branches.cn: 场所与过去：一边是吵闹的车间，一边是被重建的工艺传统。

branches.en: THE SCALE AND THE OUTPUT: a whole sector with payrolls, and the parts that come out of it.
branches.cn: 规模与产出：一个有工资单的完整部门，以及从中出来的零件。

intro.en: The compound is built from a borrowed noun and a native verb, and both halves take ordinary English endings.
intro.cn: 这个复合词由借来的名词与本族动词搭成，两半都接普通英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin contributes only the material word, metallum, borrowed in turn from Greek; the working half is native English, so the compound is mixed in origin by design.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语只贡献了材料词 metallum（它又借自希腊语）；「加工」那一半是英语本族词，因此这个复合词在来源上本来就是混合的。

items.structure: metal (n., from Old French, from Latin metallum, from Greek metallon)
items.meaning: a hard shiny material such as iron or copper
items.meaningCN: 铁、铜一类坚硬有光泽的材料
items.example: The metal is delivered as flat sheet.
items.exampleCN: 金属以平板形式送进车间。

items.structure: work (native verb and noun, Old English weorc)
items.meaning: to do; to shape or make by effort
items.example: They work the sheet by hand.
items.exampleCN: 他们用手工加工这块薄板。

items.meaning: the activity as a continuing process
items.example: Working the edge takes patience.
items.exampleCN: 加工边口需要耐心。

items.meaning: the craft, or worked metal as a class
items.meaningCN: 这门工艺，或作为一类的加工金属
items.example: The gate is fine metalwork.
items.exampleCN: 这扇门是精细的金工件。

items.meaning: one who works metal
items.example: The metalworker marked the plate before cutting.
items.exampleCN: 金工在切之前先在板上划线。

items.meaning: metal household goods as a class
items.meaningCN: 作为一类的金属家用器具
items.example: The stall sells brass and copper metalware.
items.exampleCN: 这个摊位卖黄铜与紫铜器皿。

items.meaning: working thin flat metal into shapes
items.meaningCN: 把金属薄板加工成各种形状
items.example: Sheet metalworking produces the ductwork.
items.exampleCN: 钣金加工造出这些风管。

items.meaning: the craft and industry of shaping metal
items.meaningCN: 金属成形的手艺与产业
items.example: Metalworking is taught next to welding.
items.exampleCN: 金属加工与焊接在同一处教授。

latinEntries.structure: metallum, -i (n., second declension, from Greek metallon)

definition_zh: 青铜：以铜为主、加入锡等元素熔成的合金；也指它的颜色、青铜器物、铜牌以及染色与晒黑等引申义
definition_en: an alloy of copper with tin or another metal, and by extension its colour, objects made from it and a third-place medal
core_image: 铸范打开，一件青铜斧还带着余温，表面从亮金渐渐转为青灰
scene: 铸范打开，一件斧头还带着余温，表面由亮金渐渐转成青灰。The bronze in the workshop was melted from copper and tin.
sceneCN: 这里指青铜这种合金（第 1 个义项：铜与锡等元素合成的金属材料）；句意为作坊里的青铜是由铜和锡熔炼而成的。

pos.zh: 青铜；青铜合金（不可数）
青铜色；古铜色（颜色）
青铜制品（总称，或可数指一件）
青铜制的；青铜色的
使呈青铜色；（皮肤）晒成古铜色

derivatives.zh: bronze + -ed（过去分词形容词）→ 呈青铜色的，语义偏移为「皮肤被晒成古铜色的」
bronze + -ing（动名词）→ 上青铜色；表面处理中的着色工序
bronze + -er（物）→ 修容粉，语义偏移为「让皮肤显古铜色的化妆品」
bronze + -y（形容词后缀）→ 青铜般的，语义偏移为「颜色或光泽近似青铜的」
bronze + colour + -ed → 青铜色的复合形容词

senses.title: The alloy
senses.titleCN: 青铜：铜与锡熔成的合金
senses.definition: a metal made mainly of copper with tin or another element added
senses.definitionCN: 以铜为主，掺入锡或其他元素制成的金属
senses.example: The bronze in the workshop was melted from copper and tin.
senses.exampleCN: 作坊里的青铜是由铜和锡熔炼而成的。
senses.why: Copper alone is soft; adding tin makes it harder and easier to cast, and the resulting alloy takes a name of its own rather than staying a kind of copper.
senses.whyCN: 纯铜偏软；加入锡使它更硬也更好铸，于是这种合金得到了自己的名称，而不再只被当作铜的一种。

senses.title: The colour
senses.titleCN: 青铜色：从金黄到青灰的那一层颜色
senses.definition: the brownish or greenish-gold colour of bronze
senses.definitionCN: 青铜那种偏褐或偏青的金色
senses.example: The sky turned a deep bronze before the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨前，天空变成深青铜色。
senses.why: A metal's colour is one of its most memorable properties, so the material word serves directly as a colour name without any added suffix.
senses.whyCN: 金属的颜色是它最容易记住的性质之一，因此材料名可以直接充当颜色名，不必另加词尾。

senses.title: Bronzes as a class
senses.titleCN: 青铜器物：作为一类的青铜制品
senses.definition: objects made of bronze taken together as a group
senses.definitionCN: 作为一类来看的青铜制品
senses.example: The museum's bronzes date from the late period.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆的青铜器属于晚期。
senses.why: A material name often stands for what is made from it; a whole collection can be called by the metal, with the objects understood.
senses.whyCN: 材料名常常代替用它做成的东西；整整一批藏品可以用这种金属来称呼，器物本身则被默认。

senses.title: One cast piece
senses.titleCN: 一件青铜制品：可数用法
senses.definition: a single object, usually cast, made of bronze
senses.definitionCN: 单件青铜器物，通常为铸造而成
senses.example: A small bronze stood at the corner of the table.
senses.exampleCN: 桌角立着一件小型青铜器。
senses.why: Once the class sense exists, the same noun can count individual pieces, especially in gallery and auction language.
senses.whyCN: 类别义一旦成立，同一个名词就能数单件，在画廊与拍卖语言中尤其如此。

senses.title: Third place
senses.titleCN: 铜牌：第三名的奖牌
senses.definition: a medal awarded for third place in a competition
senses.definitionCN: 比赛中授予第三名的奖牌
senses.example: She took bronze in the 400 metres.
senses.exampleCN: 她在四百米比赛中获得铜牌。
senses.why: Medals are ranked by metal, and the third rank was assigned the cheapest of the three customary metals, so the material's name became the rank's name.
senses.whyCN: 奖牌按金属排等级，第三等被分给三种常用金属中最便宜的一种，于是材料名就成了名次名。

senses.title: Made of bronze
senses.titleCN: 青铜制的：形容词用法
senses.definition: made of or relating to bronze
senses.definitionCN: 用青铜制成的，或与青铜有关的
senses.example: A bronze plate marked the entrance.
senses.exampleCN: 入口处挂着一块青铜铭牌。
senses.why: English lets a material noun modify another noun without change of form, so the same word works as an adjective of substance.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许材料名词不加形态变化就修饰另一名词，因此同一个词可以直接充当表示材质的形容词。

senses.title: To bronze the skin
senses.titleCN: 晒成古铜色：动词用法
senses.definition: to give something, especially skin, a bronze colour
senses.definitionCN: 使某物（尤指皮肤）呈现青铜色
senses.example: They bronzed themselves on the roof all summer.
senses.exampleCN: 整个夏天他们都在屋顶上把皮肤晒成古铜色。
senses.why: The colour sense turns into a verb: applying the metal's hue to a surface, whether by sun, lotion or plating, is expressed by the material's name.
senses.whyCN: 颜色义转为动词：把这种金属的色调加到某个表面上，不论靠太阳、乳液还是电镀，都用这种材料名来表达。

senses.title: Shorthand for the age
senses.titleCN: 青铜时代的简称
senses.definition: a short way of referring to the Bronze Age
senses.definitionCN: 对青铜时代的简称
senses.example: The site spans the late bronze into the early iron.
senses.exampleCN: 这处遗址从青铜时代晚期延续到铁器时代早期。
senses.why: Because the age is named after the metal, the metal alone can carry the period in running text, especially in archaeology.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个时代以这种金属命名，金属名本身就能在行文中代替那个时期，在考古文献中尤其如此。

intro.en: Bronze reached English through Italian and French. The medieval Latin word behind it has no settled origin, so the usual reference works offer competing suggestions rather than a proven source.
intro.cn: bronze 经意大利语与法语进入英语。它背后的中世纪拉丁词没有定论来源，因此常见词源资料给出的是并列的猜测，而非已证实的源头。

items.en: Italian bronzo named the alloy from the fourteenth century, and its form is the earliest well-attested link in the chain that leads to English.
items.cn: 意大利语 bronzo 自十四世纪起指这种合金，它的形态是通往英语这条链上最早的有力书证。

items.en: Medieval Latin bronzium is usually cited as the form behind the Italian word. Its own origin is uncertain: one suggestion ties it to the port of Brindisi, another to a Byzantine Greek term, and neither is demonstrated.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 bronzium 常被引作意大利词背后的形式。它自身的来源不确定：一种猜测把它联系到布林迪西港，另一种联系到某个拜占庭希腊词，两种都未获证实。

items.en: French bronze appears in the sixteenth century and English borrowed it in the eighteenth. The same French form also gave English its spelling with the final silent e.
items.cn: 法语 bronze 出现于十六世纪，英语在十八世纪借入。同一个法语形式也让英语保留了词尾不发音的 e。

items.en: The colour sense follows the material directly. The medal sense grows with ranked competitions in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, when third place was regularly marked in bronze.
items.cn: 颜色义直接跟随材料义。奖牌义随十九与二十世纪的名次赛制成长，第三名通常用青铜标记。

items.en: Source uncertain: no origin for bronzium is accepted, the earliest written dates are approximate, and the material itself was known in Europe long before any of these words were recorded.
items.cn: 来源不确定：bronzium 没有任何公认来源，最早书证年代只是大致，而这种合金在欧洲被人使用的时间，远早于这些词被记录。

note.en: Group one holds words that are easily swapped for bronze; group two holds the metals and objects it is usually compared with.
note.cn: 第一组是容易与 bronze 互换的词；第二组是常与它比较的金属与物件。

entries.definition: Made of brass, and by extension shameless. It belongs to the brass family, not to bronze, and also means 'bold'.
entries.definitionCN: 黄铜制的，引申为厚颜无耻的。它属于黄铜一族而非青铜，另有「大胆的」之义。

entries.definition: Given a bronze colour, usually of skin. It is a form of the same word, not a different metal.
entries.definitionCN: 被染成青铜色的，通常指皮肤。它是同一个词的形式，不是另一种金属。

entries.definition: A copper alloy with zinc, yellower and easier to machine; bronze is copper with tin, and the two are routinely confused.
entries.definitionCN: 铜与锌的合金，更黄也更好切削；青铜是铜与锡的合金，两者常被混淆。

entries.definition: The archaeological period named after the metal; the metal alone is a material, while the phrase names a stretch of time.
entries.definitionCN: 以这种金属命名的考古时期；单独的材料名指物质，而这个短语指一段时间。

entries.definition: The reddish metal that forms the main part of bronze; copper is an element, bronze is a mixture.
entries.definitionCN: 构成青铜主体的红色金属；铜是元素，青铜是混合物。

entries.definition: Any metal deliberately mixed with another; bronze is one alloy among many.
entries.definitionCN: 任何有意把一种金属与另一种混合所得的金属；青铜只是众多合金中的一种。

entries.definition: The green or brown film that age gives a bronze surface; it is the metal's skin, not the metal.
entries.definitionCN: 岁月在青铜表面留下的绿或褐色薄膜；它是金属的表皮，而不是金属本身。

entries.definition: The object awarded for a place in a competition; bronze is only the grade of one such medal.
entries.definitionCN: 比赛中按名次授予的物件；bronze 只是其中某一等级的名称。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real metals involved, the real colour shift and the real medal ranking.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实涉及的金属、真实的颜色变化，以及真实的名次排列。

normal.en: Bronze is copper plus tin: the base metal gives the body, the added metal gives the hardness.
normal.cn: 青铜是铜加锡：基底金属提供主体，加入的金属提供硬度。

normal.en: The colour runs from gold to green as the surface oxidises, which is why old bronze looks nothing like new bronze.
normal.cn: 随着表面氧化，颜色从金黄走向青绿，所以旧青铜看起来与新青铜完全不同。

normal.en: The medal ladder is gold, silver, bronze; third place is the bronze rung.
normal.cn: 奖牌阶梯是金、银、铜；第三名就是青铜这一级。

normal.en: The family is regular: bronzed for the colour, bronzing for the process, bronzer for the cosmetic.
normal.cn: 同族形式很规整：bronzed 表颜色，bronzing 表工序，bronzer 表化妆品。

normal.en: The fixed phrases mark the uses: cast in bronze, bronze statue, bronze medal, bronzed skin.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：青铜铸造、青铜像、铜牌、古铜色皮肤。

abstract.en: Picture a metal that changes colour as it ages, so time is visible on its skin.
abstract.cn: 想象一种会随年龄变色的金属，于是时间就写在它的表皮上。

abstract.en: Picture three metals stacked as a staircase, with the cheapest one holding up the third step.
abstract.cn: 想象三种金属叠成一道楼梯，最便宜的那一种托着第三级。

abstract.en: Picture a mould opening: the same metal is first liquid fire and then a cold grey tool.
abstract.cn: 想象铸范打开的一刻：同一种金属先是流动的火，随后成了冷灰的工具。

examples.en: The bell is cast in bronze and has rung for four centuries.
examples.cn: 这口钟以青铜铸成，已经敲了四百年。

examples.en: Collectors distinguish early bronzes by the shape of their handles.
examples.cn: 收藏者靠把手形状来区分早期青铜器。

examples.en: He finished third and brought home a bronze.
examples.cn: 他得了第三名，带回来一枚铜牌。

dict_mnemonic.text: bronze＝铜加锡的合金；记「金黄入范、青灰出范、第三名挂铜牌」。

root: 经意大利语 bronzo、法语 bronze 进入英语；其背后的中世纪拉丁 bronzium 来源不确定，常见猜测或联系布林迪西港，或联系某个拜占庭希腊词，均未证实。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses radiate from one metal: the alloy, its colour, its objects as a class, one such object, a third-place medal, the material as an adjective, the act of bronzing, and the age named after it.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从同一种金属向外辐射：合金本身、它的颜色、作为一类的器物、单件器物、铜牌、作定语的材质、晒成古铜色的动作，以及以它命名的时代。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: copper and tin melt together, take a mould's shape, and slowly turn from gold to green-grey.
core.cn: 核心意象：铜与锡熔在一起，取得铸范的形状，再慢慢从金黄转为青灰。

branches.en: THE MIXTURE ITSELF: copper needs tin to become harder and castable.
branches.cn: 混合物本身：铜需要锡才能变得更硬、更好铸。

branches.en: THE COLOUR: the metal's hue becomes a colour word, then a verb for giving that hue.
branches.cn: 颜色：金属的色调成为颜色词，再成为赋予这种色调的动词。

branches.en: THE OBJECTS: a whole class of bronzes, and one countable piece in a gallery.
branches.cn: 器物：作为一整类的青铜器，以及画廊里可数的一件。

branches.en: THE RANK: third place wears the cheapest of the three medal metals.
branches.cn: 名次：第三名佩戴三种奖牌金属中最便宜的一种。

branches.en: THE MODIFIER AND THE PERIOD: material as adjective, skin bronzed by sun, and the age called by the metal's name.
branches.cn: 修饰与时期：作定语的材质、被太阳晒成古铜色的皮肤，以及用金属名命名的时代。

intro.en: Bronze is a borrowed noun that became a verb and an adjective without adding a prefix; its endings are all ordinary English ones.
intro.cn: bronze 是借来的名词，不加前缀就变成了动词与形容词；它接的词尾都是普通英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin form behind the word, bronzium, is medieval and its origin is uncertain; Latin also had aes for copper or bronze, but that is a different word with a different history.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词背后的拉丁形式 bronzium 属中世纪，来源不确定；拉丁语另有 aes 指铜或青铜，但那是另一个词，历史也不同。

definition_zh: 青铜时代：以青铜器作为主要技术标志的考古时期，位于石器时代与铁器时代之间；也指某一地区的这一阶段及其文化
definition_en: the archaeological period marked by the use of bronze, between the Stone Age and the Iron Age, and the regional stage of that period
core_image: 展柜里一排青铜剑、斧与饰件，标签只写着一个年代区间
scene: 展柜里并排摆着青铜剑、斧与饰件，标签上只写着一个年代区间。The term Bronze Age was coined to name a period defined by its metal rather than by its rulers.
sceneCN: 这里指作为考古分期的青铜时代（第 1 个义项：以青铜器为标志的时期名）；句意为「青铜时代」这一说法，是为命名一个由金属而非由统治者定义的时期而造的。

pos.zh: 青铜时代（专有名词，考古分期）
某一地区的青铜时代阶段及其文化
青铜时代的（作定语，常写作 bronze-age 或 Bronze Age）

forms.label: 相关称法（铜石并用阶段）

derivatives.zh: bronze（青铜）+ age（时代）中的材料基础 → 合金本身；时代名由材料名加「时代」构成
bronze age + 连字符作定语 → 青铜时代的，语义偏移为「属于该期风格或技术的」
小写连字符形式 → 青铜时代的（多见于英式行文）
bronze age + man → 青铜时代的人，语义偏移为「该期人群的泛称」

senses.title: The named period
senses.titleCN: 时期名：考古分期中的青铜阶段
senses.definition: the period of human culture between the Stone Age and the Iron Age, marked by the use of bronze
senses.definitionCN: 介于石器时代与铁器时代之间、以使用青铜为标志的人类文化时期
senses.example: The term Bronze Age was coined to name a period defined by its metal rather than by its rulers.
senses.exampleCN: 「青铜时代」这一说法，是为命名一个由金属而非由统治者定义的时期而造的。
senses.why: The name comes from a classification that sorts whole societies by their dominant material; bronze is the material that follows stone and precedes iron in that sequence.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字来自一种按主导材料给整个社会分期的分类法；在这一序列里，青铜是排在石头之后、铁之前的材料。

senses.title: A region's version
senses.titleCN: 地区性阶段：某一地区的青铜时代
senses.definition: the local stretch of time in which a particular region used bronze as its main metal
senses.definitionCN: 某一地区以青铜为主要金属的那一段本地时间
senses.example: The Bronze Age began later in northern Europe than in the Aegean.
senses.exampleCN: 北欧的青铜时代比爱琴海地区开始得晚。
senses.why: A single label cannot start everywhere at once, because metal reaches different regions at different times; the phrase therefore always carries a place with it.
senses.whyCN: 同一个标签不可能在所有地方同时开始，因为金属到达各地区的时间不同；因此这个短语总是要带上一个地点。

senses.title: The society of the period
senses.titleCN: 该期的社会与文化
senses.definition: the people, settlements and way of life of that period taken as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 作为整体来看的该时期人群、聚落与生活方式
senses.example: Bronze Age society in the valley was organised around a few large tells.
senses.exampleCN: 这个山谷里的青铜时代社会围绕几座大型土丘聚落组织起来。
senses.why: A period name easily stands for the life lived inside it, so the phrase can name a society rather than just a stretch on a chart.
senses.whyCN: 时期名很容易代替该时期内生活本身，因此这个短语可以命名一个社会，而不只是图表上的一段。

senses.title: The attributive use
senses.titleCN: 定语用法：青铜时代的器物与遗址
senses.definition: used before a noun to mark an object, site or practice as belonging to that period
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前，标明某器物、遗址或做法属于该时期
senses.example: Bronze Age artefacts were found beneath the plough soil.
senses.exampleCN: 在耕作层之下发现了青铜时代的器物。
senses.why: English lets a period name modify a noun directly, so one phrase can turn a pot, a grave or a farm into a dated thing.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许时期名直接修饰名词，于是一个短语就能把一只罐、一座墓或一处农庄变成有年代归属的东西。

senses.title: A rung in the ladder
senses.titleCN: 分期体系中的位置：三段序列的中间一级
senses.definition: the middle term of the three-age system of Stone, Bronze and Iron
senses.definitionCN: 石、青铜、铁三段分期体系中的中间一项
senses.example: The three-age system places the Bronze Age between stone and iron.
senses.exampleCN: 三段分期体系把青铜时代放在石器与铁器之间。
senses.why: The name only works inside a ladder: without the stone rung below and the iron rung above, bronze would be a material rather than a stage.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字只在一条阶梯里成立：没有下面的石器一级和上面的铁器一级，青铜就只是一种材料，而不是一个阶段。

senses.title: Early, middle and late
senses.titleCN: 早中晚三段：更细的分期
senses.definition: a subdivision of the period into early, middle and late phases
senses.definitionCN: 把该时期细分为早期、中期与晚期
senses.example: The Late Bronze Age saw a sharp rise in trade goods.
senses.exampleCN: 青铜时代晚期，贸易品数量骤增。
senses.why: A long period needs internal divisions to be usable, and the standard early, middle and late labels are added in front of the same name.
senses.whyCN: 一段长时期需要内部划分才好用，于是标准的早、中、晚三个标签被加在同一个名字前面。

senses.title: Evidence and dating
senses.titleCN: 证据与断代：凭什么判断这一时期
senses.definition: the material evidence, such as slag, moulds and bronze objects, used to date and define the period
senses.definitionCN: 用来判定与界定该时期的有形证据，如炉渣、铸范与青铜器
senses.example: Slag and clay moulds are the Bronze Age evidence that survives best.
senses.exampleCN: 炉渣与陶范是留存最好的青铜时代证据。
senses.why: A period named after an industry is dated by that industry's waste: furnaces and moulds are more durable than the objects they produced.
senses.whyCN: 以某个行业命名的时期，要靠该行业的废弃物来断代：炉子与铸范比它们产出的器物更耐久。

senses.title: An old stage, in speech
senses.titleCN: 口语比喻：过时、老旧的阶段
senses.definition: used informally for an outdated stage of technology or practice
senses.definitionCN: 非正式用法，指技术或做法上已经过时的阶段
senses.example: Their booking system belongs to the bronze age of computing.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的订票系统还停留在计算机的青铜时代。
senses.why: Once a period name means 'early and superseded', it can be borrowed for anything old-fashioned, and the metal's low rank in the ladder supplies the joke.
senses.whyCN: 一旦一个时期名意味着「早期且已被取代」，它就能被借来形容任何过时之物，而金属在阶梯上的低位置正好提供笑点。

intro.en: The phrase joins a borrowed metal name to a native period word, and its modern sense comes from a nineteenth-century scheme for sorting prehistory by materials.
intro.cn: 这个短语把一个借来的金属名与一个本族的时期词接在一起，现代义来自十九世纪按材料给史前分期的方案。

items.en: Bronze came to English from Italian bronzo through French; the medieval Latin word behind it, bronzium, has no settled origin, and the competing suggestions for it are unproven.
items.cn: bronze 经法语从意大利语 bronzo 进入英语；其背后的中世纪拉丁词 bronzium 没有定论来源，各种竞争性的猜测都未获证实。

items.en: Age comes from Latin aetas through Old French aage, and meant a lifetime or a span of time before it came to name a division of history.
items.cn: age 经古法语 aage 来自拉丁 aetas，在用来指历史分期之前，本义是一生或一段时间。

items.en: The classification of prehistory into Stone, Bronze and Iron ages was set out by Christian Jürgensen Thomsen in a museum guide in the 1830s, based on the materials of the finds themselves.
items.cn: 把史前分为石器、青铜与铁器三个时代的分类法，由汤姆森在十九世纪三十年代的一部博物馆指南中提出，依据的是出土物本身的材料。

items.en: English adopted Bronze Age in the middle of the nineteenth century, together with the rest of the three-age vocabulary, and applied it first to European and Mediterranean sequences.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪中叶采纳 Bronze Age 这一说法，与三段分期的其余词汇一同进入，并最先用于欧洲与地中海的年代序列。

items.en: Twentieth-century archaeology subdivided the period into early, middle and late phases, extended it region by region, and let the phrase serve as an attributive label for objects, sites and societies.
items.cn: 二十世纪考古学把该时期细分为早、中、晚三段，逐地区推广，并让这个短语充当器物、遗址与社会的定语标签。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact first English citation is not fixed, the origin of bronze is unknown, and the dates of the period shift from region to region by centuries.
items.cn: 来源不确定：确切的英语首见书证没有定论，bronze 的来源不明，而这个时期的年代在不同地区相差数百年。

note.en: Group one separates the phrase from its own shorter forms and neighbours; group two separates it from the other period names.
note.cn: 第一组把这个短语与它自身的短形式及邻近说法分开；第二组把它与别的时期名分开。

entries.definition: The alloy itself. The phrase names a period; the bare noun names the substance and its objects.
entries.definitionCN: 合金本身。这个短语命名一个时期，而单独的名词命名物质及其器物。

entries.definition: The same phrase written with a hyphen when it stands before a noun; the hyphen marks its job as an adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 同一短语在名词前作定语时加连字符；连字符标出它充当形容词的角色。

entries.definition: An old name for an age of shamelessness in classical myth, built on brass rather than bronze; it is a moral label, not a material period.
entries.definitionCN: 古典神话中表示无耻时代的老说法，基于黄铜而非青铜；它是道德标签，不是材料分期。

entries.definition: The name for the sudden breakdown of eastern Mediterranean societies around the twelfth century BCE; it is an episode inside the period.
entries.definitionCN: 指公元前十二世纪前后东地中海社会突然崩溃的说法；它是该时期内部的一个事件。

entries.definition: The earlier period in the same three-age scheme, marked by stone tools.
entries.definitionCN: 同一三段体系中更早的时期，以石器为标志。

entries.definition: The following period in the same scheme, marked by iron working.
entries.definitionCN: 同一体系中随后的时期，以铁器加工为标志。

entries.definition: The transitional stage in which copper was worked alongside stone, often placed just before the Bronze Age.
entries.definitionCN: 铜与石器并用的过渡阶段，常被放在青铜时代之前。

entries.definition: Any dated division of the past defined by material or culture; the Bronze Age is one such division.
entries.definitionCN: 按材料或文化划定的任何有年代的过去片段；青铜时代只是其中一个划分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the metal in the phrase, the ladder of the three ages, and the real regional names.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：短语里的金属、三个时代的阶梯，以及真实的地区名称。

normal.en: The phrase is self-explaining: bronze + age, a stretch of time labelled by its dominant metal.
normal.cn: 这个短语自我解释：青铜 + 时代，用主导金属给一段时间贴标签。

normal.en: The ladder is stone, bronze, iron; the middle rung is the one this phrase names.
normal.cn: 阶梯是石、青铜、铁；这个短语命名的正是中间一级。

normal.en: Regional names are real and useful: Aegean Bronze Age, Early Bronze Age, Late Bronze Age.
normal.cn: 地区名称真实有用：爱琴海青铜时代、青铜时代早期、青铜时代晚期。

normal.en: The evidence words are slag, mould and crucible: waste that outlasts the objects.
normal.cn: 证据词是炉渣、铸范与坩埚：比器物存留更久的废弃物。

normal.en: The phrase is proper when it names the period and lowercase-hyphenated when it modifies a noun.
normal.cn: 作专名指该时期时首字母大写；修饰名词时常用小写加连字符。

abstract.en: Picture prehistory as a staircase with three steps, each labelled by the material that people could shape at the time.
abstract.cn: 想象史前是一道三级楼梯，每一级都用当时人们能加工的材料来命名。

abstract.en: Picture a museum case where the metal objects and the clay moulds that made them sit side by side.
abstract.cn: 想象一只展柜，金属器物与造出它们的陶范并排放着。

abstract.en: Picture the same phrase travelling from a chart to a pot: first a period, then an adjective on a label.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个短语从图表走到一只陶罐上：先是时期，随后成了标签上的定语。

examples.en: The Bronze Age in this valley ended with a shift in trade routes.
examples.cn: 这个山谷的青铜时代以贸易路线的改变而结束。

examples.en: Bronze Age graves often contain both weapons and imported beads.
examples.cn: 青铜时代的墓葬常同时随葬武器与外来珠子。

examples.en: The museum labels the case as Late Bronze Age.
examples.cn: 博物馆把这只展柜标为青铜时代晚期。

dict_mnemonic.text: bronze（青铜）+ age（时代）＝ 青铜时代；记「石—青铜—铁，中间那一级」。

root: bronze 经意大利与法语借入，来源不确定；age 经古法语来自拉丁 aetas「一生、时期」。两词合成，指以青铜为标志的考古时期。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses trace one label: the period itself, its regional versions, its society, its attributive use, its place in the ladder, its subdivisions, its evidence, and its joking use for anything outdated.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一个标签展开：时期本身、地区版本、该期社会、定语用法、在阶梯上的位置、内部细分、断代证据，以及用来调侃过时之物的用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a museum case of bronze blades and ornaments under a label that gives only a span of years.
core.cn: 核心意象：一柜青铜兵器与饰件，上方标签只写着一个年代区间。

branches.en: THE LABEL: a single name for the middle stage of a three-part scheme.
branches.cn: 标签本身：三段体系中中间阶段的单一名称。

branches.en: THE LOCAL AND THE INTERNAL: one region's stretch of the period, and its early, middle and late subdivisions.
branches.cn: 地方与内部：某一地区的那一段，以及它的早、中、晚三段。

branches.en: THE LIFE INSIDE: the label stands for the people and settlements of the period.
branches.cn: 期内生活：标签代替了该时期的人群与聚落。

branches.en: THE MODIFIER: attached to pots and sites in the normal way, and borrowed in speech for anything outdated.
branches.cn: 修饰用法：正常地附着到陶罐与遗址上，也被口语借去形容过时之物。

branches.en: THE LADDER AND THE PROOF: a rung between stone and iron, held up by slag, moulds and dated metal.
branches.cn: 阶梯与证据：夹在石器与铁器之间的一级，由炉渣、铸范与可测年的金属支撑。

intro.en: The phrase is a compound of two free words, and only the second carries the period sense; the hyphen appears when the compound works as an adjective.
intro.cn: 这个短语是两个自由词构成的复合词，只有第二个词带时期义；当它作形容词时会出现连字符。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the second word through aetas, and a medieval Latin form stands behind the first word; that form's own origin, however, is not established.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语通过 aetas 提供第二个词，第一个词背后有一个中世纪拉丁形式；不过那个形式自身的来源并未确立。

items.structure: bronze (n., borrowed through French from Italian)
items.meaning: the copper-tin alloy
items.example: Bronze tools define the period.
items.exampleCN: 青铜工具界定了这个时期。

items.structure: age (n., from Old French, from Latin aetas)
items.meaning: a span of time; a historical stage
items.example: The age lasted several centuries here.
items.exampleCN: 这一时代在这里延续了数百年。

items.meaning: the middle stage of the three-age system
items.meaningCN: 三段分期体系中的中间阶段
items.example: The Bronze Age followed the Stone Age.
items.exampleCN: 青铜时代紧接石器时代。

items.meaning: belonging to that period
items.example: A Bronze-Age barrow lies on the ridge.
items.exampleCN: 山脊上有一座青铜时代古墓。

items.meaning: the same attributive use in running text
items.meaningCN: 行文中的同一作定语用法
items.example: The bronze-age layers lie below the Roman ones.
items.exampleCN: 青铜时代的地层位于罗马地层之下。

items.meaning: the first phase of the period
items.example: Early Bronze Age pottery is coarse but distinctive.
items.exampleCN: 青铜时代早期的陶器粗糙但有特征。

items.meaning: the final phase of the period
items.example: Trade networks peaked in the Late Bronze Age.
items.exampleCN: 贸易网络在青铜时代晚期达到顶峰。

items.meaning: the breakdown of societies at the end of the period
items.meaningCN: 该时期末期社会体系的崩溃
items.example: The Bronze Age collapse is dated to about twelve hundred before the common era.
items.exampleCN: 青铜时代崩溃被定在公元前一千二百年左右。

latinEntries.meaning: life; age; a period of time

definition_zh: 铁：一种坚硬常见的金属元素；也指铁器、熨斗、高尔夫铁杆，以及「坚硬、不可动摇」等引申义
definition_en: a hard grey metal, the element Fe, and objects made from it such as tools, a pressing device or a golf club
core_image: 铁水从炉口倒进锭模，冷却成暗红的铁锭，锤子敲上去发出清硬的响声
scene: 铁水从炉口倒进锭模，冷却后表面暗红，锤子敲上去发出清硬的响声。The iron in this bridge was produced from ore smelted with charcoal.
sceneCN: 这里指铁这种金属（第 1 个义项：化学元素铁及其作为材料的形态）；句意为这座桥所用的铁，是由木炭熔炼的矿石炼成的。

熨烫（衣物）
铁的；铁制的；坚硬的、不可动摇的
