senses.title: The element
senses.titleCN: 铁：元素与材料
senses.definition: the hard grey metallic element that rusts in damp air and is the basis of steel
senses.definitionCN: 在湿空气中会生锈、作为钢之基础的坚硬灰色金属元素
senses.example: The iron in this bridge was produced from ore smelted with charcoal.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥所用的铁，是由木炭熔炼的矿石炼成的。
senses.why: Iron is named as a substance before it is named as anything made of it; the element is the anchor from which all the other senses hang.
senses.whyCN: 铁先作为一个物质被命名，然后才作为「用它做成的东西」被命名；元素义是所有其他义项挂靠的锚点。

senses.title: Ironware
senses.titleCN: 铁器：铁制工具与器物
senses.definition: tools and objects made of iron, taken together
senses.definitionCN: 铁制的工具与器物，作为一类看待
senses.example: The farm kept its irons in the shed by the yard.
senses.exampleCN: 农庄把铁器放在院子边的棚里。
senses.why: A material name stands for its products when the material is the point; a shed full of tools can be called simply by the metal.
senses.whyCN: 当重点在材料本身时，材料名就代替它的产品；一整棚工具可以直接用那种金属来称呼。

senses.title: The pressing tool
senses.titleCN: 熨斗：靠热与压平整衣物的器具
senses.definition: a small heated appliance with a flat sole, used to press cloth smooth
senses.definitionCN: 底部平坦、靠加热压平布料的器具
senses.example: The iron was still hot when she folded the shirt.
senses.exampleCN: 她折衬衫时，熨斗还很热。
senses.why: The first such tools were wedges of solid iron heated at a fire, so the object was literally a piece of iron; the material name survived the change to electric models.
senses.whyCN: 最早的熨具就是在火边加热的实心铁块，因此这个物件字面上就是「一块铁」；材料名在改成电熨斗之后仍然保留。

senses.title: The golf club
senses.titleCN: 铁杆：高尔夫球包里的一类球杆
senses.definition: a golf club with a metal head, distinguished from a wood
senses.definitionCN: 头部为金属的高尔夫球杆，与木杆相对
senses.example: He chose a five iron for the short approach.
senses.exampleCN: 短距离攻果岭时，他选了一支五号铁杆。
senses.why: Clubs were once classified by the material of the head, wood or iron; even after heads became steel, the old material names stayed as the category names.
senses.whyCN: 球杆曾按杆头材料分类，木或铁；即使杆头改用钢，旧的材料名仍留作类别名。

senses.title: To press cloth
senses.titleCN: 熨烫：用热与压使布面平整
senses.definition: to smooth cloth with a heated iron
senses.definitionCN: 用加热的熨斗把布料压平
senses.example: She ironed the collar before the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 面试前她把衣领熨平了。
senses.why: The tool's name turns into the action it performs, so a noun for a piece of metal becomes a verb for removing wrinkles.
senses.whyCN: 器具名转为它执行的动作：一个指铁块的名称，变成了去除褶皱的动词。

senses.title: Unyielding
senses.titleCN: 坚硬不可动摇：意志、纪律与掌控
senses.definition: used of will, discipline or control that cannot be bent
senses.definitionCN: 形容意志、纪律或掌控不可弯曲
senses.example: She ruled the department with an iron hand.
senses.exampleCN: 她以铁腕管理这个部门。
senses.why: Iron is hard and does not yield, so the material supplies a metaphor for any force that refuses to bend: will, grip, discipline.
senses.whyCN: 铁坚硬而不弯，因此这种材料为任何拒绝弯曲的力量提供比喻：意志、抓握、纪律。

senses.title: Of iron
senses.titleCN: 铁制的：标明材质
senses.definition: made of iron or belonging to the working of iron
senses.definitionCN: 用铁制成的，或属于铁加工范围的
senses.example: An iron gate closed the lane at night.
senses.exampleCN: 夜里一道铁门封住了小巷。
senses.why: The plainest adjectival use merely names the substance of a thing, and English allows it without any ending.
senses.whyCN: 最朴素的形容词用法只是说出某物的材质，而英语允许不加任何词尾就这样用。

senses.title: Iron in the body
senses.titleCN: 体内的铁：营养与医学中的铁
senses.definition: the mineral that the body needs to make red blood cells, taken through food or supplements
senses.definitionCN: 人体制造红细胞所需的矿物质，通过食物或补充剂摄入
senses.example: The doctor recommended an iron supplement after the test.
senses.exampleCN: 化验之后，医生建议补铁。
senses.why: The same element that makes tools also carries oxygen in blood, so a material word becomes a medical and dietary term with its own idioms.
senses.whyCN: 造工具的同一个元素也负责在血液中运送氧气，因此材料词成了医学与营养术语，并有了自己的说法。

intro.en: Iron is an old Germanic word whose deeper source is debated. The metal itself was known long before the word, so the record begins with the name, not with the material.
intro.cn: iron 是一个古老的日耳曼语词，更早的来源有争议。人类认识这种金属远早于这个词出现，因此可考的起点是名称，而不是材料。

items.en: Old English had isern and iren for the metal, with compound forms for ore, smith and blade. The word was already a common noun of daily craft, not a learned borrowing.
items.cn: 古英语用 isern 与 iren 指这种金属，并有指矿石、铁匠与刀剑的复合形式。这个词当时已是日常工艺中的普通名词，而非学术借词。

items.en: The word is reconstructed as a Germanic form represented by Old Norse jarn, Old Saxon isarn, Old High German isarn and Gothic eisarn. The reconstruction explains the family but not the family's own beginning.
items.cn: 这个词被重构为原始日耳曼语形式，同族有古诺斯语 jarn、古撒克逊语 isarn、古高地德语 isarn 与哥特语 eisarn。重构解释了族内关系，却不解释这一族自身的起点。

items.en: Many handbooks suggest the Germanic word was borrowed early from a Celtic form such as Old Irish iarn. The suggestion is widely repeated but not demonstrated, so it is presented here as a hypothesis.
items.cn: 许多工具书猜测这个日耳曼词早期借自凯尔特语形式，如古爱尔兰语 iarn。这一猜测被广泛重复，却未获证明，因此这里只作为假说列出。

items.en: A further suggestion links the Celtic word to an Indo-European term for blood, on the ground of iron's red oxide; this is a reconstruction and a conjecture, not an established etymology.
items.cn: 还有一种猜测把凯尔特词联系到某个表示「血」的印欧词，依据是铁的红褐色氧化物；这只是重构与推测，不是已确立的词源。

items.en: Middle English forms include iren and yren; the modern spelling iron and the silent r reflect later pronunciation, and the chemical symbol Fe comes from Latin ferrum, a different word.
items.cn: 中古英语形式有 iren、yren；现代拼写 iron 与不发音的 r 反映后来的读音，而化学符号 Fe 来自拉丁 ferrum，那是另一个词。

items.en: Source uncertain: no origin for the Germanic word is agreed, the Celtic borrowing is unproven, and every deeper Indo-European form proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个日耳曼词的来源没有共识，凯尔特语借词说未获证明，凡为它拟出的更深印欧形式都是重构。

note.en: Group one holds forms that look like iron but belong elsewhere; group two holds the metals and alloys it is usually set against.
note.cn: 第一组是形似 iron 却属别处的词；第二组是常与铁对照的金属与合金。

entries.definition: The expression of meaning by its opposite, from Greek eironeia 'dissimulation'. It shares letters with iron but not a root.
entries.definitionCN: 用反面表达本意的说法，来自希腊 eironeia「掩饰」。它与 iron 共享字母，却不共享词根。

entries.definition: The act of pressing cloth, or the clothes waiting to be pressed; a form of the same word, not another substance.
entries.definitionCN: 压平布料的行为，或待熨的衣物；是同一个词的形式，不是另一种物质。

entries.definition: Iron household goods as a class; it names the products rather than the metal.
entries.definitionCN: 作为一类的铁制家用器具；它命名产品，而不是金属。

entries.definition: A person or ship noted for toughness, literally 'iron side'; a compound, not a synonym for the metal.
entries.definitionCN: 以强硬著称的人或舰船，字面是「铁一般的侧面」；它是复合词，不是金属的同义词。

entries.definition: An alloy of iron with a small amount of carbon, harder and more elastic than plain iron.
entries.definitionCN: 铁与少量碳的合金，比纯铁更硬也更有弹性。

entries.definition: Containing or relating to iron, from Latin ferrum; it is the technical adjective for iron-bearing materials.
entries.definitionCN: 含铁的或与铁有关的，来自拉丁 ferrum；它是含铁材料的技术形容词。

entries.definition: Iron poured molten into a mould, hard and brittle; it is a form of iron, not a different metal.
entries.definitionCN: 把熔融铁浇入铸型所得，硬而脆；它是铁的一种形态，不是另一种金属。

entries.definition: The whole class of shiny, conductive elements; iron is one member of that class.
entries.definitionCN: 有光泽、可导电的一整类元素；铁只是其中一员。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the old Germanic name, the Latin symbol that does not match it, and the everyday objects called by the metal.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：古老的日耳曼名、与之不对应的拉丁符号，以及用金属名来称呼的日常物件。

normal.en: The chemical symbol Fe comes from Latin ferrum, so the symbol and the English word are from two different families.
normal.cn: 化学符号 Fe 来自拉丁 ferrum，因此符号与英语词来自两个不同的词族。

normal.en: The tool sense is literal history: the first pressing irons were solid pieces of the metal heated at a fire.
normal.cn: 器具义是字面历史：最早的熨具就是在火边加热的实心铁块。

normal.en: The metaphor is physical: iron does not bend, so an iron will and an iron grip are things that will not bend either.
normal.cn: 比喻是物理性的：铁不会弯，所以铁的意志与铁腕也是不会弯的东西。

normal.en: Golf keeps the old classification: woods and irons were named for the material of the head.
normal.cn: 高尔夫保留了旧分类：木杆与铁杆都按杆头材料命名。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the forge and the body: cast iron, wrought iron, iron ore, iron deficiency.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出炉与身体两面：铸铁、熟铁、铁矿石、缺铁。

abstract.en: Picture a single element pulled in two directions: into tools and into blood.
abstract.cn: 想象同一种元素被拉向两个方向：一边变成工具，一边进入血液。

abstract.en: Picture a hot wedge of metal sliding across cloth, leaving a flat bright path behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象一块烧热的金属在布面上滑过，身后留下一条平整发亮的痕迹。

abstract.en: Picture hardness as a material property that leaks into character words: will, grip, discipline, hand.
abstract.cn: 想象硬度作为一种材料性质，渗进了形容人的词里：意志、抓握、纪律、手腕。

examples.en: The old iron bridge was replaced but its piers were kept.
examples.cn: 那座旧铁桥被替换了，但桥墩保留了下来。

examples.en: He pressed the shirt with a heavy iron.
examples.cn: 他用一把沉甸甸的熨斗熨衬衫。

examples.en: Low iron in the blood can make a person tired.
examples.cn: 血液中缺铁会让人疲倦。

dict_mnemonic.text: iron＝铁；记「炉里出锭、火上熨衣、意志如铁」。

root: 古英语 īsern／īren「铁」，可重构为原始日耳曼语形式，同族有古诺斯语 jarn、哥特语 eisarn；更早来源不确定，凯尔特语借词说未获证明。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one element: the metal, its tools, the pressing iron, the golf iron, the act of pressing, the metaphor of hardness, the material as adjective, and iron in the body.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一种元素展开：金属本身、铁器、熨斗、铁杆、熨烫动作、坚硬的比喻、作定语的材质，以及体内的铁。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: molten iron fills a mould, cools to a dark red block, and rings hard under a hammer.
core.cn: 核心意象：铁水注入锭模，冷却成暗红铁块，在锤下发出硬响。

branches.en: THE ELEMENT: the substance itself, the anchor of every other sense.
branches.cn: 元素本身：物质层面的铁，是所有其他义项的锚点。

branches.en: THE THINGS MADE OF IT: ironware as a class, and the plain adjective of material.
branches.cn: 用它做成的东西：作为一类的铁器，以及朴素的材质形容词。

branches.en: THE DOMESTIC AND SPORTING TOOL: a pressing iron, a golf iron, and the verb of pressing.
branches.cn: 家用与运动器具：熨斗、铁杆，以及熨烫这个动词。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: hardness of metal becomes hardness of will and discipline.
branches.cn: 比喻层：金属的硬度变成意志与纪律的硬度。

branches.en: THE BODY: the same element becomes a nutrient and a medical word.
branches.cn: 身体层：同一种元素成为养分与医学词。

intro.en: Iron is a free morpheme that compounds very widely; its suffixes are the ordinary noun, agent and adjective endings.
intro.cn: iron 是能广泛构成复合词的自由语素；它接的后缀都是普通的名词、施事与形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin named iron with ferrum, a different word that gave English ferrous and ferric; it is the source of the chemical symbol but not a cognate of the English noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 ferrum 指铁，那是另一个词，英语的 ferrous 与 ferric 来自它；它是化学符号的来源，却不是英语名词的同源词。

items.structure: iron (n., adj., v.; Old English isern)
items.meaning: the metal, and to press cloth with it
items.meaningCN: 这种金属，以及用它熨布
items.example: They iron the linen on Mondays.
items.exampleCN: 他们每周一熨亚麻布。

items.meaning: the activity, or the clothes awaiting it
items.meaningCN: 这项活动，或待熨的衣物
items.example: The ironing is piled on the table.
items.exampleCN: 要熨的衣物堆在桌上。

items.meaning: one who irons; a pressing appliance
items.example: The ironer runs the last mangle.
items.exampleCN: 熨工操作最后一台压平机。

items.meaning: iron goods as a class
items.example: The stall sells ironware and tin.
items.exampleCN: 这个摊位卖铁器与马口铁。

items.meaning: iron parts, especially decorative building work
items.meaningCN: 铁制构件，尤指建筑铁饰
items.example: The gate's ironwork was made by hand.
items.exampleCN: 这道门的铁饰是手工做的。

items.meaning: a dealer in hardware and household iron goods
items.meaningCN: 经营五金与家用铁器的商人
items.example: The ironmonger sold nails by weight.
items.exampleCN: 五金商按重量卖钉子。

items.meaning: covered with iron; impossible to overturn
items.meaningCN: 铁甲包覆的；无法推翻的
items.example: They offered an ironclad guarantee.
items.exampleCN: 他们给出了无法推翻的保证。

items.meaning: not needing to be pressed after washing
items.example: He travels with non-iron shirts.
items.exampleCN: 他出差只带免熨衬衫。

items.meaning: iron shaped by pouring into a mould
items.example: The cover is cast iron.
items.exampleCN: 这个盖子是铸铁的。

definition_zh: 铁器时代：以铁器的使用为主要技术标志的考古时期，通常位于青铜时代之后；也指某一地区的这一阶段
definition_en: the archaeological period marked by the use of iron, usually following the Bronze Age, and the regional stage of that period
core_image: 展柜里锈迹斑斑的铁剑与犁头排成一列，说明牌只给出一段年代
scene: 展柜里锈迹斑斑的铁剑与犁头排成一列，旁边的说明牌只写着一个年代区间。The Iron Age is dated from the first widespread smelting of iron.
sceneCN: 这里指作为考古分期的铁器时代（第 1 个义项：以铁器为标志的时期名）；句意为铁器时代的起点，是以铁的普遍熔炼来断代的。

pos.zh: 铁器时代（专有名词，考古分期）
某一地区的铁器时代阶段
铁器时代的（作定语，常写作 Iron-Age 或 iron-age）

collocations.phrase: the end of the Iron Age

forms.label: 相关称法（无铁器阶段的地区）

derivatives.zh: iron（铁）+ age（时代）中的材料基础 → 金属本身；时代名由材料名加「时代」构成
iron age + 连字符作定语 → 铁器时代的，语义偏移为「属于该期风格或技术的」
小写连字符形式 → 铁器时代的（多见于英式行文）
iron age + man → 铁器时代的人，语义偏移为「该期人群的泛称」

senses.title: The named period
senses.titleCN: 时期名：以铁器为标志的阶段
senses.definition: the period of human culture marked by the use of iron, usually placed after the Bronze Age
senses.definitionCN: 以使用铁器为标志、通常排在青铜时代之后的人类文化时期
senses.example: The Iron Age is dated from the first widespread smelting of iron.
senses.exampleCN: 铁器时代的起点，是以铁的普遍熔炼来断代的。
senses.why: The name comes from a scheme that sorts societies by their dominant metal; iron is the material that follows bronze in that sequence.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字来自一种按主导金属给社会分期的方案；在这一序列里，铁是排在青铜之后的材料。

senses.title: A region's version
senses.titleCN: 地区性阶段：某一地区的铁器时代
senses.definition: the local stretch of time in which a particular region used iron as its main metal
senses.definitionCN: 某一地区以铁为主要金属的那一段本地时间
senses.example: The Iron Age in this region began with the first local smelting of iron.
senses.exampleCN: 这一地区的铁器时代，始于本地第一次炼铁。
senses.why: Iron reached different regions at different times and sometimes not at all, so the label is always tied to a place rather than to a single date.
senses.whyCN: 铁到达各地区的时间不同，有些地区甚至没有经历这一阶段，因此这个标签总是与地点绑定，而不是与单一日期绑定。

senses.title: The society of the period
senses.titleCN: 该期的社会与文化
senses.definition: the people, settlements and way of life of that period taken as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 作为整体来看的该时期人群、聚落与生活方式
senses.example: Iron Age society here was organised around fortified hilltops.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的铁器时代社会围绕设防的山顶组织起来。
senses.why: A period name can stand for the life inside it, especially when the new metal changed farming, warfare and trade together.
senses.whyCN: 时期名可以代替该时期内生活本身，尤其当这种新金属同时改变了农耕、战争与贸易时。

senses.title: The attributive use
senses.titleCN: 定语用法：铁器时代的器物与遗址
senses.definition: used before a noun to mark an object, site or practice as belonging to that period
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前，标明某器物、遗址或做法属于该时期
senses.example: Iron Age weapons were often repaired rather than replaced.
senses.exampleCN: 铁器时代的武器常常是修补而不是替换。
senses.why: English lets a period name modify a noun directly, so one phrase can turn a blade, a ditch or a farm into a dated thing.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许时期名直接修饰名词，于是一个短语就能把一把刀、一道沟或一处农庄变成有年代归属的东西。

senses.title: Iron after bronze
senses.titleCN: 在分期中的位置：铁取代青铜成为主材
senses.definition: the stage in the three-age system that follows the Bronze Age and precedes no further metal stage
senses.definitionCN: 三段体系中排在青铜时代之后、且不再有后续金属阶段的那一级
senses.example: Iron displaced bronze first for tools, later for weapons.
senses.exampleCN: 铁先在工具上取代青铜，之后才在武器上取代。
senses.why: The ladder ends here: iron ore is widespread and iron can be made harder than bronze, so the sequence has no fourth rung based on a common metal.
senses.whyCN: 阶梯到这里为止：铁矿分布广，铁又能做得比青铜更硬，因此这个序列没有以常见金属为基础的第四级。

senses.title: Early, middle and late
senses.titleCN: 早中晚三段：更细的分期
senses.definition: a subdivision of the period into early, middle and late phases, where the local sequence allows it
senses.definitionCN: 在本地序列允许时，把该时期细分为早期、中期与晚期
senses.example: The Late Iron Age saw larger and better-made iron bars.
senses.exampleCN: 铁器时代晚期出现了更大、更精良的铁条。
senses.why: A long period needs internal divisions to be usable, and the standard early, middle and late labels are added in front of the same name.
senses.whyCN: 一段长时期需要内部划分才好用，于是标准的早、中、晚标签被加在同一个名字前面。

senses.title: Evidence and dating
senses.titleCN: 证据与断代：凭什么判断这一时期
senses.definition: the material evidence, such as slag, furnace remains and iron objects, used to date and define the period
senses.definitionCN: 用来判定与界定该时期的有形证据，如炉渣、炉址与铁器
senses.example: Slag heaps and furnace bottoms are the best Iron Age evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 炉渣堆与炉底是判定铁器时代最好的证据。
senses.why: A period named after an industry is dated by that industry's waste: furnaces and slag survive when individual tools are reworked or rusted away.
senses.whyCN: 以某个行业命名的时期，要靠该行业的废弃物来断代：炉子与炉渣能留存，而单件工具往往被改锻或锈蚀殆尽。

senses.title: An old stage, in speech
senses.titleCN: 口语比喻：过时、老旧的阶段
senses.definition: used informally for an outdated stage of technology or practice
senses.definitionCN: 非正式用法，指技术或做法上已经过时的阶段
senses.example: Their ticketing belongs to the iron age of computing.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的售票系统还停留在计算机的铁器时代。
senses.why: Once a period name means 'early and superseded', it can be borrowed for anything old-fashioned; iron, though later than bronze, still sounds primitive next to modern materials.
senses.whyCN: 一旦时期名意味着「早期且已被取代」，它就能借来形容任何过时之物；铁虽晚于青铜，但与现代材料相比仍显得原始。

intro.en: The phrase joins an ancient Germanic metal name to a period word from Latin, and its modern sense belongs to the nineteenth-century classification of prehistory by materials.
intro.cn: 这个短语把古老的日耳曼金属名与来自拉丁的时期词接在一起，现代义属于十九世纪按材料划分史前的分类法。

items.en: Old English isern and iren named the metal. The deeper origin is debated: a early Celtic loan is often suggested but not proven, and every Indo-European form proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 古英语 isern 与 iren 指这种金属。更早来源有争议：常有人猜测是早期凯尔特语借词，但未获证明，凡为它拟出的印欧形式都是重构。

items.en: Age came through Old French from Latin aetas, meaning a lifetime or a span of time, before it was used for a division of history.
items.cn: age 经古法语来自拉丁 aetas，本义是一生或一段时间，之后才被用于历史分期。

items.en: Stone, Bronze and Iron were established as a sequence by Christian Jürgensen Thomsen in the 1830s, using the materials of museum finds as the sorting principle.
items.cn: 石、青铜、铁这一序列，由汤姆森在十九世纪三十年代确立，以博物馆藏品的材料作为分类原则。

items.en: English adopted Iron Age in the middle of the nineteenth century with the rest of the three-age vocabulary, first for European and Mediterranean sequences.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪中叶与三段分期的其余词汇一同采纳 Iron Age，最先用于欧洲与地中海的年代序列。

items.en: Twentieth-century archaeology added early, middle and late phases, recognised regions with no Iron Age at all, and let the phrase serve as an attributive label.
items.cn: 二十世纪考古学加入了早、中、晚三段，承认有些地区根本没有铁器时代，并让这个短语充当定语标签。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first English citation is not fixed, the origin of the metal word is unsettled, and the period's dates vary by centuries from region to region.
items.cn: 来源不确定：英语首见书证没有定论，金属词的来源未解决，而该时期年代在不同地区相差数百年。

note.en: Group one separates the phrase from its shorter forms and related labels; group two separates it from the other periods in the same scheme.
note.cn: 第一组把这个短语与它的短形式及相关标签分开；第二组把它与同一体系中的其他时期分开。

entries.definition: The metal itself. The phrase names a period; the bare noun names the substance and the objects made from it.
entries.definitionCN: 金属本身。这个短语命名一个时期，而单独的名词命名物质及其器物。

entries.definition: The same phrase with a hyphen when it stands before a noun; the hyphen marks its adjectival job.
entries.definitionCN: 同一短语在名词前作定语时加连字符；连字符标出它作形容词的角色。

entries.definition: A name for sharp social breakdown at the end of some regional Iron Ages; it is an episode, not the period.
entries.definitionCN: 指某些地区铁器时代末期社会急剧崩溃的说法；它是一个事件，而不是整个时期。

entries.definition: Iron with added carbon, harder and more elastic; steel is a product of iron, not a period name.
entries.definitionCN: 加入碳的铁，更硬更有弹性；钢是铁的产物，不是时期名。

entries.definition: The preceding period in the same three-age scheme, marked by bronze.
entries.definitionCN: 同一三段体系中更早的时期，以青铜为标志。

entries.definition: The earliest period in the same scheme, marked by stone tools.
entries.definitionCN: 同一体系中最早的时期，以石器为标志。

entries.definition: A transitional stage of copper working alongside stone, often inserted between the Stone and Bronze Ages.
entries.definitionCN: 铜与石器并用的过渡阶段，常被插在石器时代与青铜时代之间。

entries.definition: Any dated division of the past defined by material or culture; the Iron Age is one such division.
entries.definitionCN: 按材料或文化划定的任何有年代的过去片段；铁器时代只是其中一个划分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the metal name, its place in the ladder, and the real regional caveat.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：金属名、它在阶梯上的位置，以及真实的地区性例外。

normal.en: The phrase is self-explaining: iron + age, a stretch of time labelled by its dominant metal.
normal.cn: 这个短语自我解释：铁 + 时代，用主导金属给一段时间贴标签。

normal.en: The ladder ends with iron: stone, bronze, iron, and no fourth common metal.
normal.cn: 阶梯到铁为止：石、青铜、铁，没有第四种常见金属。

normal.en: Regional honesty matters: some regions have no Iron Age, and the dates shift by centuries.
normal.cn: 地区差异必须如实交代：有些地区没有铁器时代，年代相差数百年。

normal.en: The evidence words are slag, furnace and ore: waste and structures outlast the tools.
normal.cn: 证据词是炉渣、炉址与矿石：废弃物与结构比工具存留更久。

normal.en: The phrase is proper as a period name and hyphenated when it modifies a noun.
normal.cn: 作时期名时首字母大写；修饰名词时加连字符。

abstract.en: Picture a ladder whose top rung is the last one made of a common metal, with nothing above it but alloy steel.
abstract.cn: 想象一道阶梯，最高一级是最后一种常见金属做成的，上面再没有东西，只剩合金钢。

abstract.en: Picture a rusted blade beside a heap of slag: the tool decays, the waste remains.
abstract.cn: 想象一把锈刀旁堆着炉渣：工具烂掉了，废弃物却留下来。

abstract.en: Picture a label that must always carry a place name, because the same word covers centuries that do not line up.
abstract.cn: 想象一张标签必须总带一个地名，因为同一个词覆盖的世纪彼此对不齐。

examples.en: The Iron Age began at different dates in different parts of the continent.
examples.cn: 铁器时代在这块大陆的不同地区始于不同年代。

examples.en: Iron Age farmers used iron-tipped ploughs on heavier soils.
examples.cn: 铁器时代的农民在较重的土壤上使用带铁尖的犁。

examples.en: The fort was rebuilt several times during the Late Iron Age.
examples.cn: 这座堡垒在铁器时代晚期多次重建。

dict_mnemonic.text: iron（铁）+ age（时代）＝ 铁器时代；记「石—青铜—铁，铁是最后一级」。

root: iron 来自古英语 īsern／īren，更早来源不确定，凯尔特语借词说未获证明；age 经古法语来自拉丁 aetas「一生、时期」。两词合成，指以铁器为标志的考古时期。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses trace one label: the period, its regional versions, its society, its attributive use, its place after bronze, its subdivisions, its evidence, and its joking use for anything outdated.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一个标签展开：时期本身、地区版本、该期社会、定语用法、排在青铜之后的位置、内部细分、断代证据，以及用来调侃过时之物的用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rusted iron blades and plough tips in a case, beside a label that gives only a span of years.
core.cn: 核心意象：展柜里锈蚀的铁剑与犁尖，旁边标签只写着一个年代区间。

branches.en: THE LABEL: one name for the last metal stage of the three-part scheme.
branches.cn: 标签本身：三段体系中最后一个金属阶段的名称。

branches.en: THE LOCAL AND THE INTERNAL: one region's stretch of the period, and its early, middle and late phases.
branches.cn: 地方与内部：某一地区的那一段，以及它的早、中、晚三段。

branches.en: THE LIFE INSIDE: the label stands for farms, forts and the society that built them.
branches.cn: 期内生活：标签代替了农庄、堡垒以及建造它们的社会。

branches.en: THE MODIFIER: attached to weapons and settlements in the ordinary way, and borrowed in speech for anything outdated.
branches.cn: 修饰用法：正常地附着到武器与聚落上，也被口语借去形容过时之物。

branches.en: THE LADDER AND THE PROOF: the rung after bronze, held up by slag, furnace bottoms and dated iron.
branches.cn: 阶梯与证据：排在青铜之后的一级，由炉渣、炉底与可测年的铁器支撑。

intro.en: The phrase is a compound of two free words; the second carries the period sense, and a hyphen appears when the compound works as an adjective.
intro.cn: 这个短语是两个自由词构成的复合词；第二个词带时期义，作形容词时会加连字符。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the period word through aetas, but it has no cognate of the metal word; the Latin name for iron, ferrum, belongs to a different family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语通过 aetas 提供时期词，却没有与金属词同源的形式；拉丁语指铁的词 ferrum 属于另一个词族。

items.meaning: the metal
items.example: Iron replaced bronze for many tools.
items.exampleCN: 铁在许多工具上取代了青铜。

items.structure: age (n., from Old French, from Latin aetas)
items.meaning: a span of time; a historical stage
items.example: The age ended with the Roman conquest.
items.exampleCN: 这一时代随罗马征服而结束。

items.meaning: the period marked by iron
items.example: The Iron Age followed the Bronze Age.
items.exampleCN: 铁器时代紧接青铜时代。

items.meaning: belonging to that period
items.example: An Iron-Age ditch surrounds the site.
items.exampleCN: 一条铁器时代的壕沟围绕遗址。

items.meaning: the same attributive use in running text
items.meaningCN: 行文中的同一作定语用法
items.example: The iron-age layers are thin here.
items.exampleCN: 这里的铁器时代地层很薄。

items.meaning: the first phase of the period
items.example: Early Iron Age pottery copies bronze forms.
items.exampleCN: 铁器时代早期的陶器模仿青铜器形。

items.meaning: the final phase of the period
items.example: Late Iron Age coins appear in the ditch.
items.exampleCN: 壕沟里出现了铁器时代晚期的钱币。

items.meaning: a sharp social breakdown at the end of a regional Iron Age
items.meaningCN: 某地区铁器时代末期社会的急剧崩溃
items.example: The Iron Age collapse left the forts empty.
items.exampleCN: 铁器时代崩溃之后，堡垒空了。

latinEntries.meaning: life; age; a period of time

latinEntries.structure: ferrum, -i (n., second declension; not a cognate of the English noun)

definition_zh: 铜：一种紫红色金属元素；也指铜制品、铜色、小额铜币、镀铜动作，以及英式口语中的警察
definition_en: a reddish-brown metal, the element Cu, together with objects, colours, small coins and informal names derived from it
core_image: 新剖开的铜线断面露出亮红色，很快又蒙上一层暗褐
scene: 工人剥开一段旧电缆，新露出的铜芯还是亮红色，很快又蒙上一层暗褐。The copper in the wire was drawn from bars cast at the smelter.
sceneCN: 这里指铜这种金属（第 1 个义项：元素铜及其材料形态）；句意为电线里的铜，是由冶炼厂铸出的铜锭拉制而成的。

pos.zh: 铜（金属元素，不可数）
铜制品；铜器（总称）
铜色；红棕色
铜币；小额硬币（英式旧用法）
警察（英式口语，源自 cop）
镀铜；用铜包覆
铜制的；铜色的

collocations.zh: 包铜底的；引申为可靠的

derivatives.zh: copper + -y（形容词后缀）→ 铜色的，语义偏移为「带红棕色调的」
copper + plate（板）→ 铜版，语义偏移为「用于凹版印刷的铜板及其字体风格」
copper + smith（锻工）→ 铜匠，语义偏移为「专做铜器的手艺人」
copper + ware（器皿）→ 铜器，语义偏移为「成套铜制厨具与器皿」
copper + bottom + -ed → 包铜底的，语义偏移为「经得起检验、可靠的」
cupro-（铜）+ nickel（镍）→ 白铜，语义偏移为「铜镍合金，常用于铸币」

senses.title: The element
senses.titleCN: 铜：紫红色金属元素
senses.definition: a soft reddish-brown metal that conducts heat and electricity very well
senses.definitionCN: 一种偏软、红棕色、导热导电极好的金属
senses.example: The copper in the wire was drawn from bars cast at the smelter.
senses.exampleCN: 电线里的铜，是由冶炼厂铸出的铜锭拉制而成的。
senses.why: Copper is named as a substance first; its native occurrence and easy smelting made it one of the earliest metals people could use, which is why the word is ancient in every European language.
senses.whyCN: 铜先作为一个物质被命名；它能以天然形态出现、又容易熔炼，是最早被使用的金属之一，因此这个词在欧洲各语言中都很古老。

senses.title: Copper vessels
senses.titleCN: 铜器：铜制器具与容器
senses.definition: vessels, tools and fittings made of copper taken together
senses.definitionCN: 作为一类看待的铜制容器、工具与配件
senses.example: The kitchen still keeps its copper on the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 厨房仍把铜锅挂在墙上。
senses.why: A material that is easy to hammer into shape becomes a household word for the pots and bowls made from it.
senses.whyCN: 一种容易被锤打成形的材料，自然会变成指其锅碗器皿的日常词。

senses.title: The colour
senses.titleCN: 铜色：偏红的棕色调
senses.definition: the reddish-brown colour of the metal
senses.definitionCN: 这种金属的红棕色调
senses.example: Her hair had a deep copper shine in the sun.
senses.exampleCN: 阳光下她的头发泛着深铜色的光。
senses.why: The metal's colour is distinctive enough to serve as a colour name, especially for hair and autumn leaves.
senses.whyCN: 这种金属的颜色足够独特，可以直接充当颜色名，尤其用于头发与秋叶。

senses.title: The small coin
senses.titleCN: 铜币：小额硬币
senses.definition: a coin of low value, originally made of copper or bronze
senses.definitionCN: 面值很小的硬币，最初以铜或青铜铸造
senses.example: He counted the coppers in his pocket.
senses.exampleCN: 他数了数口袋里的铜币。
senses.why: Low-value coins were struck in the cheapest metal, so the metal's name became the name of small change in ordinary speech.
senses.whyCN: 低面值硬币用最便宜的金属铸造，于是这种金属名在口语中成了零钱的名称。

senses.title: The police officer
senses.titleCN: 警察：英式口语中的说法
senses.definition: a police officer, in British informal use
senses.definitionCN: 英式口语中的警察
senses.example: A copper stood at the corner of the street.
senses.exampleCN: 一名警察站在街角。
senses.why: This sense is not from the metal: it is generally traced to the verb cop 'to seize, catch', which shares the shape of the shorter word but not its origin.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项并非来自金属：一般认为它追溯到动词 cop「抓住、逮住」，与较短的词形相同而来源无关。

senses.title: To coat with copper
senses.titleCN: 镀铜：用铜包覆表面
senses.definition: to cover a surface with a thin layer of copper
senses.definitionCN: 在表面上覆一层薄薄的铜
senses.example: They copper the bottom of the pan before assembly.
senses.exampleCN: 装配前他们给锅底镀铜。
senses.why: A metal that can be deposited by electricity or by dipping gives a verb meaning to apply it, and the same verb serves cooking pans and ship hulls.
senses.whyCN: 一种可以靠电流或浸镀沉积的金属，自然产生「施加它」的动词，这个动词既用于锅底，也用于船壳。

senses.title: Copper as a commodity
senses.titleCN: 铜作为商品：行情与市场
senses.definition: the metal as a traded commodity with a price and a market
senses.definitionCN: 作为有价格与市场的交易商品来看的铜
senses.example: Copper prices rose after the mine strike.
senses.exampleCN: 铜矿罢工之后铜价上涨。
senses.why: Industrial demand makes the metal a financial object, so the bare noun appears in price reports without any article or qualifier.
senses.whyCN: 工业需求使这种金属成为金融标的，于是单独的名词会不带冠词或修饰语地出现在行情报道里。

senses.title: Copper-bottomed
senses.titleCN: 包铜底的：引申为可靠
senses.definition: used in the fixed phrase copper-bottomed to mean thoroughly reliable
senses.definitionCN: 用于固定短语「包铜底的」，引申为完全可靠、经得起检验
senses.example: The deal came with a copper-bottomed guarantee.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔交易附有一份可靠的保证。
senses.why: Ships were once sheathed in copper to keep worms out, so a copper bottom became proof against hidden failure, and the phrase moved from hulls to promises.
senses.whyCN: 船只曾用铜包底以防虫蛀，因此铜底成了防止暗中出问题的证明，这个说法便从船壳移到了承诺上。

intro.en: Copper has one of the clearest ancient etymologies in the metal vocabulary: it is named after the island that supplied it. A separate word of the same shape, for a police officer, has a different history.
intro.cn: copper 在金属词汇里属于古代词源最清楚的之一：它因供应这种金属的岛屿而得名。同形的另一个词，指警察，则有另一段历史。

items.en: Kypros is the Greek name of Cyprus, an island with celebrated copper mines. The island's name is older than the metal word and its own origin is not settled.
items.cn: Kypros 是塞浦路斯的希腊语名，这座岛以铜矿闻名。岛名比这个金属词更古老，其自身来源并无定论。

items.en: Latin called the metal aes cyprium, literally 'Cyprian metal', and the phrase was shortened to cyprium and then to cuprum; this route is generally accepted, not merely conjectured.
items.cn: 拉丁语把这种金属叫作 aes cyprium，字面是「塞浦路斯的金属」，短语先略作 cyprium，再缩成 cuprum；这条路径是公认的，不只是猜测。

items.en: Old English borrowed the Latin short form as coper and copor, alongside the native word for bronze; the modern spelling with double p appears later.
items.cn: 古英语从拉丁短形式借来 coper 与 copor，同时另有指青铜的本族词；带双 p 的现代拼写出现得更晚。

items.en: The coin sense follows the cheap metal used for small change, the colour sense follows the metal's hue, and the verb for coating follows the practice of sheathing hulls and pans.
items.cn: 硬币义跟随铸零钱所用的廉价金属，颜色义跟随金属的色调，镀覆动词则跟随包覆船壳与锅底的实践。

items.en: The police sense is a different word in origin, generally derived from the verb cop 'to seize', which itself has an uncertain source; the two words simply share a shape.
items.cn: 警察义在来源上是另一个词，一般认为出自动词 cop「抓住」，而后者本身来源不确定；两个词只是形态相同。

items.en: Source uncertain: the island name Kypros has no agreed etymology, the earliest English dates are approximate, and the slang word for a police officer is still debated.
items.cn: 来源不确定：岛名 Kypros 没有公认词源，最早的英语年代只是大致，指警察的俚语词来源也仍有争议。

note.en: Group one holds words that are easily mistaken for copper itself; group two holds the metals and values it is compared with.
note.cn: 第一组是容易被误当成 copper 本身的词；第二组是常与铜比较的金属与价值词。

entries.definition: A polished copper plate used for intaglio printing, and the style of writing modelled on it; it is a compound, not the metal.
entries.definitionCN: 用于凹版印刷的抛光铜板，以及模仿其笔迹的字体；它是复合词，不是金属本身。

entries.definition: A venomous North American snake with a copper-coloured head, and historically a political nickname; unrelated to the metal in sense.
entries.definitionCN: 一种头呈铜色的北美毒蛇，历史上也是政治绰号；在语义上与金属无关。

entries.definition: The shorter informal word for a police officer, and the verb 'to seize'; the police sense of copper is usually traced to this word.
entries.definitionCN: 指警察的更短的口语词，以及动词「抓住」；copper 的警察义通常追溯到这个词。

entries.definition: Having the colour or taste of copper; the -y ending marks a resemblance, not the substance.
entries.definitionCN: 具有铜的颜色或味道；-y 词尾标记相似，而不是物质本身。

entries.definition: An alloy of copper with tin, harder and more castable than pure copper.
entries.definitionCN: 铜与锡的合金，比纯铜更硬也更好铸。

entries.definition: An alloy of copper with zinc, yellower and easier to machine.
entries.definitionCN: 铜与锌的合金，更黄也更好切削。

entries.definition: A copper-nickel alloy used for coins and marine fittings; it is an alloy, not the element.
entries.definitionCN: 用于铸币与船用配件的铜镍合金；它是合金，不是元素。

entries.definition: A unit of small value; the coin was once copper, but the name is its own word.
entries.definitionCN: 一个小面值单位；这枚硬币曾是铜制的，但名称本身是另一个词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the island, the Latin phrase, the colour, and the separate slang word.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：那座岛、拉丁短语、颜色，以及另一个来源的俚语词。

normal.en: Cyprus gave the metal its Latin name: aes cyprium, Cyprian metal, shortened to cuprum.
normal.cn: 塞浦路斯给了这种金属拉丁名：aes cyprium（塞浦路斯的金属），再缩成 cuprum。

normal.en: The chemical symbol Cu comes from the same cuprum, so the symbol and the English word point to the same island.
normal.cn: 化学符号 Cu 来自同一个 cuprum，因此符号与英语词都指向同一座岛。

normal.en: The colour is real: fresh copper is bright red-brown and dulls quickly, which is why old copper looks brown or green.
normal.cn: 颜色是真的：新铜是亮红棕色，很快变暗，所以旧铜看起来偏褐或偏绿。

normal.en: The police sense is a shape coincidence: it belongs to cop, not to the metal.
normal.cn: 警察义只是形态巧合：它属于 cop，而不属于金属。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: copper wire, copper mine, copper alloy, copper-bottomed.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用途：铜线、铜矿、铜合金、包铜底的。

abstract.en: Picture an island whose hills are named after the red metal that ships carried away.
abstract.cn: 想象一座岛，它的山丘以那种被船只运走的红色金属命名。

abstract.en: Picture a fresh cut in a cable: bright red for a second, then brown as air reaches it.
abstract.cn: 想象电缆被剖开的一瞬：亮红只维持一秒，空气一到就转褐。

abstract.en: Picture a ship's hull sheathed in copper, the metal turned into armour against worms and doubt.
abstract.cn: 想象船壳包上铜皮，金属变成了抵御虫蛀与疑虑的铠甲。

examples.en: The roof was covered in copper that had weathered to green.
examples.cn: 屋顶覆着铜皮，已经风化成了绿色。

examples.en: A few coppers bought a loaf in those days.
examples.cn: 在那些年头，几枚铜币就能买一个面包。

examples.en: The alloy is mostly copper with a little tin.
examples.cn: 这种合金主要是铜，加了一点锡。

dict_mnemonic.text: copper＝铜；记「塞浦路斯出铜、新断面亮红、旧表面转褐」。

root: 拉丁 cuprum，来自 aes cyprium「塞浦路斯的金属」，再追溯至希腊 Kypros（塞浦路斯岛）；化学符号 Cu 同出此源。指警察的俚语义另出 cop，来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one red metal: the element, its vessels, its colour, its small coin, a slang officer from another word, the act of coating, a traded commodity, and a phrase for reliability.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一种红色金属展开：元素本身、铜器、颜色、小额铜币、来自另一个词的警察俚语、镀铜动作、作为商品，以及表示可靠的说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bright red cut edge of copper that darkens as air reaches it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一段亮红色的铜断面，在接触空气后逐渐变暗。

branches.en: THE ELEMENT: a soft, conductive metal that occurs native and melts easily.
branches.cn: 元素本身：一种偏软、可导电、能以天然形态出现且易熔的金属。

branches.en: THE OBJECTS: pots, bowls and fittings made by hammering the metal.
branches.cn: 器物层：靠锤打这种金属做出的锅、碗与配件。

branches.en: THE SURFACE: the red-brown colour, and the act of giving a surface that metal layer.
branches.cn: 表面层：红棕色调，以及给表面覆上金属层的动作。

branches.en: THE VALUE: the cheapest coin, and the metal priced by the tonne.
branches.cn: 价值层：最便宜的硬币，以及按吨计价的金属。

branches.en: THE TWO BORROWINGS: a slang officer from another word, and a copper bottom that promises reliability.
branches.cn: 两个借来之义：来自另一个词的警察俚语，以及许诺可靠的铜底。

intro.en: Copper is a free noun that compounds with craft words and takes the ordinary English endings for colour and material.
intro.cn: copper 是自由名词，能与工艺词构成复合词，并接表示颜色与材质的普通英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies cuprum and the fuller phrase aes cyprium; the island name behind both is Greek, so the whole family passes through Greek into Latin and then English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供 cuprum 与更完整的短语 aes cyprium；两者背后的岛名是希腊语，因此整个词族经希腊语到拉丁语，再到英语。

items.structure: copper (n., adj., v.; Old English coper, from Latin cuprum)
items.meaning: the metal, its colour, and to coat with it
items.meaningCN: 这种金属、它的颜色，以及给它镀层
items.example: They copper the inside of the mould.
items.exampleCN: 他们给模具内壁镀铜。

items.meaning: resembling copper in colour
items.example: The coin had a coppery tone.
items.exampleCN: 这枚硬币泛着铜色。

items.meaning: a copper printing plate
items.example: The map was printed from a copperplate.
items.exampleCN: 这幅地图是用铜版印的。

items.meaning: a worker in copper
items.example: The coppersmith hammered the bowl by hand.
items.exampleCN: 铜匠手工锤打出这只碗。

items.meaning: copper vessels as a class
items.example: The shop sells copperware and brass.
items.exampleCN: 这家店卖铜器与黄铜。

items.meaning: sheathed in copper; thoroughly reliable
items.example: The hull was copper-bottomed for the tropics.
items.exampleCN: 船壳为热带航行包了铜底。

items.meaning: copper, in alloy names
items.example: Cupronickel is used for coins.
items.exampleCN: 白铜被用于铸币。

items.meaning: nickel, in alloy names
items.example: The alloy pairs copper with nickel.
items.exampleCN: 这种合金把铜与镍配在一起。

items.meaning: a metal based on copper with other elements added
items.meaningCN: 以铜为主并加入其他元素的金属
items.example: Bronze is the best-known copper alloy.
items.exampleCN: 青铜是最有名的铜合金。

latinEntries.meaning: Cyprian; of the island of Cyprus
copper, bronze; the material of aes cyprium
latinEntries.meaningCN: 铜、青铜；aes cyprium 的材料成分

definition_zh: 铜加工；铜器制作：把铜及铜合金锤打、铸造、退火、连接并进行表面处理，制成器物与构件的手艺
definition_en: the craft of hammering, casting, annealing, joining and finishing copper and copper alloys into objects and parts
core_image: 一块烧红的铜片在砧上被锤子一下下敲成弧形，边缘泛出虹彩
scene: 铜片在炭火上烧红，取出后放在砧上，被锤子一下一下敲成弧形。Copperworking in this valley goes back to hand-hammered bowls made before any casting.
sceneCN: 这里指铜器制作这门手艺整体（第 1 个义项：以铜为材料的加工工艺总称）；句意为这个山谷的铜加工，可以追溯到早于铸造的手工锤打碗。

具体的铜器制作活动（可数，少见）

copperworking + -er（从事者）→ 铜工、铜器制作者

senses.title: The craft as a whole
senses.titleCN: 工艺总称：以铜为材料的加工手艺
senses.definition: the whole craft of turning copper and its alloys into vessels, tools and parts
senses.definitionCN: 把铜及其合金做成器皿、工具与构件的整套手艺
senses.example: Copperworking in this valley goes back to hand-hammered bowls made before any casting.
senses.exampleCN: 这个山谷的铜加工，可以追溯到早于铸造的手工锤打碗。
senses.why: Copper is soft enough to be shaped cold and tough enough to last, so one craft can cover both hammering and casting; the -ing form names that whole range as one activity.
senses.whyCN: 铜软到可以冷态成形，又韧到可以使用很久，因此同一门手艺能同时涵盖锤打与铸造；动名词形式把这一整段范围说成一项活动。

senses.title: Hammering into shape
senses.titleCN: 锤打成形：热锻与冷锻
senses.definition: forming copper by heating it and hammering it against an anvil or stake
senses.definitionCN: 加热后放在砧或桩上锤打成形的做法
senses.example: Hammering is the oldest branch of copperworking.
senses.exampleCN: 锤打是铜加工中最古老的一支。
senses.why: Native copper can be found already metallic, so the earliest workers could shape it without ever smelting; hammering therefore precedes casting in the record.
senses.whyCN: 天然铜可以直接以金属态获得，最早的工匠不必熔炼就能给它形状；因此在证据序列里，锤打早于铸造。

senses.title: Casting it
senses.titleCN: 铸造：把熔铜浇进范里
senses.definition: melting copper and pouring it into a mould to reproduce a shape
senses.definitionCN: 把铜熔化后浇入铸型，复制出某个形状
senses.example: Casting allowed copperworking to produce identical axe heads.
senses.exampleCN: 铸造使铜加工能够成批做出同样的斧头。
senses.why: A mould separates the shape from the hand: once the form is fixed in clay or stone, many copies can be made, which is why casting marks a change in scale.
senses.whyCN: 铸型把形状与手分开：一旦形状被固定在陶或石中，就能做出许多同样的件，因此铸造标志着规模上的变化。

senses.title: Softening and joining
senses.titleCN: 退火与连接：让铜重新变软并接合
senses.definition: heating copper to soften it after hammering, and joining pieces by heat or filler
senses.definitionCN: 锤打后加热使铜重新变软，并靠热或填料把部件接合
senses.example: Annealing is essential in copperworking because the metal hardens as it is hammered.
senses.exampleCN: 退火在铜加工中必不可少，因为铜在锤打中会变硬。
senses.why: Hammering hardens copper until it cracks, so the craft must repeatedly undo the hardening with heat; joining is the same principle applied between two pieces.
senses.whyCN: 锤打会把铜硬化到开裂，因此这门手艺必须反复用热来解除硬化；连接不过是把同一原理用在两块材料之间。

senses.title: Finishing the surface
senses.titleCN: 表面处理：打磨、着色与锈色控制
senses.definition: polishing copper and controlling the colour of its surface, including the green patina it develops outdoors
senses.definitionCN: 打磨铜面并控制其表面颜色，包括它在户外生成的绿锈
senses.example: Copperworking ends with polishing or with a deliberate green finish.
senses.exampleCN: 铜加工以打磨或刻意做出绿锈收尾。
senses.why: Copper changes colour on its own in air, so the craft must decide whether to keep it bright, let it brown, or force the green that architecture prizes.
senses.whyCN: 铜在空气中自己会变色，因此这门手艺必须决定：保持明亮、任其转褐，还是催出建筑所珍视的绿色。

senses.title: The workshop and its people
senses.titleCN: 作坊与工匠：进行铜加工的地方和人
senses.definition: the workshop where copper is worked, and the craftsmen who work it
senses.definitionCN: 进行铜加工的作坊，以及在那里干活的匠人
senses.example: The copperworking moved to the coast when the mine closed.
senses.exampleCN: 矿山关闭后，铜器制作迁到了海边。
senses.why: A craft and its place are named together because the tools, the hearth and the skill are all fixed in one room.
senses.whyCN: 手艺与场所被一起命名，因为工具、火塘与技艺都固定在同一间屋子里。

senses.title: What archaeology sees
senses.titleCN: 考古证据：坩埚、炉渣、铸范与工具
senses.definition: the traces of copper working that survive in the ground, used to reconstruct the craft
senses.definitionCN: 留在地层中的铜加工痕迹，用来重建这门手艺
senses.example: Crucibles and slag are the clearest signs of early copperworking.
senses.exampleCN: 坩埚与炉渣是早期铜加工最清楚的标志。
senses.why: Finished copper objects can be recycled, but crucibles, moulds and slag cannot easily be re-melted into something else, so the waste is the best witness.
senses.whyCN: 成品铜器可以被回收重熔，而坩埚、铸范与炉渣不容易变成别的东西，因此这些废弃物是最好的见证。

senses.title: The industry and its output
senses.titleCN: 产业与制品：铜加工工业及其产品
senses.definition: the commercial sector that works copper, and the goods it produces
senses.definitionCN: 以铜加工为业的商业部门，以及它产出的制品
senses.example: Modern copperworking supplies roofing, wiring and plumbing.
senses.exampleCN: 现代铜加工供应屋面、线缆与管道材料。
senses.why: Once workshops are counted together and their output is sold by weight, the craft becomes an industry and its name covers products as well as process.
senses.whyCN: 当作坊被合并计数、产出按重量出售，手艺就成了产业，它的名称也同时覆盖产品与过程。

intro.en: Copperworking is a modern compound of a metal name borrowed from Latin and the oldest English verb for doing; both halves are transparent, but only the metal half has a clear ancient source.
intro.cn: copperworking 是一个现代复合词：一半是从拉丁语借来的金属名，一半是英语最古老的「做」动词；两半都透明，但只有金属那一半有清楚的古代来源。

items.en: Cuprum came from aes cyprium, 'Cyprian metal', named after the island of Cyprus; this route is generally accepted and is confirmed by the chemical symbol Cu.
items.cn: cuprum 来自 aes cyprium「塞浦路斯的金属」，以塞浦路斯岛命名；这条路径是公认的，化学符号 Cu 可以为证。

items.en: Old English borrowed the Latin short form as coper and copor. The word arrived with the metal trade, not with learned writing.
items.cn: 古英语把拉丁短形式借作 coper 与 copor。这个词随金属贸易而来，而不是随学术写作而来。

items.en: Work goes back to Old English weorc 'deed, labour', with cognates across the Germanic languages; its deeper Indo-European ancestry is reconstructed rather than recorded.
items.cn: work 可追溯到古英语 weorc「行为、劳作」，在日耳曼诸语中有同族词；它更早的印欧来源属于重构，而非有记录的形式。

items.en: The compound copperworking belongs to industrial and archaeological writing of the modern period; copperwork is recorded earlier for the objects, and the -ing form grows with workshop vocabulary.
items.cn: copperworking 这一复合词属于现代工业与考古文献；copperwork 更早被记录，指铜制物件，而动名词形式随作坊词汇一同成长。

items.en: The craft itself is far older than the word: native copper was hammered into ornaments before any smelting, and casting followed once furnaces could reach the needed heat.
items.cn: 这门手艺本身远早于这个词：在任何熔炼之前，天然铜就被锤成饰件；等到炉子能达到所需温度，铸造才随之出现。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first use of the exact compound is not fixed, the island name behind cuprum has no agreed etymology, and the earliest workshop dates remain approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这一确切复合词的最早用例没有定论，cuprum 背后的岛名没有公认词源，最早的作坊年代也只是大致。

note.en: Group one separates the close family forms; group two separates working copper from working other metals or from the wider trade.
note.cn: 第一组把同族的近形词分开；第二组把铜加工与加工其他金属或更大的行当分开。

entries.definition: Worked copper as a class, or a single piece of it; the -ing form names the activity, the shorter form the output.
entries.definitionCN: 作为一类的加工铜件，或单件铜工件；动名词形式指活动，较短形式指产出。

entries.definition: Copper household vessels taken as a class; it names products rather than the craft that made them.
entries.definitionCN: 作为一类的家用铜器；它命名产品，而不是制造产品的工艺。

entries.definition: A polished copper plate for intaglio printing; it is one product of copperworking but belongs to printing.
entries.definitionCN: 凹版印刷用的抛光铜板；它是铜加工的产物之一，却属于印刷业。

entries.definition: The craftsman, marked by the -smith ending; it names a worker, not a process.
entries.definitionCN: 手艺人，以 -smith 词尾标记；它命名工人，而不是过程。

entries.definition: The general craft of shaping any metal; copperworking is its copper branch.
entries.definitionCN: 加工任何金属的总手艺；铜加工是它的铜分支。

entries.definition: The same operations applied to bronze, which is copper alloyed with tin and therefore harder to hammer cold.
entries.definitionCN: 把同样的操作用于青铜；青铜是铜锡合金，因此更难冷锻。

entries.definition: Working brass, a copper-zinc alloy that is more brittle when hot than pure copper.
entries.definitionCN: 加工黄铜；黄铜是铜锌合金，热态时比纯铜更脆。

entries.definition: Winning metal from ore; it supplies the copper that copperworking then shapes, but is a separate stage.
entries.definitionCN: 从矿石中提取金属；它为铜加工提供铜料，但属于另一个阶段。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the island source of the metal name, the native-metal beginning, and the real sequence of operations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：金属名的岛屿来源、天然铜的起点，以及真实的操作顺序。

normal.en: copper + working: the compound says what is done to the metal, with no learned suffix in between.
normal.cn: copper + working：这个复合词直接说出对金属做了什么，中间没有任何学术词尾。

normal.en: The craft order is hammer, anneal, hammer again, then cast if a furnace is hot enough.
normal.cn: 工艺顺序是：锤、退火、再锤，若炉温够高才铸造。

normal.en: Slag and crucibles are the archaeologist's favourite words here, because objects get recycled and waste does not.
normal.cn: 在考古里，炉渣与坩埚是关键词，因为器物会被回收，废弃物不会。

normal.en: The family is regular: copperwork for the output, copperworker for the person, copperware for the goods.
normal.cn: 同族形式很规整：copperwork 指产出，copperworker 指人，copperware 指货物。

normal.en: The colour change is part of the craft: bright copper can be left to brown or forced to green.
normal.cn: 变色也是手艺的一部分：亮铜可以任其转褐，也可以催成绿色。

abstract.en: Picture a hammer and a furnace taking turns: one shapes, the other undoes the hardness that shaping created.
abstract.cn: 想象锤子与炉子轮流上场：一个给形状，另一个解除给形状时造成的硬化。

abstract.en: Picture a bowl made before casting existed, its surface still showing the hammer marks.
abstract.cn: 想象一只在铸造出现之前做成的碗，表面仍留着锤痕。

abstract.en: Picture a green roof and a bright wire as two endings of the same metal's life in air.
abstract.cn: 想象绿色的屋顶与明亮的电线，是同一金属在空气中的两种结局。

examples.en: Copperworking traditions often pass the hammer from master to apprentice.
examples.cn: 铜器制作传统常把锤子从师傅传到徒弟手里。

examples.en: The site's copperworking waste dates to the earliest phase.
examples.cn: 这处遗址的铜加工废料属于最早的阶段。

examples.en: Modern copperworking has to control both hardness and colour.
examples.cn: 现代铜加工必须同时控制硬度与颜色。

dict_mnemonic.text: copper（铜）+ working（加工）＝ 铜器制作；记「烧红、锤打、退火、再锤、收尾上色」。

root: copper 来自拉丁 cuprum（源自 aes cyprium「塞浦路斯的金属」）；working 来自古英语 weorc「劳作」。两词合成，指把铜加工成器物的手艺。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the metal through the shop: the craft, hammering, casting, annealing and joining, finishing, the workshop, the archaeological trace, and the modern industry.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着铜走进作坊：工艺整体、锤打、铸造、退火与连接、表面处理、作坊与工匠、考古痕迹，以及现代产业。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red-hot copper sheet is hammered on an anvil until it curves, its edge showing rainbow oxides.
core.cn: 核心意象：烧红的铜片在砧上被锤成弧形，边缘泛出虹彩氧化物。

branches.en: THE CRAFT: hammering and casting treated as one continuous tradition.
branches.cn: 手艺整体：锤打与铸造被视为一条连续的传统。

branches.en: TWO ROUTES TO SHAPE: the hammer works the metal directly, the mould reproduces it.
branches.cn: 两条成形路线：锤子直接加工金属，铸型则复制形状。

branches.en: THE NECESSARY PAUSE: heat must undo the hardness that hammering creates, and also joins pieces.
branches.cn: 必要的停顿：热必须解除锤打造成的硬化，也负责把部件接上。

branches.en: THE SURFACE AND THE ROOM: colour control at the end, and the workshop where all of it happens.
branches.cn: 表面与房间：最后的颜色控制，以及这一切发生的作坊。

branches.en: THE TRACE AND THE TRADE: slag left in the ground, and a sector selling copper goods by weight.
branches.cn: 痕迹与行业：留在地层里的炉渣，以及按重量出售铜制品的产业。

intro.en: The compound joins a borrowed metal noun to a native verb; both halves take ordinary English endings and combine freely.
intro.cn: 这个复合词把借来的金属名词与本族动词接在一起；两半都接普通英语词尾，也能自由组合。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies cuprum from aes cyprium, and the island name behind it is Greek; Latin has no cognate of the English verb work, which is native.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语从 aes cyprium 提供 cuprum，其背后的岛名是希腊语；拉丁语没有与英语动词 work 同源的形式，后者是本族词。

definition_zh: 合金：把一种金属与另一种金属或非金属熔合而成的材料；也指掺混、降低成色以及由此引申的混合体
definition_en: a metal made by melting and mixing two or more elements, and the act of mixing metals or of debasing one by adding another
core_image: 熔炉里两种金属液汇合，颜色由亮红转为银白，冷却后的断面均匀一致
scene: 坩埚里铜液与锡液汇合，颜色由亮红转向银白，冷却后的断面看不出两种金属。An alloy of copper and tin is harder than either metal alone.
sceneCN: 这里指合金这种材料（第 1 个义项：两种以上元素熔合而成的金属材料）；句意为铜与锡的合金，比其中任何一种金属都硬。

pos.zh: 合金（材料，可数或不可数）
掺混物；降低成色的成分（常用于比喻）
熔合（金属）；掺杂使降低成色

collocations.phrase: an alloy of copper and tin

derivatives.zh: alloy + -ed（分词形容词）→ 已成合金的，语义偏移为「掺了其他成分而不再纯净的」
alloy + -ing（动名词）→ 合金化，语义偏移为「向金属中有意加入元素的工序」
super-（超）+ alloy → 高温合金，语义偏移为「能在极端温度下保持强度的合金」
non-（非）+ alloy → 非合金的，语义偏移为「未加合金元素的纯金属」
alloy + steel（钢）→ 合金钢，语义偏移为「加入铬、镍等元素的钢」

senses.title: The material
senses.titleCN: 合金：熔合而成的金属材料
senses.definition: a metal produced by melting and mixing two or more elements so that they form one material
senses.definitionCN: 把两种以上元素熔合、混合成一种材料的金属
senses.example: An alloy of copper and tin is harder than either metal alone.
senses.exampleCN: 铜与锡的合金，比其中任何一种金属都硬。
senses.why: Melting lets different metals dissolve into one another; when the melt solidifies, the mixture behaves as a single material, which is why the result gets its own name.
senses.whyCN: 熔炼让不同金属彼此溶解；熔体凝固后，混合物作为一个整体表现，因此产物得到了自己的名称。

senses.title: One recipe
senses.titleCN: 一种配比：特定成分的合金
senses.definition: a particular combination of metals with a stated proportion
senses.definitionCN: 按一定比例配成的特定金属组合
senses.example: The bell is cast from an alloy with about a fifth tin.
senses.exampleCN: 这口钟用一种含锡约五分之一的合金铸成。
senses.why: Once the class exists, each recipe counts as one alloy, because proportions change hardness, colour and sound.
senses.whyCN: 类别义一旦成立，每一种配方就算一种合金，因为比例会改变硬度、颜色与声音。

senses.title: A debasing mixture
senses.titleCN: 掺杂降质：混入物与不纯
senses.definition: something mixed in that lowers the purity or value of a metal, and by extension any unwanted addition
senses.definitionCN: 混入后降低金属纯度或价值的东西，引申为任何不需要的掺杂
senses.example: The gold was accepted without alloy.
senses.exampleCN: 这批黄金被认定毫无掺杂。
senses.why: Adding a cheaper metal to a precious one was a way of cheating weight and value, so the word also carries the sense of a loss of purity.
senses.whyCN: 在贵金属里掺入便宜金属，是偷重量、偷成色的手段，因此这个词也带有「纯净度受损」的含义。

senses.title: To fuse metals
senses.titleCN: 动词：把金属熔合在一起
senses.definition: to melt two or more metals together into one material
senses.definitionCN: 把两种以上金属熔成一种材料
senses.example: They alloy the copper with a little beryllium.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在铜里加入少量铍，熔成合金。
senses.why: The noun's process sense turns into a verb, naming the deliberate act of combining melts rather than the result.
senses.whyCN: 名词的过程义转为动词，命名的是有意把熔体合并的动作，而不是结果。

senses.title: To debase
senses.titleCN: 动词：掺杂使降低成色
senses.definition: to lower the quality of a metal by adding a cheaper one
senses.definitionCN: 加入较便宜的金属以降低成色
senses.example: The mint alloyed the silver to stretch the supply.
senses.exampleCN: 铸币厂在银里掺料，以拉长供应。
senses.why: The same verb covers honest metallurgy and dishonest coinage; context decides whether the mixing is a recipe or a fraud.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动词既指正当的冶金，也指不正当的铸币；语境决定这种混合是配方还是欺诈。

senses.title: The coinage sense
senses.titleCN: 货币成色：铸币中的合金比例
senses.definition: the proportion of base metal in a coin, as a historical standard of value
senses.definitionCN: 硬币中贱金属所占的比例，历史上作为价值标准
senses.example: The alloy of the coin was fixed by royal decree.
senses.exampleCN: 这种硬币的成色由王室法令规定。
senses.why: Coins were valued by their precious metal content, so the mixing ratio became a matter of law rather than of workshop choice.
senses.whyCN: 硬币的价值取决于贵金属含量，因此配比成了法律问题，而不是作坊选择。

senses.title: The attributive use
senses.titleCN: 定语：合金制的、含合金的
senses.definition: used before a noun to mark an object or material as made of or containing an alloy
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前，标明某物由合金制成或含有合金
senses.example: Alloy wheels are lighter than steel ones.
senses.exampleCN: 合金轮毂比钢制的轻。
senses.why: A material noun can modify another noun directly, so the same word labels wheels, steel and frames without any ending.
senses.whyCN: 材料名词可以直接修饰另一名词，因此同一个词不加词尾就能标记轮毂、钢与车架。

senses.title: A mixture of anything
senses.titleCN: 比喻：由不同成分构成的混合体
senses.definition: a figurative mixture of different qualities, styles or feelings
senses.definitionCN: 比喻义：不同性质、风格或情感构成的混合
senses.example: Her optimism was an alloy of memory and stubbornness.
senses.exampleCN: 她的乐观是记忆与固执的混合体。
senses.why: If a metal can be improved or debased by mixing, then a character or a style can be described as a mixture in the same way, with the same hint of impurity.
senses.whyCN: 既然金属能靠混合而改良或降质，那么性格或风格也可以用同样的方式描述为混合物，并带有同样一丝「不纯」的暗示。

intro.en: Alloy comes from a Latin verb meaning 'to bind to'. The metallurgical sense is the older one; the figurative sense of a mixed or debased thing grows out of it.
intro.cn: alloy 来自一个意为「绑到……上」的拉丁动词。冶金义是较早的一层，混合或降质的比喻义由它生长出来。

items.en: Alligare combined ad- 'to' with ligare 'to bind', and meant to tie or attach something to something else. This derivation is generally accepted and is reflected in the modern spelling.
items.cn: alligare 由 ad-「向」与 ligare「绑」组合而成，意为把某物系到另一物上。这一派生是公认的，并在现代拼写中留下痕迹。

items.en: Old French aloier took the Latin verb and used it for combining metals; the noun aloi named the resulting mixture and passed into English as alloy.
items.cn: 古法语 aloier 承袭这个拉丁动词，并用它指把金属合在一起；名词 aloi 指所得的混合物，进入英语后成为 alloy。

items.en: The noun is recorded in English from the sixteenth century, first in the language of mints and metal trades, where combining and debasing were practical everyday matters.
items.cn: 这个名词自十六世纪起见于英语，最早出现在铸币与金属行业的话语里，在那里合料与降质是日常实务。

items.en: Because adding a base metal lowers value, the word acquired the sense of an unwanted element mixed into anything, which produced the phrase 'without alloy' for something pure.
items.cn: 因为掺入贱金属会降低价值，这个词获得了「混入任何东西里的不想要成分」之义，并产生「毫无掺杂」这一表示纯净的说法。

items.en: Modern metallurgy uses alloy for any deliberate multi-element metal and for the corresponding verb, and the attributive form labels products such as alloy steel and alloy wheels.
items.cn: 现代冶金用 alloy 指任何有意配成的多元素金属，也指相应的动词；定语形式则标记合金钢、合金轮毂一类产品。

items.en: Dating and sense shift: the exact first English citation is not fixed, and the sense development from 'binding' to 'mixing metals' happened inside French rather than in Latin.
items.cn: 年代与语义转移：确切的英语首见书证没有定论，而从「绑定」到「混合金属」的语义发展发生在法语内部，不在拉丁语中。

note.en: Group one holds words whose shapes invite confusion; group two holds the real neighbouring materials and processes.
note.cn: 第一组是形态上容易混淆的词；第二组是真正相邻的材料与工艺。

entries.definition: To reduce fear or pain, from Old English alecgan 'to lay down'; it sounds like alloy but has a native origin.
entries.definitionCN: 减轻恐惧或疼痛，来自古英语 alecgan「放下」；它读起来像 alloy，但来源是本族的。

entries.definition: A narrow passage between buildings, from Old French alee 'a going'; the ending differs and the sense is unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑物之间的窄通道，来自古法语 alee「行走」；词尾不同，意义也无关。

entries.definition: A state or person joined to another by agreement, from Latin alligare through French; it shares the root 'to bind' but means a partner, not a material.
entries.definitionCN: 通过协议与他方联合的国家或个人，经法语来自拉丁 alligare；它与 alloy 共享「绑」的词根，但指的是伙伴，不是材料。

entries.definition: Made into an alloy, or mixed with something less pure; a form of the same word, not a separate metal.
entries.definitionCN: 被做成合金的，或掺了较不纯成分的；是同一个词的形式，不是另一种金属。

entries.definition: An alloy in which mercury is the main component, and by extension any blend; it is a special kind of alloy, not a general synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 以汞为主要成分的合金，引申为任何混合物；它是合金的一个特殊种类，不是一般同义词。

entries.definition: A specific copper-tin alloy; alloy is the general class to which bronze belongs.
entries.definitionCN: 特指铜锡合金；alloy 是 bronze 所属的总类。

entries.definition: A material made of distinct components that remain separate, such as fibres in resin; an alloy is chemically mixed, a composite is not.
entries.definitionCN: 由仍保持分离的组分构成的材料，如树脂中的纤维；合金是化学意义上的混合，复合材料不是。

entries.definition: Any mixture, often of things that stay distinguishable; an alloy specifically involves molten metals.
entries.definitionCN: 任何混合物，通常其中成分仍可分辨；合金则专指熔融金属的混合。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin verb 'to bind', the mint's practical sense, and the real alloy names.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁动词「绑」、铸币厂的实务义，以及真实存在的合金名称。

normal.en: The root is 'to bind': ad- plus ligare, so an alloy is metals tied together rather than merely stirred.
normal.cn: 词根是「绑」：ad- 加 ligare，因此合金是被绑在一起的金属，而不只是被搅在一起。

normal.en: The same root gives ally: an ally is bound to you by agreement, an alloy is bound into one material.
normal.cn: 同一词根也给出 ally：盟友靠协议与你绑定，合金则被绑成一种材料。

normal.en: The dishonest sense is old: mints alloyed silver to make more coins from the same weight.
normal.cn: 不诚实的义项很古老：铸币厂在银里掺料，用同样的重量造出更多硬币。

normal.en: The real named alloys are bronze and brass, copper with tin and copper with zinc.
normal.cn: 真实有专名的合金是青铜与黄铜：铜加锡、铜加锌。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the class and the purity: alloy steel, alloy wheel, without alloy.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出类别与纯度：合金钢、合金轮毂、毫无掺杂。

abstract.en: Picture two melts meeting in one crucible and coming out as a single colour that neither had before.
abstract.cn: 想象两种熔体在同一只坩埚里相遇，出来时是一种两者原本都没有的颜色。

abstract.en: Picture a coin whose value is written into its recipe, so the workshop becomes a courtroom.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚硬币的价值被写进它的配方，于是作坊变成了法庭。

abstract.en: Picture a character described as a mixture: the same word that debases metal now debases a feeling.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人的性格被描述为混合物：同一个曾用来降低金属成色的词，如今在降低一种情感的纯度。

examples.en: The frame is made of a light alloy that resists corrosion.
examples.cn: 这个车架由一种耐腐蚀的轻合金制成。

examples.en: Their joy was real but not without alloy.
examples.cn: 他们的快乐是真的，但并非毫无掺杂。

examples.en: The smith alloyed the copper with tin until the colour matched.
examples.cn: 铁匠在铜里加锡，直到颜色对得上。

dict_mnemonic.text: alloy＝合金；记「ad 向 + ligare 绑，把两种金属绑成一种」。

root: 拉丁 alligare「绑到……上」（ad- + ligare「绑」），经古法语 aloier、aloi 进入英语；由「合料」引申出合金、掺杂与混合体诸义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one binding: the material, one recipe of it, a debasing addition, the verb of fusing, the verb of debasing, coinage standard, the attributive label, and a mixture of anything.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着「绑合」这一动作展开：材料本身、一种配比、降低成色的掺入、熔合的动词、降质的动词、铸币成色、定语标签，以及任何事物的混合体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two molten metals meet in a crucible and solidify as one uniform block.
core.cn: 核心意象：两种熔融金属在坩埚中相遇，凝固成一块均匀的整体。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL: mixing by melting produces something that behaves as one metal.
branches.cn: 材料本身：熔融混合产生的材料，表现得像一种金属。

branches.en: THE RECIPE: each set of proportions is a countable alloy with its own properties.
branches.cn: 配比层：每一组成分比例都是可数的一种合金，各有自己的性能。

branches.en: THE LOSS OF PURITY: adding a cheaper metal debases value, and in coinage the ratio becomes law.
branches.cn: 纯净度的损失：掺入便宜金属会降低价值，在铸币中配比还成了法律。

branches.en: THE ACT: the verb names the deliberate combining of melts.
branches.cn: 动作层：动词命名有意把熔体合并的行为。

branches.en: THE EXTENSIONS: a material used as a modifier, and any mixture of qualities in a person or style.
branches.cn: 延伸层：作修饰语的材料，以及人或风格中任何性质的混合。

intro.en: Alloy is a borrowed noun and verb; its endings are ordinary English, and it compounds with material words such as steel and wheel.
intro.cn: alloy 是借来的名词兼动词；它接的词尾都是普通英语词尾，也能与 steel、wheel 这类材料或物件词构成复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin alligare, from ad- and ligare, is the source; the related noun alligatio meant a binding, and the same root reached English again through ally.
latinIntro.cn: 来源是拉丁 alligare，由 ad- 与 ligare 构成；相关名词 alligatio 意为绑缚，同一词根又经 ally 再次进入英语。

items.structure: alloy (n., v.; from Old French aloi, from Latin alligare)
items.meaning: a mixed metal, and to mix metals
items.meaningCN: 混合而成的金属，以及混合金属
items.example: They alloy the melt before casting.
items.exampleCN: 他们在浇铸前对熔体做合金化处理。

items.meaning: made into or containing an alloy
items.meaningCN: 已成合金的或含合金的
items.example: The alloyed surface resists wear.
items.exampleCN: 合金化的表面更耐磨。

items.meaning: the process of adding elements to a metal
items.meaningCN: 向金属中加入元素的过程
items.example: Alloying changes both strength and colour.
items.exampleCN: 合金化同时改变强度与颜色。

items.meaning: steel with added elements such as chromium
items.example: The frame uses alloy steel.
items.exampleCN: 这个框架使用合金钢。

items.meaning: an alloy that keeps its strength at extreme heat
items.meaningCN: 在极端高温下仍保持强度的合金
items.example: Turbine blades are made from a superalloy.
items.exampleCN: 涡轮叶片由高温合金制成。

items.meaning: a wheel cast from a light alloy
items.example: The car came with alloy wheels.
items.exampleCN: 这辆车配了合金轮毂。

items.meaning: the removal of one element from an alloy
items.meaningCN: 从合金中去除某一元素的过程
items.example: Dealloying can make a bronze brittle.
items.exampleCN: 脱合金会使青铜变脆。

items.meaning: metal without added alloying elements
items.example: Non-alloy steel is cheaper but softer.
items.exampleCN: 非合金钢更便宜但更软。

definition_zh: 合金化：把一种或多种元素加入金属熔体，以改变其强度、耐蚀性、导电性等性能的工艺
definition_en: the process of adding one or more elements to a metal so as to change its strength, corrosion resistance or other properties
core_image: 炉前工人用长钳夹起一小块银亮金属，压入翻涌的铜液，成分记录随之改写
scene: 炉前工人用长钳夹起一小块银亮金属，压入翻涌的铜液，成分记录随之改写。Alloying raises the strength of aluminium without making it much heavier.
sceneCN: 这里指合金化这一工艺（第 1 个义项：向金属中加入元素以改变性能的过程）；句意为合金化提高了铝的强度，却没有让它重太多。

pos.zh: 合金化（工艺或过程，不可数）
一次合金化操作（可数，少见）

collocations.zh: 合金添加（加入的元素量）

senses.title: The process
senses.titleCN: 合金化：向金属中加入元素的工序
senses.definition: the deliberate addition of elements to a metal in order to change its properties
senses.definitionCN: 有意向金属中加入元素以改变其性能的做法
senses.example: Alloying raises the strength of aluminium without making it much heavier.
senses.exampleCN: 合金化提高了铝的强度，却没有让它重太多。
senses.why: The verb alloy means to combine metals; the -ing form names the ongoing technical operation, with the emphasis on the act of adding rather than on the resulting material.
senses.whyCN: 动词 alloy 意为把金属合在一起；动名词形式命名正在进行的技术作业，重点在「加入」这个动作，而不是所得的合金。

senses.title: One heat, one addition
senses.titleCN: 一次操作：某一炉的合金化作业
senses.definition: a single act of adding elements to a particular melt
senses.definitionCN: 对某一炉熔体进行的一次元素加入
senses.example: The alloying of this heat took twenty minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 这一炉的合金化用了二十分钟。
senses.why: A countable use appears when the process is tied to one furnace charge, because each heat has its own timing and its own record.
senses.whyCN: 当过程与某一炉炉料绑定时，就会出现可数用法，因为每一炉都有自己的时间与记录。

senses.title: The element's role
senses.titleCN: 合金元素的作用：少量加入、明显改变
senses.definition: the function of an element added in small amounts to control a property
senses.definitionCN: 以少量加入、用来控制某项性能的元素所起的作用
senses.example: Chromium is the alloying element that makes stainless steel resist rust.
senses.exampleCN: 铬是那种让不锈钢抗锈的合金元素。
senses.why: A small addition can change a large property, so the added element is treated as an agent with a job rather than as a filler.
senses.whyCN: 少量加入就能改变很大的性能，因此被加入的元素被看作承担任务的角色，而不是填充物。

senses.title: How it works inside
senses.titleCN: 冶金机理：固溶、析出与晶粒控制
senses.definition: the mechanisms by which added elements enter the solid metal, such as solid solution, precipitation and grain refinement
senses.definitionCN: 加入的元素进入固态金属的机制，如固溶、析出与晶粒细化
senses.example: Solid-solution alloying distorts the lattice and blocks dislocation motion.
senses.exampleCN: 固溶合金化使晶格畸变，从而阻碍位错运动。
senses.why: An added atom does not disappear: it either fits into the lattice or forms its own particles, and either way it interferes with the movement that lets metals deform.
senses.whyCN: 加入的原子不会消失：它要么嵌进晶格，要么形成自己的颗粒；两种方式都会干扰金属变形所依赖的运动。

senses.title: Designing the recipe
senses.titleCN: 配比设计：成分与加入量的确定
senses.definition: choosing which elements to add and in what amounts for a target property
senses.definitionCN: 为达成某项目标性能而选择加入哪些元素、各加多少
senses.example: Alloying for marine service means balancing chromium against cost.
senses.exampleCN: 为海洋环境做合金化，意味着在铬含量与成本之间取平衡。
senses.why: Every addition buys one property and pays for it in another, so the craft becomes a trade-off rather than a simple strengthening step.
senses.whyCN: 每一种加入都换来一项性能，同时又在另一项上付出代价，因此这门手艺成了权衡，而不是简单的强化步骤。

senses.title: The property changed
senses.titleCN: 性能后果：强度、耐蚀与导电的变化
senses.definition: the resulting change in strength, hardness, corrosion resistance or conductivity
senses.definitionCN: 由此产生的强度、硬度、耐蚀性或导电性的变化
senses.example: Alloying improves corrosion resistance but lowers conductivity.
senses.exampleCN: 合金化提高耐蚀性，却降低了导电性。
senses.why: The point of the operation is a measurable difference, so the word often appears where results are compared rather than where metals are described.
senses.whyCN: 这道工序的目的就是一种可测量的差别，因此这个词常出现在比较结果的地方，而不是描述金属的地方。

senses.title: In the plant
senses.titleCN: 工业实践：炼钢与铝合金车间里的合金化
senses.definition: the industrial practice of alloying in steelmaking and light-metal plants
senses.definitionCN: 炼钢与轻金属工厂中实际的合金化作业
senses.example: Alloying is done in the ladle, just before the steel is cast.
senses.exampleCN: 合金化在钢包中进行，就在浇铸之前。
senses.why: Timing is part of the craft: adding an element too early lets it burn away, so the operation is placed at a precise point in the plant's sequence.
senses.whyCN: 时机本身就是手艺的一部分：加得太早元素会被烧掉，因此这道操作被安排在工厂流程中的一个精确位置。

senses.title: A metaphor of blending
senses.titleCN: 比喻：把不同成分融为一体的过程
senses.definition: a figurative process of combining different elements into one whole
senses.definitionCN: 比喻义：把不同成分融合成一个整体的过程
senses.example: The alloying of two traditions produced a style that belonged to neither.
senses.exampleCN: 两种传统的融合，产生了一种不属于任何一方的风格。
senses.why: When metals are alloyed, each loses its separate identity while changing the whole; the same image describes cultures, styles and ideas that merge.
senses.whyCN: 金属合金化时，各自失去独立身份却改变了整体；同一个意象可以描述融合的文化、风格与观念。

intro.en: Alloying is the verbal noun of alloy, a word whose root means 'to bind'. Its form is modern, but the operation it names is as old as the first deliberately mixed melt.
intro.cn: alloying 是 alloy 的动名词，而 alloy 的词根意为「绑」。它的形态是现代形成的，但它命名的操作，与人类第一次有意配制的熔体一样古老。

items.en: Alligare, from ad- 'to' and ligare 'to bind', meant to tie one thing to another. The derivation is generally accepted and explains both alloy and ally.
items.cn: alligare 由 ad-「向」与 ligare「绑」构成，意为把一物系到另一物上。这一派生是公认的，也同时解释了 alloy 与 ally。

items.en: Old French aloier applied the Latin verb to the combining of metals, and the noun aloi passed into English, where the verb alloy followed.
items.cn: 古法语 aloier 把这个拉丁动词用于金属的合并，名词 aloi 进入英语，动词 alloy 随后出现。

items.en: The noun is recorded in English from the sixteenth century and the verb a little later. The -ing form is the ordinary verbal noun that English builds from any verb.
items.cn: 名词自十六世纪见于英语，动词稍晚出现。动名词形式是英语从任何动词都能构成的常规名词。

items.en: The technical sense narrows to the deliberate addition of elements to a melt, as distinct from the simple mixing of scrap or the accidental contamination of a charge.
items.cn: 技术义收窄为有意向熔体中加入元素，以区别于废料的简单混合或炉料的意外污染。

items.en: Twentieth-century steelmaking and light-metal production turned alloying into a measured step with its own ladle timing, its own addition agents and its own quality records.
items.cn: 二十世纪的炼钢与轻金属生产，把合金化变成一个有计量、有钢包时机、有添加介质、有质量记录的工序。

items.en: Dating and usage: the earliest English dates are approximate, and the shift from 'binding' to 'adding an element' happened through trade usage rather than by any recorded decision.
items.cn: 年代与行业用法：最早的英语年代只是大致，而从「绑合」到「加入元素」的转变是经由行业用法发生的，并无任何有记录的约定。

note.en: Group one separates the close forms of the same family; group two separates alloying from other ways of changing a metal.
note.cn: 第一组把同族的近形形式分开；第二组把合金化与改变金属的其他方式分开。

entries.definition: The substance itself, or the verb of mixing; alloying names the ongoing operation.
entries.definitionCN: 物质本身，或混合的动词；alloying 命名正在进行的操作。

entries.definition: The state after the operation; alloying is the act, alloyed is the metal that has undergone it.
entries.definitionCN: 操作之后的状态；alloying 是动作，alloyed 是经历了该动作的金属。

entries.definition: The element added, not the process of adding it; the phrase names a role inside the operation.
entries.definitionCN: 被加入的元素，而不是加入它的过程；这个短语命名操作中的一个角色。

entries.definition: Steel that has been alloyed; it is the output of alloying, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 经过合金化的钢；它是合金化的产出，不是动作。

entries.definition: Alloying with very small amounts of an element, enough to change grain size but not composition class.
entries.definitionCN: 只加入极少量元素的合金化，足以改变晶粒尺寸却不改变材料类别。

entries.definition: Adding trace elements to a semiconductor to change its conductivity; the idea is similar but the field is not metallurgy.
entries.definitionCN: 向半导体加入微量元素以改变导电性；思路相似，但领域不是冶金。

entries.definition: Mixing materials without melting them together; alloying requires a melt so that the elements dissolve.
entries.definitionCN: 不把材料熔在一起地混合；合金化要求熔体，以便元素相互溶解。

entries.definition: A pre-made rich alloy added to a melt to introduce an element easily; it is a tool of alloying, not the process.
entries.definitionCN: 预先配好的高含量合金，加入熔体以便容易地引入某种元素；它是合金化的工具，而不是过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the binding root, the real sequence in a plant, and the real trade-off words.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：「绑」的词根、工厂里的真实顺序，以及真实的权衡词。

normal.en: The root is 'bind': alloying ties an extra element into the metal so that it cannot be separated by simple melting.
normal.cn: 词根是「绑」：合金化把额外元素绑进金属里，使其无法靠简单熔炼分开。

normal.en: The plant order is melt, alloy, cast: the addition happens in the ladle, just before the metal leaves it.
normal.cn: 工厂顺序是熔、合金化、浇铸：加入发生在钢包里，就在金属离开它之前。

normal.en: The typical gains and losses are a pair: more strength for less ductility, more corrosion resistance for less conductivity.
normal.cn: 典型的得失成对出现：强度换来延性损失，耐蚀换来导电下降。

normal.en: The family is regular: alloy for the material, alloyed for the result, alloying for the act, alloying element for the ingredient.
normal.cn: 同族形式很规整：合金指材料，已合金化的状态指结果，合金化指动作，加入的元素指成分。

normal.en: Chromium, nickel and molybdenum are the usual named additions in stainless and high-strength steels.
normal.cn: 铬、镍与钼是不锈钢与高强钢中最常被点名的添加元素。

abstract.en: Picture a single foreign atom sitting in a neat lattice, pushing its neighbours slightly out of line.
abstract.cn: 想象一个外来原子坐在整齐的晶格里，把邻近原子稍稍挤歪。

abstract.en: Picture a recipe where every ingredient you add takes away something else, so no dish is free.
abstract.cn: 想象一份配方，每加一味料就要拿走另一样东西，因此没有一道菜是白得的。

abstract.en: Picture two traditions melting into a third style that neither could have produced alone.
abstract.cn: 想象两种传统熔成第三种风格，而这种风格任何一方单独都做不出来。

examples.en: Alloying with a little chromium turns ordinary steel into stainless steel.
examples.cn: 加入少量铬的合金化，把普通钢变成不锈钢。

examples.en: The alloying step is recorded for every heat.
examples.cn: 每一炉都记录了合金化这一步。

examples.en: Microalloying saves cost by using grams rather than kilos of the added element.
examples.cn: 微合金化用克而不是公斤的加入量，从而节省成本。

dict_mnemonic.text: alloy（合金）+ ing（过程）＝ 合金化；记「炉前加料、成分改写、性能改变」。

root: alloy 来自拉丁 alligare「绑到……上」（ad- + ligare「绑」），经古法语进入英语；加 -ing 构成动名词，指有意向金属熔体加入元素的工序。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one addition: the process, one heat's operation, the added element's role, the mechanism inside, the recipe, the property changed, the plant practice, and a metaphor of merging.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着一次「加入」展开：工艺本身、某一炉的操作、加入元素的作用、内部机理、配比设计、性能变化、工厂实践，以及融合的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small bright lump is pushed into a churning melt, and the charge record is rewritten.
core.cn: 核心意象：一小块银亮金属被压进翻涌的熔体，炉料记录随之改写。

branches.en: THE OPERATION: the deliberate act of adding elements, named as a process.
branches.cn: 操作层：有意加入元素的行为，作为过程被命名。

branches.en: THE HEAT AND THE PLANT: one charge's timing, and the place in the works where the addition is made.
branches.cn: 炉次与工厂：某一炉的时机，以及工厂中进行加入的位置。

branches.en: THE INGREDIENT AND THE RECIPE: what is added, and how much of it is chosen.
branches.cn: 成分与配方：加入什么，以及加入多少。

branches.en: THE MECHANISM: the foreign atom enters the lattice or forms particles, and blocks deformation.
branches.cn: 机理层：外来原子进入晶格或形成颗粒，从而阻碍变形。

branches.en: THE RESULT AND THE METAPHOR: a measured property changes, and different traditions merge into one style.
branches.cn: 结果与比喻：可测量的性能发生变化，不同传统融合成一种风格。

intro.en: Alloying is a verb plus the ordinary -ing noun ending; its technical vocabulary is built by adding prefixes such as micro- and de-.
intro.cn: alloying 是动词加普通的 -ing 名词词尾；它的技术词汇靠 micro-、de- 这类前缀继续扩展。

latinIntro.en: The root is Latin alligare, from ligare 'to bind'; the same root reached English through ally, so the two words are relatives in origin but not in meaning.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是拉丁 alligare，出自 ligare「绑」；同一词根经 ally 进入英语，因此两词在来源上是亲属，在意义上不是。
