senses.title: The process
senses.titleCN: 熔炼：高温还原提取金属
senses.definition: heating ore with a reducing agent until the metal separates from the waste rock
senses.definitionCN: 把矿石与还原剂加热，直到金属与废石分离
senses.example: Smelting turns crushed ore into a metal that can be cast and worked.
senses.exampleCN: 熔炼把碎矿石变成可以铸造和加工的金属。
senses.why: Ore is a compound, not a metal; heat alone melts it, but a reducing agent must also strip the oxygen away, which is why smelting is chemistry as much as melting.
senses.whyCN: 矿石是化合物而不是金属：单靠热只能熔化它，还必须用还原剂把氧夺走，因此熔炼既是熔化，也是化学。

senses.title: One furnace charge
senses.titleCN: 一炉作业：某一次熔炼
senses.definition: a single run of a furnace with one charge of ore and fuel
senses.definitionCN: 一座炉子装入一炉矿石与燃料后的一次运行
senses.example: The first smelting of the day produced a full crucible.
senses.exampleCN: 当天第一炉熔炼出了一整坩埚金属。
senses.why: A countable use appears when the process is tied to one charge, because each run has its own ore mix, its own heat and its own yield.
senses.whyCN: 当过程与某一炉料绑定时，就会出现可数用法，因为每一次运行都有自己的矿石配比、温度与产出。

senses.title: A step in the chain
senses.titleCN: 工序链中的一环：焙烧、熔炼、精炼
senses.definition: the central step between preparing the ore and refining the metal
senses.definitionCN: 在准备矿石与精炼金属之间的核心一步
senses.example: Roasting removes sulphur before smelting begins.
senses.exampleCN: 焙烧在熔炼开始之前把硫去掉。
senses.why: Smelting is bracketed by other operations: ore must be dressed and roasted first, and the raw metal must be refined afterwards.
senses.whyCN: 熔炼被其他操作夹在中间：矿石先要选矿与焙烧，所得的粗金属之后还要精炼。

senses.title: The works
senses.titleCN: 冶炼厂与熔炼炉：进行熔炼的场所
senses.definition: the plant or furnace where smelting is carried on
senses.definitionCN: 进行熔炼的工厂或炉子
senses.example: The smelting on the coast closed when the ore ran out.
senses.exampleCN: 矿源枯竭后，海边的冶炼厂关闭了。
senses.why: The activity's name transfers to the place built for it, because a works exists only for the furnace it houses.
senses.whyCN: 活动的名称转移到为它建造的场所，因为一座厂存在的理由就是它所容纳的炉子。

senses.title: The earliest furnaces
senses.titleCN: 历史与考古：早期炼铜与炼铁
senses.definition: the early history of the process, studied from furnaces, slag and crucibles
senses.definitionCN: 该过程的早期历史，依据炉址、炉渣与坩埚研究
senses.example: Early copper smelting used charcoal and simple clay furnaces.
senses.exampleCN: 早期炼铜使用木炭与简易陶炉。
senses.why: The first smelting was a narrow technical achievement, because reaching the needed temperature and controlling the air supply had to be solved before metal could flow.
senses.whyCN: 最早的熔炼是一项狭窄的技术成就：必须先解决达到所需温度与控制进风的问题，金属才可能流出。

senses.title: Heat, fuel and emissions
senses.titleCN: 能源与排放：熔炼的能耗与环境代价
senses.definition: the fuel demand and atmospheric emissions that come with industrial smelting
senses.definitionCN: 工业熔炼带来的燃料需求与大气排放
senses.example: Smelting accounts for a large share of the plant's sulphur emissions.
senses.exampleCN: 熔炼占该厂硫排放的很大一部分。
senses.why: Sulphide ores release sulphur dioxide when heated, so a process that extracts metal also produces a gas that must be captured or cleaned.
senses.whyCN: 硫化物矿石受热会释放二氧化硫，因此提取金属的过程同时也产生必须收集或净化的气体。

senses.title: Melting scrap again
senses.titleCN: 再生熔炼：以废金属为原料
senses.definition: smelting applied to scrap and used metal rather than to fresh ore
senses.definitionCN: 以废料与旧金属而非新矿石为原料的熔炼
senses.example: Secondary smelting recovers lead from old batteries.
senses.exampleCN: 再生熔炼从旧电池中回收铅。
senses.why: Once metal exists, it can be melted again without chemical reduction, so a second branch of the industry feeds on objects instead of on rock.
senses.whyCN: 金属一旦存在，就能不经化学还原再次熔化，因此这一行业的第二支以器物而不是以岩石为食。

senses.title: A metaphor of fusion
senses.titleCN: 比喻：像高温熔化一样整合
senses.definition: a figurative process of melting separate things into one mass
senses.definitionCN: 比喻义：把分开的东西熔成一体的过程
senses.example: The smelting of many dialects produced one broadcast voice.
senses.exampleCN: 多种方言的「熔炼」产生了一种广播腔。
senses.why: Heat that destroys the shape of separate solids and merges them into one liquid is a natural image for any process that fuses different things.
senses.whyCN: 把分开的固体毁去形状、合成一体液体的热，是任何融合不同事物的过程都自然会借用的意象。

intro.en: Smelting is a Germanic word that entered English from the Low Countries in the sixteenth century, in the vocabulary of metalworkers rather than of scholars.
intro.cn: smelting 是一个日耳曼语词，十六世纪从低地国家进入英语，属于金属工匠的词汇，而不是学者的词汇。

items.en: Middle Dutch smelten and Middle Low German smelten meant to melt or fuse. The word reached English in the sixteenth century, when Low Country furnace practice was influential.
items.cn: 中古荷兰语 smelten 与中古低地德语 smelten 意为熔化、熔合。这个词在十六世纪进入英语，当时低地国家的炉冶实践很有影响。

items.en: The verb is reconstructed as a Germanic causative form related to melt, with cognates in German schmelzen and Swedish smälta. The reconstruction explains the family, not its first origin.
items.cn: 这个动词被重构为与 melt 相关的日耳曼语使役形式，同族有德语 schmelzen 与瑞典语 smälta。重构解释的是族内关系，而不是最初的来源。

items.en: Smelting and melting are close relatives: one is the general act of becoming liquid, the other the industrial act of melting ore to win metal.
items.cn: smelting 与 melting 是近亲：一个是变成液体的一般动作，另一个是熔化矿石以取得金属的工业动作。

items.en: The technical sense is fixed by the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, when smelting named the furnace stage that turns ore into crude metal, distinct from refining it afterwards.
items.cn: 技术义在十八与十九世纪固定下来，smelting 指把矿石变成粗金属的炉内阶段，与之后的精炼相区别。

items.en: Modern usage adds flash smelting, secondary smelting and smelting emissions, marking changes in furnace technology, in feedstock and in environmental accounting.
items.cn: 现代用法增加了闪速熔炼、再生熔炼与熔炼排放，标记出炉子技术、原料来源与环境核算的变化。

items.en: Dating and reconstruction: the earliest English citation is not fixed precisely, and the deeper Indo-European ancestry of the Germanic verb is reconstructed rather than recorded.
items.cn: 年代与重构：最早的英语书证没有被精确确定，这个日耳曼动词更早的印欧来源属于重构，而非有记录的形式。

note.en: Group one separates the word from melting and from the unrelated fish; group two separates it from the other stages around it.
note.cn: 第一组把这个词与「熔化」以及无关的鱼名分开；第二组把它与前后相邻的工序分开。

entries.definition: Turning a solid into a liquid by heat alone; smelting adds reduction, so the metal is chemically freed from its ore.
entries.definitionCN: 仅靠加热把固体变成液体；熔炼还加入还原，使金属在化学上从矿石中释放出来。

entries.definition: The base verb 'to smelt ore', and separately a small silvery fish; the fish is a different word of the same shape.
entries.definitionCN: 原形动词「熔炼矿石」，另指一种银色小鱼；鱼是同形的另一个词。

entries.definition: A plant where ore is smelted, or a worker who does it; the -er ending marks the doer or the site.
entries.definitionCN: 熔炼矿石的工厂，或做这项工作的工人；-er 词尾标记施事或场所。

entries.definition: Having been through the furnace; it describes the metal, not the process.
entries.definitionCN: 已经过炉子的；它描述金属，而不是过程。

entries.definition: Purifying crude metal after smelting; the furnace gives an impure metal, refining makes it usable.
entries.definitionCN: 熔炼之后提纯粗金属；炉子给出不纯的金属，精炼才使它可用。

entries.definition: Heating ore in air to remove sulphur and water before smelting; it prepares the charge.
entries.definitionCN: 在空气中加热矿石以除去硫与水，为熔炼准备炉料。

entries.definition: Pouring the smelted metal into a mould; smelting produces the metal, casting gives it a shape.
entries.definitionCN: 把熔炼所得金属浇入铸型；熔炼产出金属，铸造给它形状。

entries.definition: Crushing and concentrating ore before the furnace; it raises the metal content that smelting will handle.
entries.definitionCN: 入炉前把矿石破碎并富集；它提高熔炼要处理的金属含量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Low Country origin, the furnace sequence, and the real emissions vocabulary.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：低地国家的来源、炉内顺序，以及真实的排放词汇。

normal.en: Smelting is melting plus chemistry: heat liquefies the ore, a reducing agent takes the oxygen away.
normal.cn: 熔炼是熔化加化学：热把矿石液化，还原剂把氧夺走。

normal.en: The order around it is dress, roast, smelt, refine, cast.
normal.cn: 围绕它的顺序是：选矿、焙烧、熔炼、精炼、铸造。

normal.en: The plant words are real: smelter for the works, smelting furnace for the equipment, smelting works for the site.
normal.cn: 场所词都是真的：熔炼厂指厂，熔炼炉指设备，熔炼场指场地。

normal.en: Secondary smelting is the scrap route; primary smelting starts from ore.
normal.cn: 再生熔炼走废料路线；原生熔炼从矿石开始。

normal.en: Sulphide ore and sulphur dioxide belong together, which is why emissions are part of the word's modern company.
normal.cn: 硫化物矿石与二氧化硫总是相伴，因此排放成了这个词在现代的常见搭配。

abstract.en: Picture rock losing its identity in heat and coming out as a liquid that can be poured.
abstract.cn: 想象岩石在高温中失去身份，出来时成了可以倾倒的液体。

abstract.en: Picture a furnace as a locked room where stone is forced to give up the metal it was hiding.
abstract.cn: 想象炉子是一间上锁的屋子，石头在里面被迫交出它藏着的金属。

abstract.en: Picture slag floating on metal like the discarded part of a sentence.
abstract.cn: 想象炉渣浮在金属上，像一句话里被丢弃的那部分。

examples.en: Smelting releases sulphur dioxide unless the gas is captured.
examples.cn: 若不收集气体，熔炼会释放二氧化硫。

examples.en: The valley's first smelting furnaces were built of clay and stone.
examples.cn: 这个山谷最早的熔炼炉用黏土与石头砌成。

examples.en: Secondary smelting supplies a growing share of the lead market.
examples.cn: 再生熔炼供应了铅市场中越来越大的一份。

dict_mnemonic.text: smelt（熔炼）+ ing（过程）＝ 熔炼；记「矿石入炉、还原夺氧、金属流出」。

root: 来自中古荷兰语与中古低地德语 smelten「熔化、熔合」，与 melt 同族，可重构为原始日耳曼语使役形式；更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the furnace: the process, one charge, its place in the chain, the plant, its early history, its emissions, the scrap route, and a metaphor of fusion.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着炉子走：过程本身、一炉作业、在工序链中的位置、厂与炉、早期历史、排放、废料路线，以及融合的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: ore and coke alternate in a furnace, and dark red metal runs out into a mould.
core.cn: 核心意象：矿石与焦炭在炉中层层相叠，暗红金属液流进模子。

branches.en: THE CHEMISTRY: heat plus a reducing agent frees the metal from its compound.
branches.cn: 化学层：热与还原剂把金属从其化合物中释放出来。

branches.en: THE HEAT AND THE CHAIN: one furnace charge, and the step between roasting and refining.
branches.cn: 炉次与链条：一炉炉料，以及焙烧与精炼之间的那一步。

branches.en: THE PLACE: a works exists because a furnace is inside it.
branches.cn: 场所层：一座厂因为里面有一座炉子而存在。

branches.en: THE EARLIEST AND THE LATEST FEED: first clay furnaces with charcoal, and today's scrap-fed plants.
branches.cn: 最早与最新的原料：最早的木炭陶炉，以及今天以废料为食的工厂。

branches.en: THE COST AND THE IMAGE: sulphur emissions as the price, and fusion as the metaphor.
branches.cn: 代价与意象：硫排放作为代价，融合作为比喻。

intro.en: Smelt is a Germanic verb with the ordinary English endings -ed, -er and -ing, and it compounds with furnace, works and secondary.
intro.cn: smelt 是日耳曼语动词，接普通的 -ed、-er、-ing 词尾，并能与 furnace、works、secondary 构成复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin had no cognate of smelt; it expressed the same idea with excoquere 'to boil out' and fundere 'to pour', which are different families and are not the source of the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语没有与 smelt 同源的形式；它用 excoquere「煮出」与 fundere「倾倒」表达同一意思，那是别的词族，也不是这个英语词的来源。

items.structure: smelt (base verb, Middle Dutch/Low German origin)
items.meaning: to melt ore in order to win metal
items.example: They smelt the ore in a small furnace.
items.exampleCN: 他们用小炉子熔炼这种矿石。

items.meaning: having been through the furnace
items.example: The smelted metal is poured into bars.
items.exampleCN: 熔炼好的金属被浇成条锭。

items.meaning: a plant or a worker
items.example: The smelter runs three furnaces.
items.exampleCN: 这家冶炼厂开三座炉子。

items.meaning: the process or one run of it
items.example: Smelting is the hottest stage in the works.
items.exampleCN: 熔炼是厂里温度最高的一步。

items.meaning: the equipment in which ore is smelted
items.example: The smelting furnace was relined last year.
items.exampleCN: 熔炼炉去年换了内衬。

items.meaning: the site where smelting is done
items.example: The smelting works sits beside the river.
items.exampleCN: 冶炼厂坐落在河边。

items.meaning: smelting fine concentrate in a suspended blast
items.meaningCN: 让细精矿在悬浮气流中瞬间反应
items.example: Flash smelting treats the concentrate in seconds.
items.exampleCN: 闪速熔炼在数秒内处理精矿。

items.meaning: smelting scrap instead of ore
items.meaningCN: 以废料而非矿石为原料的熔炼
items.example: Secondary smelting avoids mining new ore.
items.exampleCN: 再生熔炼无需开采新矿石。

definition_zh: 锻造：把金属加热后锤打成形；也指铁匠铺、锻炉，以及缔造、伪造、稳步推进等引申义
definition_en: to shape metal by heating and hammering, and the workshop or hearth where this is done, with extensions of creating, counterfeiting and advancing
core_image: 铁块在炉火中烧到橙黄，被钳出放在砧上，第一锤落下时火星四散
scene: 铁块在炉火里烧到橙黄，钳出放在砧上，第一锤落下时火星四散。The smith can forge a blade from a single bar in one afternoon.
sceneCN: 这里指锻造这一动作（第 1 个义项：加热后锤打金属成形）；句意为铁匠能在一个下午里，用一根铁条锻出一把刀。

pos.zh: 锻造；锤打成形（金属）
铁匠铺；锻工车间
锻炉；炉膛本身
缔造；建立（关系、联盟）
伪造（签名、文件、货币）
稳步推进；奋力前进

derivatives.zh: forge + -ing（动名词）→ 锻造；锻件，语义偏移为「一次成形作业或其产物」
forge + -ed（分词形容词）→ 锻造的；伪造的，语义偏移为「经锤打成形或经假冒制成」
forge + -er（施事）→ 伪造者；锻工，语义偏移为「做假的人」
forge + -ery（行为或产物）→ 伪造；伪作，语义偏移为「假冒的文件或物件」
forge + -able（可……的）→ 可锻造的，语义偏移为「在高温下能锤打成形的」

senses.title: To hammer hot metal
senses.titleCN: 锻造：加热后锤打成形
senses.definition: to heat metal and shape it by hammering, pressing or stamping
senses.definitionCN: 把金属加热后靠锤打、压制或冲压成形
senses.example: The smith can forge a blade from a single bar in one afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 铁匠能在一个下午里，用一根铁条锻出一把刀。
senses.why: Hot metal flows under a hammer instead of cracking, so the craft is defined by the combination of heat and impact rather than by cutting material away.
senses.whyCN: 热金属在锤下流动而不开裂，因此这门手艺的决定性特征是热与冲击的结合，而不是把材料切掉。

senses.title: The smithy
senses.titleCN: 铁匠铺：进行锻造的作坊
senses.definition: a workshop where a smith heats and hammers metal
senses.definitionCN: 铁匠在其中加热并锤打金属的作坊
senses.example: The forge at the end of the lane is still working.
senses.exampleCN: 巷子尽头的铁匠铺还在营业。
senses.why: The place is named by its central activity, because a smithy exists around its hearth, anvil and tools.
senses.whyCN: 场所按核心活动命名，因为铁匠铺正是围绕它的火塘、铁砧与工具存在的。

senses.title: The hearth itself
senses.titleCN: 锻炉：烧金属的火塘
senses.definition: the hearth or fire where metal is brought to working heat
senses.definitionCN: 把金属加热到可加工温度的火塘或炉子
senses.example: He kept the forge bright while the iron soaked up heat.
senses.exampleCN: 铁块吸热时，他把锻炉烧得很旺。
senses.why: The same noun narrows from the whole shop to the one fire inside it, since the fire is what makes the shop possible.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词从整间作坊缩小到里面的一堆火，因为正是这堆火让作坊得以存在。

senses.title: The large works
senses.titleCN: 锻造厂：大型锻压车间
senses.definition: an industrial plant where heavy parts are forged with presses or power hammers
senses.definitionCN: 用压力机或动力锤锻造重型部件的工厂
senses.example: The forge supplies shafts for the turbine maker.
senses.exampleCN: 这家锻造厂为涡轮制造商供应轴。
senses.why: When the craft moves from a hand hammer to a press, the old word moves with it, naming a plant instead of a room.
senses.whyCN: 当手艺从手锤转到压力机，旧词也跟着走，命名的是工厂而不是一间屋子。

senses.title: To bring into being
senses.titleCN: 缔造：建立关系、联盟或事业
senses.definition: to create or establish something lasting, such as a link, an alliance or a career
senses.definitionCN: 创造或建立某种持久之物，如联系、联盟或事业
senses.example: The two towns forged a trade agreement in the spring.
senses.exampleCN: 两座镇子在春天缔结了一项贸易协议。
senses.why: Shaping metal into a durable object supplies an image for making anything that is meant to hold: a bond, a pact, a path.
senses.whyCN: 把金属锻成耐久器物，为任何意在「牢固」的创造提供了意象：纽带、契约、道路。

senses.title: To counterfeit
senses.titleCN: 伪造：假冒签名、文件或货币
senses.definition: to make a false copy of a signature, document or valuable object in order to deceive
senses.definitionCN: 为欺骗而假冒签名、文件或有价物的副本
senses.example: Someone forged the letter and dated it a year early.
senses.exampleCN: 有人伪造了这封信，还把日期提前了一年。
senses.why: The sense grows out of 'fabricate': making a thing that pretends to be what it is not, with the same skill but a dishonest aim.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项从「制作」生长出来：做出一件冒充它物的东西，用的还是同样的手艺，目标却是不诚实的。

senses.title: To push forward
senses.titleCN: 稳步推进：顶着阻力向前
senses.definition: to move forward steadily despite difficulty, especially in the phrase forge ahead
senses.definitionCN: 在困难中稳步向前，常用于「顶着阻力推进」这一说法
senses.example: The team forged ahead despite the loss of its captain.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管队长缺阵，球队仍稳步向前。
senses.why: A smith's work advances one blow at a time against resistant metal, which gives the phrase its sense of steady effort rather than speed.
senses.whyCN: 铁匠的工作是一锤一锤对着顽固的金属推进，这使该短语带有稳定用力而非追求速度的意味。

senses.title: The craft itself
senses.titleCN: 锻造这门手艺与行业
senses.definition: the craft of forging taken as a trade or an industrial process
senses.definitionCN: 作为行当或工业过程来看的锻造手艺
senses.example: Forge work and casting compete for the same aerospace orders.
senses.exampleCN: 锻造与铸造争夺同一批航空订单。
senses.why: A noun that names a place and a process can also name the trade that fills both, especially when it is counted as an industry.
senses.whyCN: 一个同时命名场所与过程的名词，也能命名填满两者的行当，尤其在它被当作产业来计算时。

intro.en: Forge comes from Latin through French: a word for a workshop became a word for the craft done in it, and then for several kinds of making.
intro.cn: forge 经法语来自拉丁语：一个指作坊的词，变成了指作坊里所做手艺的词，随后又指好几种「制作」。

items.en: Faber meant a craftsman, especially one who works hard materials, and is the person-noun behind fabrica. The family is old and its deeper connections are reconstructed.
items.cn: faber 指工匠，尤指加工硬材料的匠人，是 fabrica 背后的人名词。这个词族很古老，更深的联系属于重构。

items.en: Fabrica meant a workshop or a craft, and fabricare meant to make or build. English takes both strands through French, one as forge, the other as fabricate.
items.cn: fabrica 指作坊或手艺，fabricare 指制作或建造。英语经法语吸收两条线索：一条成为 forge，另一条成为 fabricate。

items.en: Old French forge named the smithy and forgier the act of hammering; the verb also came to mean to make or invent something, including something false.
items.cn: 古法语 forge 指铁匠铺，forgier 指锤打的动作；这个动词也逐渐表示制作或编造某物，包括编造假的东西。

items.en: Middle English borrowed both noun and verb. The smithy sense is the oldest, and the senses of creating and counterfeiting follow from the idea of making.
items.cn: 中古英语同时借入名词与动词。铁匠铺义最早，缔造与伪造两义都从「制作」这一想法延伸而来。

items.en: The phrase forge ahead develops from the image of steady blows; forging becomes an industrial term; forged acquires the sense of both hammered and faked.
items.cn: 「顶着阻力推进」这一短语从稳定落锤的意象发展而来；动名词形式成为工业术语；过去分词同时获得「锻打过」与「假冒」两种含义。

items.en: Dating and reconstruction: the exact dates of each sense are approximate, and the deeper pre-Latin origin of faber is reconstructed rather than recorded.
items.cn: 年代与重构：各义项的精确年代只是大致，faber 在拉丁语之前更早的来源属于重构，而非有记录的形式。

note.en: Group one separates the members of the forge family; group two separates the craft from its neighbouring metal trades.
note.cn: 第一组把 forge 词族的各个成员分开；第二组把这门手艺与相邻的金属行当分开。

entries.definition: The act or process of hammering metal, and its products; the base word forge names the place or the single act.
entries.definitionCN: 锤打金属的行为或过程及其产物；原形 forge 指场所或单次动作。

entries.definition: Shaped by hammering, or made false; it describes the object, not the workshop.
entries.definitionCN: 经锤打成形的，或假冒的；它描述物件，而不是作坊。

entries.definition: A person who counterfeits documents; the -er ending marks the doer, and in ordinary use it usually means the dishonest one.
entries.definitionCN: 伪造文件的人；-er 词尾标记施事，在日常用法中通常指不诚实的那一类。

entries.definition: The crime of counterfeiting, or the false object itself; it is a noun of result, not of the workshop.
entries.definitionCN: 伪造的罪行，或伪造出的物件本身；它是结果名词，不是作坊名词。

entries.definition: A blacksmith's workshop; it names the place, while forge can name the place, the fire or the act.
entries.definitionCN: 铁匠的作坊；它命名地点，而 forge 可以指地点、炉火或动作。

entries.definition: A works where metal is melted and poured into moulds; forging shapes solid metal instead.
entries.definitionCN: 熔化金属并浇入铸型的工厂；锻造则加工固态金属。

entries.definition: To make or assemble, and also to invent a false story; it comes from the same Latin verb as forge.
entries.definitionCN: 制作或装配，也指编造假话；它与 forge 来自同一个拉丁动词。

entries.definition: The tool used in forging, and the act of striking; it names the instrument, not the whole craft.
entries.definitionCN: 锻造所用的工具，以及敲击的动作；它命名工具，而不是整门手艺。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin workshop word, the heat-and-hammer image, and the real sense branches.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁语的作坊词、热与锤的意象，以及真实的义项分支。

normal.en: The root is a workshop: fabrica gave both forge and fabricate, one for metal and one for making in general.
normal.cn: 词根是一间作坊：fabrica 同时给出 forge 与 fabricate，一个指金属，一个指一般的制作。

normal.en: The physical image is heat plus impact: without heat the metal cracks, without impact it does not change shape.
normal.cn: 物理意象是热加冲击：没有热金属会裂，没有冲击它不会改变形状。

normal.en: The 'create' sense is the same verb used for alliances and careers, not a separate word.
normal.cn: 「缔造」义只是同一个动词被用在联盟与事业上，并不是另一个词。

normal.en: The 'counterfeit' sense comes from making a false thing, which is why forger and forgery are its everyday companions.
normal.cn: 「伪造」义来自制作假东西，因此 forger 与 forgery 是它的日常伙伴。

normal.en: The phrase forge ahead keeps the smith's rhythm: one steady blow after another.
normal.cn: 「顶着阻力推进」这一短语保留了铁匠的节奏：一锤接一锤地稳定落下。

abstract.en: Picture a single bar changing shape without losing any material: forging moves metal rather than removing it.
abstract.cn: 想象一根铁条改变形状却不失去材料：锻造是移动金属，而不是削掉金属。

abstract.en: Picture a signature being drawn with the same skill that shapes a blade, only aimed at deceit.
abstract.cn: 想象一只签名用与锻刀相同的手艺写下，只是目标变成了欺骗。

abstract.en: Picture a workshop, a fire and a verb all sharing one word because they cannot exist apart.
abstract.cn: 想象作坊、炉火与动作共用一个词，因为它们无法彼此分离。

examples.en: The gate hinges were forged by hand a century ago.
examples.cn: 这道门的铰链是一百年前手工锻打的。

examples.en: They forged a partnership that outlasted the original contract.
examples.cn: 他们缔结了一段比原合同更持久的合作关系。

examples.en: He forged the cheque and was caught within a week.
examples.cn: 他伪造了那张支票，一周之内就被抓了。

dict_mnemonic.text: forge＝锻造；记「炉火烧热、砧上落锤、火星四散」，并记「缔结」与「伪造」两义。

root: 拉丁 fabrica「作坊、手艺」与 fabricare「制作」，经古法语 forge／forgier 进入英语；更早的 faber「工匠」来源属于重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one shop: hammering hot metal, the smithy, the hearth, the large works, the making of lasting things, counterfeiting, steady advance, and the trade itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一间作坊展开：锤打热金属、铁匠铺、炉火、大型锻造厂、缔造持久之物、伪造、稳步推进，以及这门行当本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: orange-hot iron on an anvil, struck once, throwing sparks.
core.cn: 核心意象：砧上一块橙热的铁，被敲一锤，火星四散。

branches.en: THE ACT: heat makes the metal flow, and the hammer fixes its new shape.
branches.cn: 动作层：热让金属流动，锤子把新的形状固定下来。

branches.en: THE PLACE AT THREE SCALES: a smithy, the hearth inside it, and the industrial works it grows into.
branches.cn: 场所的三个尺度：铁匠铺、里面的炉火，以及它长成的工业厂区。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR OF MAKING: shaping metal becomes building a bond or a career.
branches.cn: 制作的比喻：把金属成形变成建立纽带或事业。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR OF FAKING: the same skill of making turned to a false object.
branches.cn: 造假的比喻：同样的制作手艺转向虚假的物件。

branches.en: THE RHYTHM AND THE TRADE: steady blows become steady progress, and the craft becomes an industry.
branches.cn: 节奏与行当：稳定的落锤变成稳定的推进，手艺变成产业。

intro.en: Forge is a borrowed noun and verb; its endings are ordinary English, and its compounds name tools, methods and workplaces.
intro.cn: forge 是借来的名词兼动词；它接普通英语词尾，复合词则命名工具、方法与场所。

latinIntro.en: Latin fabrica 'workshop' and fabricare 'to make' are behind the word; fabricate is the learned cousin that kept the Latin shape, while forge took the French one.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fabrica「作坊」与 fabricare「制作」在这个词背后；fabricate 是保留拉丁形态的学术亲属，forge 则走了法语形态。

items.structure: forge (n., v.; from Old French, from Latin fabrica)
items.meaning: to hammer hot metal; the shop or hearth
items.meaningCN: 锤打热金属；作坊或炉火
items.example: They forge the brackets in the old shop.
items.exampleCN: 他们在老作坊里锻打托架。

items.meaning: the process, or a forged part
items.example: Forging is cheaper than machining for this shape.
items.exampleCN: 对这种形状来说，锻造比机加工便宜。

items.meaning: hammered into shape; also faked
items.meaningCN: 锤打成形的；也指假冒的
items.example: The forged ring needs no welds.
items.exampleCN: 这个锻制圆环不需要焊缝。

items.meaning: one who counterfeits
items.example: The forger copied the seal exactly.
items.exampleCN: 伪造者把印章复制得一模一样。

items.meaning: the crime or the false object
items.example: The painting was exposed as a forgery.
items.exampleCN: 这幅画被揭穿是伪作。

items.meaning: able to be shaped by hammering
items.example: The alloy is forgeable at moderate heat.
items.exampleCN: 这种合金在中温下可锻造。

items.meaning: joining metal by hammering it while hot
items.meaningCN: 在热态下靠锤打把金属接合
items.example: Forge welding needs a clean, hot surface.
items.exampleCN: 锻焊需要干净而炽热的表面。

items.meaning: to keep advancing steadily
items.example: They forged ahead with the plan.
items.exampleCN: 他们按计划稳步推进。

items.meaning: a machine that shapes hot metal under pressure
items.meaningCN: 在压力下使热金属成形的机器
items.example: The forging press closed with a heavy blow.
items.exampleCN: 锻造压力机重重合上。

definition_zh: 锻造：把金属加热后用锤击或压制使其成形；也指锻件、锻造行业，以及伪造、缔造等动名词用法
definition_en: the shaping of metal by hammering or pressing it while hot, together with forged parts, the trade, and the gerund uses of counterfeiting and building
core_image: 锻锤落下，烧红的钢坯被压扁拉长，表面的氧化皮像碎屑一样脱落
scene: 锻锤一下下落下，烧红的钢坯被压扁拉长，表面的氧化皮碎屑四处飞溅。Forging aligns the grains of the steel and makes the shaft much stronger.
sceneCN: 这里指锻造工艺本身（第 1 个义项：加热后靠锤打或压制使金属成形）；句意为锻造使钢的晶粒排列一致，让这根轴强得多。

pos.zh: 锻造；锻造工艺（不可数）
一次锻打作业；一个火次（可数）
锻件（可数，复数形式指成批锻件）
锻造；伪造；缔造（原动词的现在分词与动名词）

derivatives.zh: forge（铁匠铺；锻造）+ -ing → 锻造活动的基础词，指整间作坊或单次动作
forge + -ed（分词形容词）→ 锻造的；伪造的，语义偏移为「经锤打成形或假冒制成」
forge + -er（施事）→ 伪造者；锻工，语义偏移为「做假文件的人」
forge + -ery（行为或产物）→ 伪造；伪作，语义偏移为「假冒的文件或艺术品」
die（模具）+ forging → 模锻，语义偏移为「金属在闭合模腔中成形」
forging + press（压机）→ 锻造压力机，语义偏移为「以巨大压力使热坯成形」

senses.title: The process
senses.titleCN: 锻造工艺：加热后锤打或压制成形
senses.definition: the process of shaping metal by hammering, pressing or stamping it while hot
senses.definitionCN: 在热态下靠锤击、压制或冲压使金属成形的过程
senses.example: Forging aligns the grains of the steel and makes the shaft much stronger.
senses.exampleCN: 锻造使钢的晶粒排列一致，让这根轴强得多。
senses.why: Hot metal deforms instead of cracking, and the deformation lines up the grain structure; that is why forging is valued for strength rather than only for shape.
senses.whyCN: 热金属变形而不开裂，变形又使晶粒结构排列一致；因此锻造的价值在强度，而不只在形状。

senses.title: One heat, one operation
senses.titleCN: 一个火次：一次锻打作业
senses.definition: a single heating of a workpiece and the hammering that follows before it cools
senses.definitionCN: 对工件的一次加热，以及随后在其冷却前完成的锤打
senses.example: The first forging brought the bar down to a square section.
senses.exampleCN: 第一个火次把铁条锻成了方截面。
senses.why: Metal can only be worked while it is above a certain temperature, so the craft is counted in heats rather than in hours.
senses.whyCN: 金属只有在高于某温度时才能加工，因此这门手艺按火次计数，而不是按小时计数。

senses.title: The forged part
senses.titleCN: 锻件：锻造出来的零件
senses.definition: a part that has been produced by forging, especially in the plural forgings
senses.definitionCN: 靠锻造制成的零件，复数形式尤指成批的锻件
senses.example: The order covers castings and forgings for the same engine.
senses.exampleCN: 这批订单包括同一台发动机的铸件与锻件。
senses.why: A count noun appears when the output is handled as stock: foundries ship castings, forges ship forgings.
senses.whyCN: 当产出被当作库存来处理时，就会出现可数名词：铸造厂发铸件，锻造厂发锻件。

senses.title: The shop and the trade
senses.titleCN: 锻造车间与锻造行业
senses.definition: the workshop where forging is done, and the trade that carries it on
senses.definitionCN: 进行锻造的车间，以及从事这项工作的行当
senses.example: Forging moved to a new bay with two presses.
senses.exampleCN: 锻造搬进了一个有两台压机的新车间。
senses.why: The activity's name transfers to the place and to the occupation, because both are defined by the operation.
senses.whyCN: 活动的名称转移到场所与职业，因为两者都由这项操作来定义。

senses.title: Ways of forging
senses.titleCN: 锻造方法：自由锻、模锻与锻焊
senses.definition: the recognised methods of forging, such as open-die, closed-die and forge welding
senses.definitionCN: 被公认的锻造方法，如自由锻、闭式模锻与锻焊
senses.example: Die forging gives a near-final shape with little waste.
senses.exampleCN: 模锻能得到接近最终的形状，废料很少。
senses.why: Once forging becomes an industry, its variants need names: an open die lets the metal spread, a closed die forces it into a cavity.
senses.whyCN: 锻造一旦成为产业，各种变体就需要名称：自由锻让金属自由展宽，闭式模锻则把金属逼进模腔。

senses.title: Counterfeiting
senses.titleCN: 伪造：由锻造动词引申的动名词用法
senses.definition: the act of making a false copy of a document, signature or valuable
senses.definitionCN: 假冒文件、签名或有价物的行为
senses.example: The forging of the will was proved by the ink.
senses.exampleCN: 遗嘱是伪造的，这一点由墨迹得到证明。
senses.why: The gerund inherits the 'make a false thing' sense of the verb, so it names the act rather than the person or the object.
senses.whyCN: 动名词继承动词「制作假东西」的义项，因此它命名行为，而不是人或物件。

senses.title: Building something lasting
senses.titleCN: 缔造：建立关系或事业
senses.definition: the act of creating or establishing a lasting link, alliance or career
senses.definitionCN: 创造或建立持久联系、联盟或事业的行为
senses.example: The forging of ties between the two ports took a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 两座港口之间联系的建立用了十年。
senses.why: Shaping metal into a durable object supplies the image for making anything meant to hold, so the gerund can name the building of bonds.
senses.whyCN: 把金属锻成耐久器物，为任何意在牢固的创造提供意象，因此动名词可以命名纽带的建立。

senses.title: A stage in production
senses.titleCN: 生产链中的一环：锻造、机加工、热处理
senses.definition: the forging stage considered as one link in a manufacturing sequence
senses.definitionCN: 作为制造序列中一环来看的锻造阶段
senses.example: The part goes from forging straight to heat treatment.
senses.exampleCN: 这个零件从锻造直接进入热处理。
senses.why: In a factory a craft becomes a step with an input and an output, so forging is scheduled between the billet and the finished part.
senses.whyCN: 在工厂里，手艺变成有输入与输出的一个步骤，因此锻造被排在钢坯与成品之间。

intro.en: Forging is the verbal noun of forge, a word that came from a Latin workshop term through French; its form is ordinary English, but it carries several centuries of sense development.
intro.cn: forging 是 forge 的动名词；forge 这个词语经法语来自拉丁语的作坊词。它的形态是普通英语，却承载了几个世纪的语义发展。

items.en: Fabrica meant a workshop or craft, and fabricare meant to make or build; the pair stands behind both forge and fabricate, which entered English by different routes.
items.cn: fabrica 指作坊或手艺，fabricare 指制作或建造；这一对词是 forge 与 fabricate 的共同背景，而两者经不同路线进入英语。

items.en: Old French forgier meant to hammer metal and also to make or invent; the second sense is the seed of both the 'create' and the 'counterfeit' meanings.
items.cn: 古法语 forgier 指锤打金属，也指制作或编造；第二个义项正是「缔造」与「伪造」两义的种子。

items.en: Middle English took forge as noun and verb. The smithy sense is earliest, and the -ing form appears as the ordinary verbal noun of the verb.
items.cn: 中古英语把 forge 既作名词也作动词。铁匠铺义最早，而带动名词词尾的形式作为该动词的常规动名词出现。

items.en: From 'make' come the senses of establishing an alliance and of making a false document; from 'hammer' comes the industrial sense of a shaping stage.
items.cn: 从「制作」生出缔结联盟与制作假文件两义；从「锤打」生出作为成形阶段的工业义。

items.en: Nineteenth- and twentieth-century industry fixed the countable forgings for finished parts and the method names die forging, open-die forging and forge welding.
items.cn: 十九与二十世纪的工业固定了可数用法（成品锻件），以及模锻、自由锻、锻焊等方法名。

items.en: Dating and reconstruction: the dates of each sense are approximate, and the pre-Latin origin of faber is reconstructed rather than recorded.
items.cn: 年代与重构：各义项的年代只是大致，faber 在拉丁语之前的来源属于重构，而非有记录的形式。

note.en: Group one separates the forms of the forge family; group two separates forging from the competing shaping processes.
note.cn: 第一组把 forge 词族的各种形式分开；第二组把锻造与竞争性的成形工艺分开。

entries.definition: The workshop, the hearth or the single act; forging names the activity or its output, not the place.
entries.definitionCN: 作坊、炉火或单次动作；forging 命名活动或产出，而不是场所。

entries.definition: Hammered into shape, or faked; it describes the object that resulted.
entries.definitionCN: 锤打成形的，或假冒的；它描述所得的物件。

entries.definition: The false document or artwork itself, or the crime of making it; forging is the act, forgery is the thing.
entries.definitionCN: 假冒的文件或艺术品本身，或制作它的罪行；forging 是行为，forgery 是物件。

entries.definition: The press that delivers the blows; it is equipment, not the process.
entries.definitionCN: 施加压力的机器；它是设备，而不是过程。

entries.definition: Shaping metal by pouring it molten into a mould; forging works on solid metal and therefore gives different grain flow.
entries.definitionCN: 把熔融金属浇入铸型来成形；锻造加工固态金属，因此晶粒流向不同。

entries.definition: Pressing sheet metal into a shape with a die; it is a cold-forming cousin of forging, used on thin stock.
entries.definitionCN: 用模具把薄板压成形状；它是锻造的冷成形亲属，用于薄料。

entries.definition: Cutting metal to size with powered tools; forging moves material into shape instead of removing it.
entries.definitionCN: 用动力工具把金属切到尺寸；锻造是把材料移到所需形状，而不是去掉材料。

entries.definition: Hammering metal by hand at an anvil; forging also covers press work on an industrial scale.
entries.definitionCN: 在铁砧上手工锤打金属；forging 还涵盖工业规模的压制成形。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin workshop pair, the countable output, and the real method names.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁语的作坊词对、可数的产出，以及真实的方法名。

normal.en: forge + -ing: the process and its product, the same ending that turns casting into castings and smelting into a trade.
normal.cn: forge + -ing：过程与产物共用这一词尾，正如 casting 变 castings、smelting 变行业名。

normal.en: The countable output is forgings, just as the countable output of a foundry is castings.
normal.cn: 可数产出是 forgings，正如铸造厂的可数产出是 castings。

normal.en: The method names are real: open-die, closed-die, and forge welding.
normal.cn: 方法名都是真的：自由锻、闭式模锻、锻焊。

normal.en: The three figurative senses are all still alive: forging a link, forging a document, forging ahead.
normal.cn: 三个引申义至今都活着：建立联系、伪造文件、稳步推进。

normal.en: The strength comes from grain flow: hammering bends the grain lines to follow the shape instead of cutting them.
normal.cn: 强度来自晶粒流向：锤打让晶粒线顺着形状弯，而不是把它们切断。

abstract.en: Picture a bar being squeezed rather than carved, so nothing is lost and the grain is rearranged.
abstract.cn: 想象一根铁条被挤压而不是被雕刻，因此没有材料损失，晶粒则被重新排列。

abstract.en: Picture a document and a blade made by the same motion of the hand, one honest and one not.
abstract.cn: 想象一份文件与一把刀由同一手势做出，一个诚实，一个不诚实。

abstract.en: Picture a factory schedule where a craft becomes a slot between billet and finished part.
abstract.cn: 想象一张工厂排程，其中一门手艺变成钢坯与成品之间的一个格子。

examples.en: Forging produces a stronger shaft than cutting it from a solid block.
examples.cn: 锻造做出的轴，比从整块材料上切出来的更强。

examples.en: The plant orders forgings from three different suppliers.
examples.cn: 这家工厂从三家不同供应商订购锻件。

examples.en: The forging of the certificate was detected by the serial number.
examples.cn: 证书的伪造被序列号识破。

dict_mnemonic.text: forge（锻造）+ ing（过程/产物）＝ 锻造、锻件；记「热坯受压、晶粒顺形、废料极少」。

root: forge 来自拉丁 fabrica「作坊」与 fabricare「制作」，经古法语 forge／forgier 进入英语；加 -ing 构成动名词，指锻造工艺及其产物。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the hammer: the process, one heat, the forged part, the shop and trade, the method names, counterfeiting, building a bond, and a stage in production.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着锤子走：工艺本身、一个火次、锻件、车间与行业、方法名、伪造、建立纽带，以及生产链中的一个阶段。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a power hammer falls, the hot billet flattens and lengthens, and scale flies off the surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：锻锤落下，热坯被压扁拉长，氧化皮从表面飞散。

branches.en: THE PROCESS: deformation under heat lines up the grain and raises strength.
branches.cn: 工艺本身：热态变形使晶粒排列一致，从而提高强度。

branches.en: THE UNIT AND THE SLOT: one heat counted as a working unit, and the stage scheduled in a factory.
branches.cn: 火次与工序格：一个火次作为作业单位，以及工厂排程中的一个阶段。

branches.en: THE OUTPUT AND THE PLACE: countable forgings shipped as stock, and the bay or trade that makes them.
branches.cn: 产出与场所：作为库存发运的可数锻件，以及制造它们的车间或行当。

branches.en: THE METHODS: open dies, closed dies and forge welding split the craft into named routes.
branches.cn: 方法层：自由锻、闭式模锻与锻焊把手艺分成有名目的路线。

branches.en: THE TWO GERUNDS: making a false document, and making a bond that is meant to last.
branches.cn: 两个动名词：制作假文件，以及建立意在持久的纽带。

intro.en: Forging is forge plus the ordinary -ing noun ending; the technical vocabulary adds method and equipment words rather than prefixes.
intro.cn: forging 是 forge 加普通的 -ing 名词词尾；技术词汇靠方法与设备词扩展，而不是靠前缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin fabrica and fabricare stand behind the base word, and faber 'craftsman' behind them; the verbal noun itself is purely English in formation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fabrica 与 fabricare 是基础词的来源，更早还有 faber「工匠」；动名词本身在构词上完全是英语的。

items.structure: forge (n., v.; from Old French, from Latin fabrica)
items.meaning: to hammer hot metal; the shop
items.example: They forge the ring in one heat.
items.exampleCN: 他们一个火次就把圆环锻好。

items.meaning: the process, or its countable product
items.example: The forgings are stacked by size.
items.exampleCN: 锻件按尺寸堆放。

items.meaning: shaped by hammering; also faked
items.meaningCN: 锤打成形的；也指假冒的
items.example: A forged shaft resists fatigue better.
items.exampleCN: 锻制的轴更耐疲劳。

items.meaning: one who fakes documents
items.example: The forger used an old typewriter.
items.exampleCN: 伪造者用了一台旧打字机。

items.meaning: the false object or the crime
items.example: The forgery passed as an original for years.
items.exampleCN: 这件伪作多年被当作原作。

items.meaning: forging inside a shaped die
items.example: Die forging holds tight tolerances.
items.exampleCN: 模锻能保持很紧的公差。

items.meaning: forging between flat or simple dies
items.meaningCN: 在平砧或简单砧面之间锻造
items.example: Open-die forging shapes the ingot first.
items.exampleCN: 自由锻先把钢锭锻出粗形。

items.meaning: the machine that delivers the pressure
items.example: The forging press is rated in tonnes.
items.exampleCN: 这台锻造压力机以吨位标定。

items.meaning: joining by hammering hot metal together
items.example: Forge welding leaves no filler metal.
items.exampleCN: 锻焊不留填充金属。
